text:
I have been using laptops for the past 30 years, and haven’t bought a new one since 2013. It was a special treat getting this new FusionTech G3. I’m not a crazy gamer, but I do play games. I was attracted to this computer because I wanted performance, and I know gamers expect high performance!
PROS:
-FAST FAST FAST. It is by far the fastest computer I’ve ever owned. I often blamed my speed on my Internet connection -- but am now discovering that my computer itself was at least 75% of the problem.
-The graphics card is amazing! My 10yr old nephew tried out Minecraft, Java Edition on my laptop. He gave it a 98/100. The Frames Per Second rate started around 90+. He gave it the TNT test (a fast animation to stress out the frame rate) and the frame rate dropped 30 then immediately recovered to the high level.
-The keyboard glows blue. Not only is it super cool, it’s easy to see in low light.
-Compared to other laptops I’ve had, this one is MUCH cooler (ie you can actually put it on your lap without burning your legs!). Yay for thermal cooling!
-Great battery life. So far, I have had zero issues with battery life. According to the battery icon, a full battery should last about 5 hours - which I fully believe.
-The power cord has a blue light where it plugs into the computer so you KNOW it’s charging!
CONS:
-It’s heavier than any laptop I’ve had - I assume because of the robustness of the machine.
-The power supply is HUGE - Again, I have to assume because of the robustness of the computer, but it seems unnecessarily large.
-For me personally, the keyboard is different than I’m used to. It has a numeric keypad on the right end of the keyboard -- so the QWERTY keys are not as central as I’m used to. There are raised bits on the F&J so you can find home base, and on the center of the number pad, which is good. I think this will just take some getting used to the change.

Overall, I’m elated by this laptop. After having it for about 3 weeks, I have no regrets thus far.

text:
Compared to my 5 year old PC that I was using for gaming, this is a really solid computer. As you can see from the photo, the power adapter is huge and pretty cumbersome to haul around. I like the design and the weight is about the same as other laptops.
The keys have a nice blue backlight which I like quite a bit as I often am in dim or no light. You can also adjust the brightness of the screen itself depending on room lighting conditions, preference or battery life.

I made sure the battery was fully charged and embarked on several hours of gaming, music editing programs and plain old internet surfing. I got about 3 1/2 hours of continuous use before needing to plug in to a power source.
I did have the laptop sitting on a laptop mat which has a built in fan that will kick on when higher heat levels are detected, however the internal fan system does the trick and my external fan never had the need to kick on.

Pretty standard with newer Microsoft components, Cortana is the embedded virtual assistant. You can enable voice commands in the settings or access her through the desktop. I found the voice settings to be useful so you don't have to disengage in game play or anything else to access her.

The memory is decent, but not great. I have an external drive which I use for storage and so this isn't a huge influence to my opinion. title_x: A powerful brick -  basically, a small desktop with limited upgradability and poor battery life
text: I got this laptop, 13500-7722BLK-PUS, from Costco. I use it exclusively to run Zwift and Rouvy, which both are sofware for indoor cycling. I am not a gamer, but these applications fall under the "game" categories. What can I say? This laptop is a brick, large and amazingly heavy for today's standards. This is because its processor and graphics card generate massive amount of heat and require substantial cooling. It also burns a lot of power, so its power supply is another brick which weighs more than many modern laptops and is the biggest I have seen in many years, perhaps even ever! The battery life is miserable, it really depends on what one does, but you will be lucky to get more than 3 hours (no wonder, with such energy hungry components!). Carrying it along with power supply would be a significant chore, due to size and weight. Its performance is on par with a decent desktop (albeit RTX 2060 desktop version would be about 30% faster than this laptop version), and it runs Zwift at highest resolution setting quite nicely. Unlike desktops, it is not really upgradable - you cannot increase RAM beyond 16 GB, no room for extra SDD, etc. Keyboard is not super comfortable. I suppose, its best use is when you intend to use it as a desktop replacement, i.e., have limited space for it and do not intend to run it on the battery much, or at all, but I would still use an external keyboard and mouse. On a positive side, a good selection of ports and a reasonably large (although, at 1080p, not stellar by today's standards) screen. A true gamer would use a desktop which enables one to get significantly higher computing power for the same money. A road warrior would not want such a brick. I got it because it was on sale at Costco and was cheaper than a desktop with similar specs - and the fact that it takes less room is beneficial for what I use it for. Zwift runs very well on it, although many people would say it is an overkill to use such laptop for it. I am still fighting some problems with Rouvy which I did not have on my desktop, not sure what causes them - drivers, hardware, or what.

title_x: Runs warm/hot when pushed hard, keyboard backlight is blue only, otherwise awesome!
text:
So coming from console gaming, PC gaming is actually a new experience for me. After a few hiccups I managed to get the Witcher 3, Wild Hunt installed, updated and running with a game pad. I have already played this game on the Nintendo Switch, so I was excited to see what a more robust processor and graphics hardware could do with it.

Well, the graphics are WAY, WAY better than the Switch. I did experience a little hitching in the video very rarely, but I also haven't taken the time to optimize the settings for the hardware (I need to learn how first). Suffice it to say, this game is simply beautiful on this computer. The scenery is gorgeous and it draws you in, in ways that less detailed graphics cannot.

Compared to my aging desktop PC, this machine has probably already saved me a couple of hours over the last week in load times alone. I am an amateur photographer and use Affinity Photo software to process my pictures. This computer opens it within a few seconds, where my older computer used to take at least half a minute. Aside from gaming, photo and video processing are likely to be the most resource-heavy uses I would undertake with this machine, so it's probably going to handle those easily, at least with current generation software.

Waking from sleep mode is lightning fast as well, likely due to the solid state drive. Everything just seems to run smoother.

Like other reviewers, I was a bit surprised at the sheer size of the power supply. It is a monster. Battery life is not great compared to my work laptop, but I imagine most users will have this connected to wall power while gaming anyway. As a substitute for a general purpose computer for typical web browsing and household use, it might be a bit over powered, but it certainly will run common applications fast. These powerful components do tax the battery though, so unless you actually need the power for gaming and other resource hungry apps, you might consider a machine with longer battery life and milder specs.

Things I was a little let down by...

It gets hot and the cooling system runs a little noisy when pushed hard running games. There is enough heat coming out of the vents to make nearby USB and power cables more soft and pliable. I would make sure this has good ventilation all around. I have a separate monitor I like to use, but closing the screen might make cooling more difficult, so keep that in mind.

Also I was surprised to discover it was not a touch screen. There is no fingerprint scanner, and the keyboard backlight is only blue, not RGB. I confirmed this will FusionTech tech support. They were very helpful and patient, and as with most outsourced tech support, you will have a better experience chatting with them online than talking on the phone. I was really looking forward to the RGB backlight but alas, it wasn't part of this model.

Also, like other reviewers, I noticed the lack of a DVD drive. I ordered one to use installing the game discs.

On to other things, there are 3 total USB ports, one of which is a USB 3.0 and very fast for data transfer. I transferred many, many GB of music to the drive from a big thumb drive and it transferred in less than 20 minutes. The same music files took almost 4 hours to download over my fiber internet connection from Google play.

If you want to use an external monitor, it has an HDMI port for the purpose. I believe it also supports audio over the HDMI protocol so you should be able to game on a flat screen TV just by plugging it in.

There is a 1/8" jack for external speakers or headphones. The on board speakers sounded good listening to several different songs, but are a little underpowered for gaming in a loud family room with dogs barking, kids playing, other entertainment devices going, etc. If this sounds like your house, you will want to connect external speakers.

Styling is nice. The anti-skid feet on the bottom are huge, and it isn't likely to slip on your desk or table if you are a keyboard and mouse gamer. Not sure how you would use a touch pad in that scenario but if you are going to buy a mouse, might as well spend the same money and get a cool looking wireless game pad instead. But again, coming from consoles that's going to be my preference anyway.

So, while it's not a blazing fast, bleeding edge, state of the art gaming machine with all the bells and whistles, it definitely outperforms my Switch by a large margin, and runs other software effortlessly that my older PC often struggles with.

If you are used to using laptop computers costing 1/4 of this one from big retail marts, you will be VERY impressed with its performance. So is it a good value? Given the cost of a current "flagship" cell phone from any of the major brands, I think this is a very reasonable price for a laptop with these specs and capability. It actually costs quite a bit less in today's dollars than a more "cutting edge" laptop I purchased many years ago that would be woefully inadequate to run Windows 10 today. So yes, I think its a good value for the price.

title_x: Maybe the most frustrating PC I have ever had.
text: This computer is great for the most part. That said, I have had several issues since purchasing it. When I first received the computer, I had issues with it not wanting to run certain games that I had on Steam. Several games would not start. Instead, I received a popup regarding missing .dll files. I didn't blame this on the computer though. About three months after purchasing this computer, it overheated and fried the hard drive out of NOWHERE. The computer was asleep and closed. The following morning, I went to use it and it was hot to the touch. I opened the computer and shut it down (from the login screen). I let the computer cool off for a while. When I came back to it and turned it on, the computer sent me to a startup error screen. I sent the computer to FusionTech for warranty repairs, and it came back better than ever. Or so I thought. One day, I went to play a game and was notified that my drivers were pretty old. This confused me, so I went to open the GeForce Experience application. Huh. My computer does not detect that I have a GeForce GTX graphics card. I still have this issue today - whenever it occurs, I just have to restart my PC. It's annoying, but I figured it probably wasn't my computer. A few months later, I went to my mother's house. We decided to watch a movie, but she did not have a smart TV. When we plugged the HDMI cable into my computer, nothing happened. I thought it was the cable, but we plugged the same cable into another laptop and everything worked perfectly. I am now having issues with my USB ports. All three USB ports will provide power to a device, but that is it. This becomes an issue when you need to use an external mouse. No matter what I do, I cannot get any external mice to work. I use this computer for school and gaming. While I can do all of my school work with a trackpad, gaming is another story. This computer seriously runs great, but there have been so many hardware issues that I felt like I needed to write this review. Perhaps I just got a dud? Who knows? I do have Avast Premium antivirus, and I use a VPN every time I connect to the internet. I am kind of a computer nerd, and I care a lot about my computer's security, so I am not like your grandmother who clicks on everything she sees. That said, I don't believe my issues are caused by malware.

title_x: A solid laptop with some minor drawbacks.
text:
It's taken me a week or so to fully digest the functionality and pros/cons of this laptop. Overall, if you read the product description (and know anything about electronics) it's pretty straight forward what you're getting. That being said, I feel it's important to outline a few cool features as well as drawbacks you may overlook.

Initial Impression: Materially, this is a really solid piece of equipment. Though somewhat heavier than I expected, this is typical with a gaming laptop. The power adapter is massive however, and unnecessarily so. I don't know if this has anything to do with requiring more energy for intense gaming, but it's literally a quarter the size of the laptop itself. The keys are backlit (which can be turned on and off with the press of a button), and there are ports for virtually everything you could imagine. The screen itself is somewhat of a matte texture which is something I'm not used to, but after a few hours of use I appreciated how it prevents glare. As with most laptops, the brightness is adjustable on the keyboard - something to take into consideration when trying to preserve battery life. That being said, startup was a nightmare... but this was due largely in part to my internet being down - an essential requirement to get up and running. I'm very much a "plug and play" kind of guy, so you can imagine my frustration when the computer repeatedly froze on a black screen until I was able to get online to download essential updates and software components (all of which should be pre-installed for a device this new). Trying to add a secondary user was equally frustrating as it also needed to re-download many of the same components as my setup, once again freezing repeatedly. Once past all the initial turmoil, everything was a breeze.

Extended use: After a full charge, the battery lasted roughly 2.5-3 hours while I browsed the internet and worked on documents. With streaming and game play, the battery life is surprisingly close to the same (roughly 2 hours depending how much multi-tasking you're doing). The dual fan system is incredibly quiet and kept the laptop from heating more than say your average smartphone after prolonged use.

Cortana is your virtual assistant (similar to Siri). While she is accessible from your desktop, you can also enable "Hey Cortana" in the settings which will allow her to respond to voice commands.

Link your phone using the edge app. This allows you to sync browsing history, favorites, and alternate seamlessly between devices (simply by logging into your Microsoft account). It is worth noting the functionality for Apple products is more limited than Android (which allows you to see/sync SMS, MMS, pictures, and video). I have an iPhone, so I cannot personally attest to whether or not the additional Android features actually work, but the information showed up while setting up my device.

Game Shift, a function controlled by a button on your keyboard, is said to increase the fan speed to cool the processor, and prioritizes game data over annoying popups or background apps (and updates). Basically, it is supposed to optimize the resources needed during gaming (processor, video card, memory, etc). I attempted to test this function with several games and did not notice a difference or receive the on-screen prompt that it was working. Perhaps I need to update a driver for this? It wouldn't surprise me given the number of essentials I had to install during setup. That being said, the gaming I did was pretty seamless and ran without issues.

It's worth mentioning there is no CD/DVD drive. I completely overlooked this prior to ordering, and the vast majority of my software is on discs. This is easily resolvable with an external drive which costs virtually nothing nowadays.

The webcam has an indicator light next to it to ensure privacy (so you know when it's on). The resolution is average, but consistent with other laptop cams on the market.

Lastly, a few quick notes. As an avid gamer and video editor, I will say one thing I found discouraging is the computer's memory. Though this is something easily resolved with an external drive, all of these "plug in" devices begin to defeat the purpose and simplicity of a laptop. Additionally, the included manual indicates a fingerprint reader on/by the power button... this is NOT a standard feature with all G3 models.

Summary: When utilized for office use (or basic functionality) this laptop is superior in terms of speed and software capabilities. For standard gaming it's average, and for the professional gamer it might be underwhelming in some of the areas outlined above. Still, when put to the test it's a reliable laptop that I'd consider a nice addition to FusionTech's product line.

title_x: A Portable Next-Gen Console of a Laptop
text:
With GPUs being in short supply these days, gaming laptops may be the new way gamers get to enjoy their favorite games. I guess the miners arent using gaming laptops to do their crypto stuff.

My particular model of the Advance m15 r4 came with a Intel Core i7-10870H and a RTX 3070. In Geekbench 5, this laptop scored a 1254 on the single core score and 7026 on the multicore score. The video card scored 132987 on CUDA, 117718 on OpenCL, and 72857 on Vulkan. These are the best video card device scores I have ever seen in any of my devices. I think the CPU scores are a little disappointing though.

This model has 16GB or RAM, which I condsider the sweet spot for Windows 10 for price and performance.
The white body of the laptop is an off-white color. When paired with my Razer Deathaddder white mouse, you can see a difference in the shade of white, but they do look nice together.

The laptop features RGB backlighting under the keys and also around the backside of the laptop. Speaking of the backside, this laptop has a weird shape to it, that only photos can accurately convey. It almost looks like a rounded-rectangle exhaust port on an alien ship. I guess that's what they were going for.

The keyboard is not the new-fangled Cherry mechanical switches. At least, I don't think they are. They sound like membrane keys and have a dull thud when pressed.

The glass trackpad is small, but very nice. The sharp edges of the laptop keyboard deck may bother your wrists after extended playing sessions. I am noticing it just typing this review.

Enabling the performance mode in the Advance Command Center makes the fans sound like a rocket launch.

I am using this laptop in balanced mode, and that was the mode I used for benchmarks as well.

It paired easily with an Xbox controller, that I bought specifically to use with this laptop.

Overall, I am very happy with this laptop and might make the jump to PC gaming instead of getting a new next-gen console.

text:
So, instead of going into benchmarks, recaps of all the ports, and all that other stuff, I'm going to jump right in and talk about real-world use of this thing, because that's what really matters. Most people aren't going to tweak it carefully to get every a few more FPS out of it, and frankly, I'm not a competitive gamer or Twitch streamer or Youtuber. I'm a gamer who likes to actually play games instead of fussing with overclocking and benchmarks.

So how does it do out of the box?

The answer, you'll be happy to know, is very well indeed. Fast. In fact, the screen refresh and speed was TOO high for Fallout 4 and I needed to install a mod (high FPS fix) to make the game playable because without it everything was flying at super speed. Other, more modern games fared better in that regard, and pretty much everything I have thrown at it plays beautifully on high or ultra settings at 1080p with frame rates well above 60 FPS on the 300Hz screen. Rest assured, when it comes to gaming this thing can handle anything you throw at it up to and including games released in 2021. My favorite is an older title-- Skyrim-- but I run with a TON of mods including 4k textures, tons of new actors, and improved lighting and weather effects, and this thing crunches all of that like it's nothing. I've never seen the game looking so amazing, so smooth, or so full. On the other hand, if you want to try something newer like Cyberpunk 2077, you'll be happy to see this uses all the latest tricks. DLSS, Ambient occlusion, ray tracing... The works. You'll cry, it looks so good.

The screen, by the way, is gorgeous. Yes, it's 'only' 1080p resolution, but the 300Hz refresh rate is out of this world and the colors pop. It's beautiful, and it makes me kind of glad this isn't a touch screen model because frankly, it would be a shame to get fingerprints on that screen!

The body is aluminum. It's smooth, sleek, and cool (temperature-wise, but also socially speaking). The LED lights are a nice touch, and they're fully customizable via the My Advance app. The system comes with no bloatware, thank goodness, except for the usual Windows 10 stuff like Skype, Office 365 trial, and some games that are all easily uninstalled.

I have also added extra storage, which was extremely easy. Remove the bottom panel (several screws, including some that are 'capture screws' that you should know Do Not Come Out, but are designed to stay in the housing so you don't lose them) and then slot in your own M.2 in the available slot. There are actually two M.2 slots, but one is a weird small sized one that, from what I've seen, is nearly impossible to find for any decent price at this point in time. Still, I was able to add an additional 500GB to the included 1TB, and that's plenty of space for a gaming laptop.

Let's talk about the keyboard: It's REALLY nice. It has a sort of mechanical feel. The keys have decent travel and give feedback, but they're not too loud. Of course it's backlit (and customizable) and there are no surprises like power buttons where the Delete key should be (you designers know who I'm talking about). All in all, if this wasn't a gaming laptop it would be an incredibly fine laptop for writing and doing office work.

The sound is equally impressive. I couldn't believe the near-surround effect it provides, along with the rich sound, from small laptop speakers. In terms of sound this blows away any laptop I've had, and I've had everything from high-end VAIOs to Microsoft Surface to MacBook Pros. The sound on this beats them as far as I'm concerned. Again, this is clearly made to be a gaming laptop and it shows.

Now, the downside of all this: Heat. Anything you do that taxes the system even a little will kick in the fans on the normal setting. You can make it run in a quiet mode (and then it runs hot) or in a cool mode (and then it runs loud), but the bottom line is that you're rocking a new i7 and a GeForce RTX 3070 in this thing, and those are going to produce some heat. I highly suggest a cooling pad of some sort, even though the fans on the laptop can handle the heat. It's always nice to cut down the risk and extend the life of your laptop by keeping it cool and happy.

And for all that power, it's pretty darn lightweight although you'll find the power brick to be another story. It's a big beast that gives you the wattage required for top-tier gaming, but will definitely take up some space in your laptop bag. I suggest a BIG bag with separate compartments, because you'll want this big brick well away from the screen on your laptop.

So yeah, there are trade-offs, but at the end of the day the point of a gaming laptop is POWER, and this has it to spare. Connect to a nice monitor and sound system and you have a gaming laptop that can rival most gaming desktops. Even without the monitor and external sound, you have a solid gaming system here that will impress you and keep you gaming for a long time to come.

So it's without any hesitation that I give this Advance masterpiece of a laptop five glowing stars. Bravo!

title_x: 300 hz Screen and RTX 3070 Lives up to the hype - CPU runs hot
text:
I went from a very budget friendly gamin pc laptop to this Advance M15 R4. I opted for the 300mhz screen and RTX 3070 GPU that runs on the Intel Core i7-10870H and 16gb RAM, to be clear which one I am reviewing.
Now just because I had a budget laptop previously does not mean I haven't had my share of beefy systems in the past years as I am a veteran gamer. So my reaction comes with experience.

Build Quality
The look, the feel, the presentation and build quality are top notch. The laptop feels solid. Its WAY lighter than my last laptop. Its not Macbook level but for a gaming laptop Im surprised at how sleek and shallow it is. I work as a graphic designer so showing up to a client meeting with a big ole ugly gaming computer was just out of the question for me. If your client isn't a gamer, they wont think anything of your laptop other than that glowing alien head looks cool as heck! The RGB lighting is subtle but looks amazing. Very well designed and it can be fully customized or even turned off if you so desire. The lighting across the keys is not 100% consistent however. Its like they put just enough to light it up but there are some areas that vary in brightness. Its subtle and definitely not a deal breaker. I also notice that when set to white (which is what I like to set it at during the day) is not quite white but a little pink. So I manually added in a bit of blue to it so it looks better.

Its unfortunate other reviews have received damaged goods. But that should be on a seller review not the product review. Please keep that in mind.

Performance
Ill start with the 300hz monitor. All I can say is wow. Nice and bright. Clear enough. Its not 2k/4k but its clean. Not sure you would want a 4k laptop monitor (yet) but maybe in a few years. The refresh rate for gaming is just awesome. Seeing FPS go into the 200s on some games is just butter. Love the screen.

3070 GPU - For me this GPU hit the sweet spot for me. Its not so overpriced as the 3080 or 3090 (or hard to find) so I can keep several hundred dollars off the cost but its not going to be outdated in a year or 2 which I feel like the 3060 is close to that already. For whatever its worth, this GPU handles most AAA games that Ive thrown at it. Everything renders amazingly and smooth as silk. And when I am doing my graphic work, video editing, or even some 3D modeling, it doesn't miss a beat.

AND I can also say the GPU does great in this machine with heat. Very rarely am I pushing it to its max. And even tho the Advance software allows me to overclock the GPU, I have left it in standard mode and its done phenomenal.

Which brings us to the Intel Core i7-10870H CPU. Its a great CPU, multi-thread, latest design, runs great. It can handle the games and even more so, it can handle my motion graphic and 3d modeling work easily. However it runs really HOT in this chassis. So much so that I often max it out at 100C. Good thing I monitor it closely and sometimes just have to take a break after playing a AAA game for a bit. I do notice if I have both the GPU and CPU fans going it does a better job at cooling down, but its unfortunate because then the fan noise gets loud. They are not obnoxious fans by any means, but still, a fan is a fan and it would be nice to not have to worry ALL the time. Im sure this is also a byproduct of how slim the laptop is so, if I had to choose, Ill take the slimmer design any day. Just need to find a good cooling pad that works.

Now for the big bummer...
RAM is fixed and cannot be changed. While I am generally getting 2999mhz out of RMA, as someone who likes to tinker this was a hard one to decide upon. Mostly because it comes back to the gaming laptops that do allow you to tinker are often big and bulky and was not what I wanted for this round. I understand why companies make this choice, doesn't mean I have to like it, but for something that cannot be changed out, at least its high quality and is running at a high rate with no issues. Keep this in mind, as I think this comes down to personal choice. Id rather have high quality components I cant change rather than giving the company an excuse to put crappy unusable components simply because you CAN change them out, which is usually the story with other gaming laptops that do allow you to change out the ram. Just my 2 cents. So if you are deciding to get one of these, be sure to go for 16gb or more. 8gb just isnt going to cut it for very long.

On the upside, it does have 3 bays for SSDs. x2 2280 slots and x1 2242(I believe, which is the shorter version). It comes with the the first 2280 slot occupied but all are NVMe so that is great. I saw some reports online to NOT get the RAID setup as it is wildly under-performing so just go with a straight 1tb and then add the additional space you need. I opted for another 1tb which is working out. If you like to download a LOT of games, then add a 2tb to be safe.

Battery life is non-existent. You may get 2 hrs at the very BEST if you turn everything down, but never more than that. My last laptop was no different. I have not read one review on any powerhouse gaming laptop that has great battery life though, so, if you plan on gaming you need to be plugged in anyway. Not to mention, the GPU wont get the full load it needs on battery. Most laptops are like this as well so to me, not really a point I used to decide upon. They all suck and to run games you still need to be plugged in so if you are looking for a laptop to carry around campus or on the road, you shouldn't even be considering a gaming laptop anyway. :D

Overall I am very happy with the purchase. I think that if you are an older gamer and just want something that is sophisticated looking and performs just like any higher priced system, this is the best choice. If you are a tinkerer, and want what you want, then you may have to look somewhere else. But if you do decide on this laptop and plan to work by day and game by night, then be sure to get yourself a good cooling pad (as probably with any gaming laptop). Hope this helps! Good luck!

title_x: An Overall Excellent Computer With A Few Issues
text:
[[VIDEOID:b5e29231068f7a642779e2bb9bd7162f]] TL;DR - This is a very powerful laptop - if that’s what you’re looking for, it will not disappoint. It games well, looks good and can double as a space heater when under load! I think the price is justified based on what it includes spec-wise and the mostly-premium build quality. But I have a lot more to say, so read on if you’re interested.

Yes, I got this for free through Vine. No, that will not influence my review - if anything it makes me more stringent because I have nothing to lose. I’m a Mac guy and have been since the switch to Intel in 2006. I prefer macOS over Windows any and every day of the week. But, as we all know there’s quite the Apple tax on their hardware. My current Mac is a 2018 Mini that does alright, but lacks the oomph of modern machines in some tasks. While browsing the Vine items one day I saw this laptop and once I realized what it was, I ordered it immediately. I mean, who doesn’t want a free Advance computer!? I was pretty excited to get it. I’m also NOT an avid gamer - Nintendo classics are my jam and it’s rare that I spend much time playing a game start to finish. But I am a hobbyist photographer so I can and do appreciate the value of a powerful computer and am looking forward to using it for editing my photos. So although this m15 will not see as much game time as most will, I still feel pretty confident I can give it a fair review. So here goes…

First off - if you don’t need the powerhouse that is this laptop, DO NOT BUY IT! There are other similarly spec’d machines that are far more practical than this. This is more like a gaming computer first, and a laptop second. It’s big, kinda heavy, runs really hot, burns through the battery quickly (even when not gaming) and overall is just a lot of computer. It can only use the dedicated GPU, not the one integrated into the CPU because of the 300Hz screen, so there are just no power savings to be had. The fans are always on, though the speed varies of course, and using it in your lap gets it hot quick. Using it on a flat surface where all the vents are usable is the best bet. Once you unplug it, the battery drains quickly. I used it for about 2 hours for just web browsing type stuff and I was approaching dead by the time I finished. I played a game (Forza Horizon 4) on battery for 20-ish minutes and I was at 40% battery remaining. So true portability is not what this computer’s about - sure it’s portable in the sense that it can be picked up and brought somewhere, but you’ll never want to be too far from a power source. Another note about the fans - they are loud when gaming. They’re not quite as high-pitched and annoying as your usual laptop fans, but if you want to hear your game you better have headphones or a loud-enough sound system to overpower the fan noise. The internal speakers get plenty loud, but when you’re sitting right in front of the machine it’s tough to not hear the fans. The touchpad is pretty small for 2021, but it’s definitely usable and very responsive. It also stinks that the RAM is soldered and not upgradeable after purchase - this is a trend in the industry, although not a good one in my opinion. I know a touch screen is not necessary for a gaming laptop, but seems like it should be a “throw in” for what this costs. I also wish the card reader was full-size SD instead of micro, but that’s nothing a USB one can’t fix. But the silver lining to all of that - everything you do with this machine is FAST! I didn’t do a deep dive into performance settings, but whatever throttling algorithms are in place do well enough to make the experience a pleasant one - no matter what the task.

How about the things I do love? The overall design is great. It has a premium look and feel to it. There’s a nice combination of plastic and aluminum, the latter of which seems to be coated with something. With the RGB lights off it doesn’t scream “gaming laptop” with the exception of the alien on the back. And speaking of the RGB lights, those are really cool too and the fact you can customize them is great. I wish the screen was 4K, but 1080p is fine for my 37-year-old eyes - everything looks plenty sharp. It seems to be pretty color accurate and the brightness is good too. The keyboard is a little “clicky” for long-winded typing sessions, but it’s very nice to type on aside from that. The speakers are pretty great as far as laptop speakers go, so no real complaints there. It’s also awesome that there is space for THREE SSDs inside. Being out of the gaming scene for a while, I had no idea how large game downloads have gotten - but now I understand why someone might need all three! Regardless, it’s still awesome. I was able to use Lightroom and Photoshop (to edit the photos for this review, nonetheless) with ease. Everything was fluid and responsive. I imagine a machine spec’d like this one would do great with video editing as well.

I don’t have access to any of the usual suspects as far as benchmarking goes, so instead I used the Benchmark Mode of Forza Horizon 4. Using the laptop screen’s resolution of 1920x1080 with the FPS cranked up to 300, it averaged about 134. Since the human eyes can’t really see that many FPS, I turned it back down to a more-reasonable 75 FPS and it had no problem maintaining that. I then connected it to my 4K Samsung TV via HDMI - at the TV’s native resolution of 3840x2160 it breezed through the test again at 60 FPS, which is the highest my TV can support - I think. You can see screenshots of the results attached to my review. Worth noting is that when I had the TV connected and both displays active, I had tons of stuttering and low frame rates even when only showing the game on one of them. I’m not sure if this is the GPU showing its limitations or me not setting something up correctly.

So as nice as this machine is, there are a few things that have left me unimpressed - especially when the cost for this is almost $2,200 at the time of review. The screen has a lot of backlight bleed on dark screens (see photo) - this just should not happen at this price point. And the screen is pretty flexible - not in a good way. You can see it visibly flexing if you only use one hand to open the lid. Not to the point of breakage of course, but I would expect some more rigidity. And mine seems to be permanently bent slightly - there’s an ever-so-small gap on the left side between the screen and the palm rest when the lid is closed. Also, at least on my particular machine, the RGB lights under the keys have a bit of a gremlin. When I have the lights turned off I still see some green flashes under the right-hand area from time to time. And, as shown in my video, it seems to react to taps on the bezel. This does not appear to be an intended feature but rather a malfunction. Luckily it doesn’t affect anything else, but I imagine it will get worse over time. When I took my computer out of the box for the first time, I could see some scuffs near the power port - looks like it was some careless employee in the testing part of assembly. Lastly, and this could just be a Microsoft thing, but it locked up during the initial setup of Windows - I had to shut it down forcefully and reboot.

All that said, this is a great computer. I anticipate using it for many years to come. It’s flaws are negligible in comparison to the whole package. Had I truly spent $2,200 on it it there’s no way I wouldn’t exchange it to get rid of the RGB gremlins and to try for a display with less backlight bleed (it varies from panel to panel). But if you get a perfect one, I truly believe you’ve gotten your money’s worth. Just make sure you put everything through its paces before the end of your return period.

text:
[[VIDEOID:23785d7ed3d89d14d8e3c26fb04f5801]] The Advance M15 R4 measures 10.86” x 14.19” x 0.78” and weighs 5 and a half pounds. The M15 R4 comes with a 15.6” 1080p display with 300 nits of brightness and 100%sRGD color gamut. My device was configured with the Intel Core i7-10870H, an RTX 3070 8GB GDDR6, 16GB of 2933MHz DDR4 RAM, a 1-TB SSD, and Killer Wi-Fi 6 AX1650i 802.11ax 2x2 Wireless LAN + Bluetooth 5.1.

I use this laptop daily for everything from coding and web development to gaming and everything in-between. When companies speak of desktop replacement laptops the Advance M15 R4 is precisely what they mean as you can get all the performance and power of a desktop in the footprint of a laptop.

What I liked most about the Advance M15 R4 was:
- Typing Experience. Other than the screen size, the thing I miss most when transitioning from a desktop to a laptop is keyboard. With a desktop I usually take advantage of a mechanical keyboard. At times, (like now) I switch things up and use a chicklet-style keyboard, but I prefer mechanical keyboards. This Advance computer comes with a mechanical keyboard that splits the difference between a chicklet keyboard and a mechanical one. The Advance’s keyboard gives the satisfying feedback of a mechanical keyboard while minimizing the sound. You don’t get the full travel distance of a standard desktop keyboard but the amount of key travel you get on the Advance is exceptional in relation to most other laptops.

- Display. I work online in IT and am a web development student at night. Color accuracy is very important for me, and I have been quite impressed by the vibrancy of this display. Colors are vivid and the screen is bright. Scrolling to test the webpages I create is a joy because I know that any hiccups, I encounter are most likely a result of bad code instead of a display that cannot keep up with how swiftly I am navigating a page. For gaming, the same holds true. Images are sharp and bright. Combining this display with a 3070 allows for insane framerates on some titles.

- Performance. I own two desktop computers that were both in heavy use before the Advance arrived. One is a FusionTech OptiPlex sleeper system that’s rocking an i-5 2400 and a GTX 1650 Super. The other is an M1 Mac Mini. The OptiPlex is good for most gaming titles I play. The M1 Mac Mini is a beast in its own right, particularly for productivity and creative tasks. Still, neither of those computers offer the versatility and performance of the Advance. While there are Mac OS exclusive titles I use for creating content that keep the M1 Mac Mini in heavy rotation for my workflow, the Advance M15 R4 has made my OptiPlex obsolete. I’ve uploaded images of my current desktop setup which includes the Advance and the M1 Mac Mini with both attached to a 34” 1440p display.

- Aesthetics. I remember falling in love with the Big Bang Theory television show a several years ago and my favorite character, Sheldon Cooper, was often found perched behind an Advance PC. That distinctive glowing head has evolved over time into something that is much more elegant and refined. The Tron lights on the back, UFO aircraft vents on the underbelly and below the display, and the customizable lights all embrace the legacy design language of Advance computers while updating it for modern times. When I meet up with other development students at our favorite Coffeeshop I see several MacBook computers. I’m the only one who has an Advance and while I initially received looks of condescension it didn’t take long for critics to become enamored with the Advance aesthetic. Very often now I hear, “You know, Apple should do a bit more with its logo, don’t you think?”

- Gaming. I saved gaming for last because gaming is last in my life right now if I am being completely honest. Between work, school, and commitments with the girlfriend my gaming time is usually around an hour a month. That said, when I do game, I can run practically anything thanks to Advance opting for the more power-hungry variant of the mobile RTX 3070 than the 30% less powerful version that was once named Max Q. I ran several benchmarks of this computer; however, Amazon only allows for one video upload per review. The video benchmark I uploaded was run on 3DMark as it’s been trusted for years. This system scored over 10000 on the Time Spy benchmark. The CPU temperature maxed at 95 C and while the GPU max temperature rose to 68 C.

A couple of disclaimers on these benchmarks. First, I captured the benchmark on my phone vs OBS or any other screen capture program but there’s still room for performance improvement. If you look in the lower right corner of the video, you’ll notice several notifications are present which indicate running programs. There’s even a Windows update icon showing in the notification center. I intentionally ran this benchmark on an unoptimized system because I think many gamers are like me in that they work, go to school, and/or generally have other things to do rather than optimize their system to get the absolute best performance before each time they game. For those reasons I think it’s possible to improve performance.

What I liked least about the Advance M15 R4 was:
- Warranty Experience. Immediately after I setup my Advance PC I registered it and started receiving notifications about extending the warranty. FusionTech makes this process as close to the 1980’s used car buying experience as possible by not making it possible to purchase an extended warranty online. Instead, you have to talk to some greedy salesperson working in a foreign country who will force you to haggle your way into the best price over a series of calls and supposed ‘meetings with a manager.’ Inevitably, I was told a single year of extended warranty coverage at the base level would cost $349 with the best coverage costing $449 for a single year. A 2-year warranty would cost as much as $899. Needless to say, I declined to pay that price but am stuck having private number calls bombarding my cellphone with requests for me to continue haggling for better pricing. FusionTech should just make the best price available online and let customers sign up that way. The only purpose this call-in requirement has is to force customers to give in and pay more than they should to protect their devices due to high-pressure sales.

- Thermals. One of the compromises to expect with a high-powered laptop that’s stuffed into a small footprint is high thermals. The keyboard warms a bit when this system is cranking out 100+ frames in a competitive game. Consequently, the fans crank up which generates a substantial amount of fan noise. Neither of these issues bother me but I wanted to disclose this for others.

- Battery life. Depending on how much a person taxes this machine its battery can last as long as 4 hours or as short as an hour and a half. Personally, I keep my device plugged in most of the time as I use this Advance M15 R4 as a desktop replacement 95% of the time. However, when I do take it to the coffeeshop to show it off I find battery life is quite poor, particularly in comparison to M1 MacBook Air computers.

Overall, this Advance M15 R4 is the perfect desktop replacement computer. The Advance is an aesthetically pleasing piece of high-performing technology that boasts a bright, color-accurate display, and exceptional performance as both a gaming and development PC. I absolutely loathed every aspect of attempting to extend the warranty and had to mention the impact thermals and battery life have on the user experience. 4.5 out of 5.0

title_x: Portable gaming beast that runs fast and smooth
text:
I've owned lots of low and mid-range setups throughout my PC gaming life. Solid workhorses that would run all games but only at minimal framerates obtained by compromising that "ooh and ahh" factor. I wasn't totally cheaping out on budget rigs but I also wasn't aiming high. These were mediocre computers.

I finally aimed high with this laptop. A mobile RTX 3070 running on high wattage in a low profile chassis with a wonderful CPU. A sleek and solid build with a plethora of ports and dizzying array of customizatio options. The only slight drawback on my model is the soldered 16 GB of RAM, but I'm not a multitasker at all and I don't do high end video and 3D editing. RAM has never been a bottleneck for me.

I purchased this computer exclusively for gaming.

Specifically, I purchased it to hook up to a 34" ultrawide at 144hz to utilize GSync. And it works perfectly.

Games run sinfully smooth. I'm talking Warhammer II, Red Dead Redemption II, Star Wars Battlefront II, Dying Light, Dragon Quest XI, No Man's Sky, you name it.

The thermal profiles in the Advance Command Center also let me run the computer in different modes depending on whether I'm gaming or just watching videos. Cool mode runs low and quiet while Performance mode kicks up the fan level for that added oomph. This unit is also capable of overclocking and undervolting but I haven't used those options yet, as my system is working just fine and at manageable temperatures.

Overall this is a classy and well-engineered piece of technology that says, "I want a top 1% experience." This is a luxury laptop, an investment, impressive from all angles and one that I'm proud to say has finally broken me of my complacency with mediocre setups.

Game on, friends.

title_x: Effective & Affordable Windows 8 Laptop (READ BELOW FOR AN IMPORTANT ANTI-VIRUS TIP)
text:
My company has used FusionTech workstations for as long as I have been employed (which is nearing the 10 year mark), but this was my first venture into the world of FusionTech laptops, so I wasn't sure what to expect from this affordably priced offering. First off, the specs are impressive for such a low-priced laptop. 4 GB's of RAM, 500 GB's of storage, 1.8Ghz processor, and a middle of the line nVidia graphics card is a steal of a deal at the current price Amazon is selling this laptop for. The first thing you'll notice that might make your eyes pop is the shipping weight of 7.8 lbs! Fear not though, I put this laptop on my trusty scale and the results came back as 4.2 lbs (.4 lbs lighter than advertised). I also have a 13.3 Macbook Pro with Retina Display, which weighed in at 3.4 lbs. So if you're looking for a laptop that you'd like to do a lot of traveling with and you can afford paying almost three times as much, you might be better off looking at a Macbook or a Macbook Air. If you can't afford jumping up to the price of an Apple, this laptop will still be very convenient to tote around as it is very slim and sleek.

Setting up this laptop was extremely easy, as I was able to immediately connect it to my home WI-FI system. This was my first experience with Windows 8, and I must admit it was a bit jolting, but I was able to get used to it after a while. The next paragraph I'm about to type is by far the most important and useful one to read, so if you're going to ready any paragraph, please read the one below.

This computer came with a trial-version of McAfee anti-virus software. That means that you get the software for a trial period, but then you have to pay for it in order to keep getting virus definition updates. Let me save you a lot of time and money, DELETE THIS FROM YOUR COMPUTER AS SOON AS YOU SET IT UP. This sounds extremely backwards, but let me explain. Microsoft has been providing free anti-virus software for Windows users for years via download. The software is called Microsoft Security Essentials, and is superior to all third party virus programs in the way that its free and also that it comes straight from Microsoft, who is always the first company to know when an issue has come up because the issue involves their own software. Companies like McAfee and Norton get their information from Microsoft, so there is always a lag. For Windows 7 and prior, you would need to download Microsoft Security Essentials in order to get the anti-virus protection, but with Windows 8, it is already installed via a beefed up version of Windows Defender that includes Microsoft Security Essentials. The trick is, and this is important, you have to remove any third party anti-virus program before being able to turn on Windows Defender. Microsoft had to do this in order to avoid getting sued by the big anti-virus companies, but make no mistake about it, YOU DO NOT NEED TO PAY FOR ANTI-VIRUS PROTECTION EVER AGAIN. Uninstall whatever was installed to begin with, re-start your computer, and turn on Windows Defender and you will be set. Anti-virus rant over!

I've been using this laptop for the past several weeks and could not be happier with it. The screen resolution is impressive, and the built-in webcam works great for Skyping. In the past I have been impressed with FusionTech for the workstations I've used at my company's office, but now I can appreciate them even more for creating a high quality affordable laptop.

Customer service was helpful, and eventually after some monkeying with the boot order and installation of a fresh BIOS, that problem was solved.

With the crashing solved, I turned my focus to the issue of the incredibly poor wifi performance. The computer would simply fail to connect with any sort of reasonable speed if I left the room the router was in. I ran comparative speed tests on the device from another room, about 30 feet away from the router, and while the new FusionTech was getting less that 1Mbps in download speed, my other devices were able to connect at speeds 10 times greater. Customer Service has been somewhat more difficult in this case, first running diagnostics, then troubleshooting my home router, before finally agreeing to replace the wireless card.

Replacing the card didn't work, nor did re-installing the operating system. Now they want to send a new hard drive rather than try replacing the antenna. FusionTech is flailing. There is something deeply wrong with this model, and if you google around you'll see that this model and the ABC 15 both seem to have issues receiving strong wireless signal which appear to be unsolvable. Personally, I'm done dealing with this nonsense, and plan to return this lemon of a computer as soon as possible.

Happily, where FusionTech has failed, Amazon picked up the slack, and has been very accommodating so far.

text:
I'm a very discerning computer user, as I've been a computer professional for decades, and I also do lots of video editing and games. FusionTech has been my go-to windows vendor as I've used multiple generations of Advance and ABC laptop and desktops.

Here are my thoughts after a few weeks with this laptop:

Love:
* Monitor

Like:
* Overall build quality
* Horsepower: graphics card and cpu
* Modern USB-C Ports
* Speakers

Needs Improvement:
* Skimpy RAM
* Very skimpy hard disk space
* Keyboard
* Trackpad

Overall this is a killer rig, although one of the first things I did was upgrade the RAM and disk space. It comes with 2 slots for memory and 2 SSD slots, so you can inexpensively double the RAM and add another 1TB or 2TB internal SSD drive for a couple hundred bucks (which I highly recommend).

I've done some video editing and it handles that well, and while I'm not a FPS gamer, I enjoy simulation games and RPG's which are pretty graphically intensive, and it runs those games very well.

The speakers are fine, they are on the sides of the keyboard, and are good enough watching videos, gaming, and light video editing. For a laptop, it has quite good sound.

My nemesis has become the touchpad, which after a couple weeks of use now frequently mis-interprets right-clicks, causing all sort of wonky things to happen. I now use a mouse exclusively with this laptop.

I'm not thrilled by the keyboard. The keys are pretty flat and don't have much feel. My Advance has a much better keyboard. The overall build quality though is still very good on the xps. The monitor is high quality and everything about the laptop feels solid and sturdy.

I have mixed feelings about the change-over to USB-C ports (this laptop has *no* traditional "usb" ports, ethernet ports or hdmi ports). I've used macs for years, so I've gotten used to dealing with it, but most of my windows peripherals are still "old school usb-a". it really is a hassle to try to attach things like an ethernet cable, an external drive, or a monitor, or even a mouse to this laptop. It definitely means having to buy some new hubs, cables, and maybe even replacing entire peripherals (if you want to fully utilize the power/speed of usb-c). I really wish they at least included an ethernet port and say an hdmi port onto the back, but I'm learning to live with it.

Overall I'm very happy and impressed with this laptop! It's not cheap, but I think it is actually a decent value considering the computing power and build quality of the ABC.

title_x: Well-built 17" Content Creator PC - but pricey
text:
When this laptop popped up, it seemed like a great option to replace/upgrade my wife’s FusionTech Insprion 17” which has been having some issues lately (difficult to diagnose, but mostly internet/network issues).

On paper, it looks like the specs are solid. Core i7-12700H CPU, 16GB RAM, 512GB NVME M.2 SSD, nVidia RTX 3050 Mobile, and a high-resolution 4K touch display.

My wife has been using this ABC 17 for several weeks, and so far her only complaint was that it randomly went into a state where the mouse pointer disappeared and the trackpad wouldn’t bring it back onscreen. A reboot fixed this issue. It has not exhibited any of the issues that she was having previously with her Worktop.

To put it through its paces, I created my own account on the laptop. When I first did this, after the initial setup I ran into another minor glitch where the mouse pointer was visible, but I could click anything (it could be moved around with the trackpad, though). This occurred while it was initially starting up after my first login to that new account on the machine. After about 30-60 seconds, the screen turned white for about 1 second and then came back to the desktop, at which point the trackpad was working normally.

I ran a couple of benchmarks on the machine (from userbenchmark.com). On the first run, which was essentially the factory fresh configuration, it scored:
Gaming - 35%
Desktop - 107%
Workstation - 38%

I noticed that the log of the results stated that the nVidia GPU was skipped, so this was run with the integrated graphics card.

I then ran it again after using the nVidia Control Panel to set the global graphics to use the nVidia card, and got the following results:
Gaming - 66%
Desktop - 107%
Workstation - 71%

The web page report for both of these runs states that Windows throttled the CPU to about 88%, and I changed the settings mentioned there to address this, with no success. Both results were set with the Performance Plan on Max Performance.

This machine isn’t intended as a gaming laptop, so I didn’t do specific game tests, but it should run non-high-end games at decent framerates (something like CS:GO should be fine).

Overall impressions:

Screen: Gorgeous! Very bright and crisp.

Keyboard: Decent - typical FusionTech laptop keyboard feel. Only disappointment is the lack of a numpad. It seems they omitted the numpad in favor of bigger speakers.

Trackpad: Nice - very large, and responsive. Very smooth to the touch - feels like a glass trackpad to me but I am not sure of this.

Build quality: Good - it is substantial and noticeably heavy, but my daily driver for personal use is a 13” Macbook Pro (but I have a company issued FusionTech Sharp 5520 for work - yes, way overdue for a refresh as it is several years old now). So almost anything feels heavy in comparison. I also have a 17” Advance m17 r4, which is downright massive - it is my home office daily driver, and it never leaves my desk due to its bulk and terrible battery life).

Connectivity/Ports: SD card slot, and 4 Thunderbolt 4 Ports (2 on each side). There is no dedicated HDMI or Displayport connector, so you will need a dongle to connect to an external monitor unless it is a USB-C. This ABC did come with a dongle in the box with a USB-A connector and HDMI.
Networking: It has a WiFI 6E card, but I don’t have WiFi 6 networking equipment, but the connection has been stable with my network setup.

Battery life: I didn’t thoroughly test battery life on it, because it spends the majority of its life plugged in. It defaulted to max brightness when I did my testing on it, and I find the dropping brightness down to 60-70% still gives acceptable visibility. At this brightness level it estimates battery duration of around 4 hours from full charge (and with the “Balanced” performance settings). If I find major discrepancies in battery life as it gets more usage on battery, I will update this review accordingly.

As a full package - this is a solid content creation PC with its big beautiful screen and good technical specifications. Average battery life and physical size may limit it to more of a desktop role, though.

The final ding against it is the price - at over $2500 at the time I write this review, and this is the biggest reason for lowering my rating down to 4 stars. I think this machine has a good use case for specific purposes - with content creation and photo editing being a couple of the biggest ones. However I think for the average user, it might be overkill and there may be better options out there for that kind of money. The Mac user in me would be eyeing a 16” Macbook Pro at that kind of price point. If this ABC was about 20% cheaper, it would be a lot more appealing to me (and possibly to the masses).

title_x: Thin and Powerful | Design is Subjective
text:
This is a very powerful computer with mostly top of the line specs. There are certain graphics and performance compromises that were made because of the thermal limitations that are common in all thin computers, but while this makes the computer less suitable as a dedicated gaming laptop; it’s fantastic for productivity.

Processor: This laptop uses the highest end processor that’s being put into laptops right now. There’s both performance and efficiency cores to provide both power and extended battery life both. This is a new type of processor design, and it’s a game changer. It has 6 Performance Cores and 8 Efficiency Cores. Your computer will assign different tasks to these cores depending on processing power needs and your computers power settings.

Graphics: The graphics card in this computer is very capable with the Nvidia RTX 3060. As far as a good analog for what you can expect performance wise, it’s similar to the performance of the GTX 1070 desktop card (there’s a difference in performance between Nvidia mobile and desktop graphics cards of the same name). The RTX 3060 has many architectural improvements that make it better and faster than the GTX 1070 though. It really is a decent card. It can play most modern games, even if you have to lower some graphics settings on some of the more demanding titles. As a thin laptop, it doesn’t have the same thermal capabilities of a laptop that was actually designed as a gaming laptop. This may factor into how it performs in extended gaming sessions. For productivity though, the RTX 3060 is more than capable to blaze through pretty much anything you might throw at it.

Screen: It’s large, and the touchscreen works fantastic. With such a large screen, this isn’t the kind of small thin and light you try to balance on one of your knees. This is definitely meant to be a portable desktop replacement (mobile workstation), and it does this in a svelte package (for a 17” laptop). The 4K resolution is also gorgeous. The colors are vibrant and accurate, and it can get very bright for use in well-lit environments. This screen would be excellent for creative work. That said, the description says antiglare. Maybe they are planning to use a different panel in the future, but the screen in my unit is definitely glossy. It is the Sharp LQ170R1 SHP1517 17.00 inch 16:10, 3840 x 2400 pixel 10-bit glossy panel. It’s a great screen, but it’s not antiglare.

Memory: 32GB of DDR5 is absolutely amazing. It is almost twice the speed of DDR4. With all of that extra speed, you can essentially lower how much memory you need for pure productivity considerations. Where 32GB is awesome though is for major multitaskers. If you keep many programs and browser tabs open all of the time (like me), you can fill an impressive amount of ram. What if you want to do some quick gaming though? With all of this memory, I’ve been able to keep everything open and still game with no issues. Awesome! Also awesome is that the memory is not soldered to the motherboard. It’s removeable, replaceable, and upgradeable.

Hard Drive/NVME SSD: It comes with a Samsung 1TB Gen 4 NVME. It’s is a good amount of storage for most people’s needs. If you need more storage though, more can be added internally via a second slot that is open and available. As another option, a Thunderbolt dock can be used to add more storage via external drives; and it’s also useful for adding ports that are unfortunately missing on this laptop.

Ports: This laptop isn’t flush with ports. What it does have is 4 fully functional Thunderbolt 4 ports. With these, you can connect docks and monitors of plenty to give you all the connectivity you could ever want. I still prefer to have more ports on the laptop itself (specifically USB Type A for my Logitech mouse adapter), but that’s one of the tradeoffs that are standard with thin and light computers. There is a full-sized SD card reader and headphone jack though. There is also an included adapter that provides a couple of extra ports as well (HDMI and USB Type A) which can be plugged into one of the available Thunderbolt 4 ports.

Design: As far as the design, I’m not a huge fan of some of the design choices. It’s sleek, don’t get me wrong, but there are a couple things I don’t like. 1. I don’t like the extremely tight tolerances. Usually this would be a plus, but the screen and body of this laptop close so tightly together that it’s difficult to open the laptop with one hand – there’s no gap to get ahold of. I find lifting the screen with both hands from the front outside corners to work best for me. 2. The tight tolerances also mean that the edges are sharper than I like. I’m fine if edges are mostly a right angle, but I much prefer it if there is a bit of rounding on the sides for hand/arm comfort; and a bevel on the front so there are no sharp angles to cause any discomfort while typing. These design issues are subjective, and are hardly deal breakers. This laptop has a beautiful design, but I’m one of those that care more about function over aesthetics. I do like the matte silver finish (doesn’t show fingerprints), and the carbon fiber keyboard platform. The laptop looks and feels high quality and well made.

Keyboard: It’s only okay. It works fine, but I wish it had more function keys. There is ample space for dedicated media keys or the like, so the fact this space wasn’t utilized better makes the keyboard seem a little basic. Key travel is standard for a laptop. It doesn’t feel like a mechanical keyboard, but it’s a very familiar feel to me as I spend most of my time typing on laptop keyboards. I’ve come to appreciate the shallower key travel, and I personally prefer it.

Trackpad: It’s huge! This is both great, and something you have to be a little more aware of. It can potentially cause a few issues with typing (depending how you type and position your arms), but the size is very nice when actually using it.

Audio: It’s great for a laptop! Laptop audio will never be as good as larger dedicated speakers, but the audio in this laptop isn’t anything to complain about. It’s very useable.

title_x: Not perfect but does the job
text:
This laptop has been my main computer for the past week and I have had an overall positive experience with it however it is far from perfect. Starting on the outside, the laptop is fairly heavy which I would expect from a 17-inch screen and metal casing, when in my backpack it is not a problem but may be a bit more difficult to carry around by hand. You do get ok ports compared to other high-end laptops, 4 USB-c ports two on both sides that you can use for charging or to hook up a monitor, a 3.5 headphone microphone combo aux jack, and a Full-size sd card reader, and a lock slot. In the box, you also get a fairly cheap but compact dongle that you can plug into one of the USB slots that has both an HDMI and USB port so you can hook up a monitor and mouse without having to buy a separate dongle but I would look into getting a nicer dock or dongle that gives you more options. Personally, I have one that gives me two USB ports so I can plug in a keyboard and mouse plus an HDMI port so that I can have a desktop-like setup but with the portability of a laptop by just pulling in one chord. One of my first small gripes is opening the laptop, the screen is heavy and there is no grip on the edge of the laptop to comfortably open it up with just one finger. Most laptops have a little indent to help out but this laptop just has a sharply angled flat surface that requires a bit more effort to open. Other than that the laptop is very well put together, the body is sturdy with no flex at all and is very thin making it a bit easier to store.
After opening up the laptop you are greeted with the trackpad, keyboard, and speakers all of which I am happy with. The keyboard is probably my least favorite out of the three but it doesn't have much to do with the keyboard itself. Instead, the form of the laptop itself puts the keyboard in a bit of an awkward spot, just a bit too far away from the edge for my liking, add on the sharp edges of the laptop and it took some getting used to as my first few days using the laptop were full of typos because each key just felt like it was slightly further away than my muscle memory was used to. I got used to it fairly quickly and have gotten much closer to my normal typing speed and accuracy since. The keys give a nice tactical bump as you would expect from a high-quality membrane keyboard while staying quiet and responsive. The trackpad is plenty big, with a bit of adjustment in the settings mainly turning off mouse acceleration I got the trackpad feeling just how I like it and its smooth surface plus perfect responsiveness makes it a pleasure to use. Finally, the speakers are something pretty prominently advertised on the amazon page and they don't disappoint. Don't expect dedicated speaker levels of volume where you can hear them over a room of people but at its loudest, I can set it down in it my living room and walk into my kitchen next door to grab a snack all while still clearly hearing the music. The speakers are not only loud but also sound great, you are not going to get brain-shaking bass or shrieking treble, but instead, a nice balanced sound that allows for use when listening to music, playing games, or watching movies plus a fairly easy to use software for adjusting the sound. However, one of my biggest problems with this laptop also relating to sound is when I plug in any headphones or even connect Bluetooth headphones the sound becomes unbalanced. On some headphones, any deep voices or bass will be too emphasized creating a sort of slight echo that is offputting as it messes up how well you can make out background noises. On the other hand, some of my headphones make higher pitches unbearable where it feels like I'm about to get a headache and higher pitch voices become harder to understand. I have tried messing with the audio setting but have gotten nowhere when on other devices the same headphones work fine. Over time I have gotten used to the sound quality but often just opt to use the built-in speakers.

Getting into the specs of the computer without looking at the raw performance the laptop is pretty packed with the latest hardware. The 12th gen i7-12700H is just about the top of the laptop processor market currently giving you 14 cores (6 performance and 8 efficiencies) plus 20 threads at lower power usage than a full-on desktop CPU meaning you get top-of-the-line performance while saving on battery life and thermal performance. 16GB of DDR5 RAM uses the full 4800 MT/S that the CPU is capable of plus should be enough for most basic creator and gaming uses and from what I have seen online is not that hard to upgrade yourself. 512GB of SSD I feel is far too little for a $2500 laptop, again from what I have seen online it is not hard to upgrade but for a laptop aimed at creators, it seems like a big weak point. The GTX 3050 is the budget card of the current 3000 series GPU from Nvidia, note that it is the version with 4GB of VRAM not the 6GB version that you will probably see if you search up benchmarks online, it is far from the best GPU out there and if you are specifically looking for great gaming performance then there are plenty of laptops out there at a fraction of the price that will provide better performance. But if you're like me personally who uses this mainly as a school/work laptop and likes the option to game on the side or is a creator who needs dedicated graphics it should be just about enough to handle most any task for the next few years. Wifi 6 will work for most cases, it is not the latest technology since wifi 6e came out which provides much more possible speed and I would have liked to see that included as future-proofing but most home uses probably won't make full use of it anyway unless your willing to fork out a lot for the latest routers. Finally, the screen is amazing, 60hz UHD+ and touchscreen make it great for use in watching movies, playing games, or creating content. The colors look sharp, it gets plenty bright and the touchscreen is very responsive.

Finally getting into the performance of this laptop, if you're using this as a workstation then it is going to blow whatever you need it to do out of the water. I ran a quick benchmark on UserBenchmark.com and while I couldn't figure out how to test the GPU, the CPU, RAM, and SSD all performed great. In my everyday tasks with dozens of tabs and programs opened the computer did not slow down at all, I could switch between tabs and programs and quickly start using each one. I did go through the installed programs and uninstall a lot of the pre-installed programs that came with the laptop which made a significant difference since there was less stuff running in the background. I also tried out a few newer games like Halo Infinite and apex legends, both ran at a smooth 60 fps which means that it can probably handle most last gen and current-gen games at 60fps, if you go on youtube and search up RTX 3050 4GB benchmarks you can find videos that will go through dozens of games to give you a better idea of what the graphics card can handle but don't expect 1 to 1 results. The battery life is disappointing, in settings it tells me around 5 hours when I am going about my normal day, I had an issue at first with the device being plugged in but not actually charging as in it wouldn't change from the current % even if the device was off, changing the charging profile in the myFusionTech app fixed that I suspect that the computer is not very efficient at deciding how much power it needs for a task because the fans tend to be fairly liberal in which scenarios they spin up, luckily they are not that loud but it is annoying when they spin up when you're just watching a video.

Overall the laptop is far from perfect, with poor battery life, annoying sharp edges, weird audio issues, and some older parts with a top-of-the-line price tag. However, as an overall package, I don't think there is any denying that the laptop can perform, it has plenty of power for most uses and works best as a desktop replacement that you can hook up to a USB-c hub at your desk and then take on the go if needed. Despite its problems, I am still happy with the laptop since it has been more than enough for all my home and work use cases.

text:
This is a fast, beautiful laptop. It’s pretty repairable/upgradeable especially by modern standards. It’s big, double the size of many ultra portable laptops. If you need something big and fast – a true desktop replacement - this is one of the best options for you. If you want something small, light, portable – aka most of the reasons people buy a laptop – this might not be for you.

Screen
Wow! What a beautiful display. It’s not OLED, it’s not high refresh rate (not that big of a deal given the GPU honestly), and FusionTech should calibrate it out of the box but those are my only complaints. It’s contrasty, sharp, bright, has good color with lots of different color profiles, and is huge. It’s a very bright screen. There are brighter screens out there and an argument could be made that on a multimedia machine costing three grand FusionTech should use micro LED or some other better screen tech. If you know you need that nice of a display, then you probably have a short list of portable machines that have it. If you don’t know that you need it, then I’m pretty confident saying this screen will work very well for you.

Keyboard
There’s nothing offensive about this keyboard. It’s easy to type on, has good feedback, and is comfortable for both short bursts and long typing sessions. It’s not a goldilocks keyboard in that it probably won’t be the perfect keyboard for anyone but it’s going to be a very good keyboard for everyone. I really do like the keyboard but it’s entirely forgettable – there’s no standout amazing feature and there’s nothing that irks me either. It’s just there and I have no complaints at all.

Touchpad
I love the size of this touchpad but it was a squirrelly mess for me. I ended up turning off nearly all the gestures since I would accidentally trigger them when typing, when moving the cursor, when trying to scroll, anytime I was even close to the touchpad really. It’s a great surface and easy to use but for me and the way I hold my hands, it registers lots of inadvertent touches. I’d try to scroll and minimize all my windows since it thought my two finger scroll had a third finger touching the touchpad. Disabling everything except scroll has made it much more predeictable. I don’t get frustrated using it now but I also use it like a touchpad from 10 years ago.

Build
Beautiful. Sleek. High end. The build of this machine is great. FusionTech is following some other well known manufacturer's thought process of don’t fix what isn’t broken. This body is the same as the last few generations but boy is it nice. And one of my favorite parts? The bottom can come off and the RAM, SSD, and fans are all serviceable and easily accessed. It’s a big machine so even though it’s a sleek build, it’s still…..well, thick. This isn’t a featherweight machine either. But it’s solid and well built and gives you a feeling of confidence.

Webcam
It’s there and not pointed up my nose. But if you rely on a webcam for work…. Maybe get an external one. You’ll be a lot happier.

Performance
The RAM, CPU, and GPU in this machine are all fantastic. I’m sure that this machine isn’t ideal for a core i9 but in my testing editing 4K video, it worked quite well and never got too hot. In fact, for shorter workloads, this machine is every bit as fast as my custom built desktop. For longer workloads, thermals might rear their ugly head but I’m very confident saying this will allow you to get any sort of productivity work done on the road. If you need a long render time or compute time? Maybe transfer the work files to a desktop for the final number crunching. But wow, what a great on the go machine.

IO
Thunderbolt 4 is great as is being able to charge the laptop from any of the ports. FusionTech feeling the need to include an HDMI and USB A to C dongle in the box? Well…. At least they included it. If you’re deep into the thunderbolt and USB C world, this won’t be a shock to you but if you mostly still live in USB A world, then welcome to dongle life if you buy this machine. But at least there’s an SD card reader built in. I can’t get too upset at FusionTech since they include a dongle but I’m not fully in USB C world yet so using this is more dongle life than any other machine I own.

Battery Life
If you’re on integrated graphics, battery life is decent. Not like leave your charger at home decent but like you won’t need to plug in at the coffee shop if you don’t want to. If you are using the discrete GPU… the battery is more like a long term UPS. You’ll stay powered on for a decent bit of time but you’re way closer to 1% of battery is 1 minute than I’d like to admit.
