text:
I would love to give a good review but, unfortunately when I received my laptop it had issues with wifi out of the box. It seemed to turn off the wifi on its own after 10-30 minutes. What I mean by turn off is that the computer would lose connection to the Internet, then lose the ability to find wifi connections. Sometimes if I disabled the connection and turned it back on it would work. Sometimes it would disable itself and required restart. It seemed to work fine while plugged in. I spent a couple of hours downloading and installing windows updates, hardware drivers and FusionTech drivers on a wired connection to see if it fixed the issue but, it didn't. I tried reformatting the drive (keep in mind this machine doesn't even have personal software on it yet), then going through the entire process 1 driver at a time to see if anything made it better or worse. I tried testing my wifi on 3 different devices including another FusionTech laptop to see if the issue was related to the router.

Eventually, I came to the conclusion that it was either a wifi specific hardware issue or a weird software bug that wasn't worth my time to test for. The computer was fast and responsive and the solid state drive made restarting the computer a dream during the driver updating process. I just can't afford to spend that much money on a laptop that I can't take anywhere.

I sent it back and am waiting on a refund so I can weigh my options. On a side note, I did look at the other reviews before buying this and it seems like a majority of people are enjoying this laptop. It may be just a lemon. Also, the self signing root issues that were mentioned some other comments have been patched out and are no longer an issue.

I would suggest doing your own research before buying this laptop. If yours works, Im sure it's well worth the price.

text:
Well, here are my thoughts on the laptop after several day having it. I will probably end up keeping the laptop. I haven't seem anything at this price point with these specs. I mainly use the laptop while on the couch. I use it to surf the web and have been playing Fallout 4 on it. So, here are my impressions on the different components.

1. Screen - I think this is my biggest gripe. I believe I have the LG panel in this laptop. Its a decent screen. From what I know there are two panels that come with this laptop. I did have to create two different profiles because of the screen. I created a web surfing and a game profile. The web surfing profile is turned down(brightness) with good color. I find this profile very acceptable. If I try to run FO4 with this profile, I cant see a thing when it is night. This is is the reason for a game profile with full brightness with everything turned up. If I leave this profile active when web surfing everything is washed out and unbearable, but again this profile is suitable for games. It could also be FO4 too. I cant turn up brightness ingame. Hey, maybe order a better panel in the future...

2. Keyboard - I think its fine maybe because I use chicklet type keyboards. I do have a mechanical keyboard that I use with my gaming rig, but the keyboard on the laptop is fine. I do use a FusionTech work laptop which I dislike because the amount of flex involved with the keyboard. The back-lit keys are a bonus too.

3. Speakers - I find the speakers lackluster on the laptop. Again, they are laptop speakers, so I wasn't expecting anything great. I will get a pop/distortion every now and then when watching youtube. I have messed with the FusionTech audio settings and that seems to help somewhat. I do use a lower profile bluetooth speaker, it sits on the laptop when I play games. Bluetooth speaker is 10x better.

4. Battery - The battery is great! If you are just surfing the web with about 75 percent brightness, it will last 6-8 hours on the battery. For a laptop this big, I was expecting 3-4 hours. That big battery helps! Of course, if I'm are playing games I always have the power cord plugged in.

5. Trackpad - I'm indifferent here. I never use trackpads on laptops. I have always used a mouse and will still use a mouse. For the couple of times I have used it, its works ok. I haven't had any issues with it. I guess if I used it exclusively, I would have more comments on it.

6. Gameplay - The gpu just chugs along. I've only played FO4 on it and it does a pretty good job. I think I'm playing with the majority of setting on high. I get around 40-45 fps which is fine with me.

I think that's all the major components. I have also added another SSD and different wifi card. I will be ordering another stick of memory this week. I have updated all drivers and the bios too. Overall, for what you get and pay for, it was a great value for me. I'm still looking at other gaming laptop, but I cant seem to find anything better at the moment. thanks...

title_x: Great for Gaming, Okay for Linux and Development
text:
I've had this laptop for the better part of a weekend. I really got it for developing Android apps as it allows me to upgrade the RAM which is essentially necessary for Android Studio. Though I have decided to keep Windows on it, my primary OS is Linux and most of my review will be about the Linux capabilities of this machine.

For my Linux Distro, I installed Linux Mint 17.3. At first, I wanted to install the new and beautiful Cinnamon DE but discovered the NVidia drivers aren't suited well out of the box for this machine and Linux compatibility. It is a known bug for the Linux Mint/Cinnamon teams and the fix for it is discussed in another review on here. I essentially walked right through Kris's review on this very laptop for how they were able to install Ubuntu on this machine. My install went very similarly - same issues with needing to adjust the boot script to boot with "nomodeset" and then swapping to NVidia drivers once the OS was loaded up.

The other issue with Linux has been the wireless card support. I will say that it appears FusionTech/Intel had a little goof-up with wireless connectivity on this card as the card seems to sporadically work and not work when coming out of sleep mode. In my Windows OS, I haven't had any problems after installing the latest Intel Dual Band WiFi driver for the 3165 model directly from the FusionTech Drivers and Downloads page. Linux does seem to have issues with the wireless card as well, but I think that stemmed from a problem with the old kernel that Linux Mint uses (3.19 or something). I upgraded the kernel to 4.5 and I can't necessarily say that it fixed the problem because I went through a bunch of hoops to get WiFi working on 3.19 kernel, but at the very least it didn't make the driver behave any worse.

Another important feature of this laptop was battery life for me. On Windows - its outstanding. I'm at 85% right now as I write this and my expected battery life remaining is around 12 hours. This is obviously while under very light usage and I've got the Power Saver feature from Windows 10 on, but it is still very useful and the computer is still performing smoothly. Linux, again, quite another story. With the experience I had with the graphics drivers and the WiFi, I ended up switching from Cinnamon DE to MATE, and now I think I'll be reinstalling again to put on XFCE. The battery life on Linux after a full charge was estimated to be around 5-8 hours, depending on usage. This is stock battery performance with no tweaks to power settings or 3rd party power apps. I have not tweaked the power settings myself much because for my Linux needs, 8 hours would be plenty. However I reckon with the proper tweaking and knowledge the Linux OS should be easily able to deliver 10-12 hours of battery life.

I'll also comment briefly about the gaming performance. For me, I'm an Elder Scrolls guy. So the first games that went on this machine were Elder Scrolls Online and Skyrim. Elder Scrolls Online plays very smoothly on Low to Medium settings, though frames are locked at 30 fps when on battery - probably a good thing, and also probably adjustable as well. Skyrim also played smoothly at 60 fps on Ultra settings with no mods (haven't had time to get much else on yet). The temperatures according to MSI Afterburner for both Skyrim and Elder Scrolls Online stayed right around 60-65 degrees for both the CPU and GPU. I don't have much experience with laptop temperatures during gaming but considering my NVIDIA 970 desktop GPU runs these games at around 60 degrees and my 6th gen i5 6500 runs them around 30 degrees, I'd say those temperatures are pretty good. title_x: Perfect for the cost! A 960m + a SSD is the BEST choice for this price range.
text:
I still can't believe I found something this decent as a laptop, for this price. I'm honestly shocked. I've built 4 desktop computers, so I'm not about to say that this will play games at an amazing settings/frames per second. However, this computer is certainly better than most things you will find at this price range.

The key features that I need for a computer before it's worth it is:
-Best Graphics card for the price
-At least 8gb of RAM (more doesn't really matter. 8gb is a very good spot)
-SSD (120gb is good, more is fantastic!)
-Quad Core
-Runs Windows (for programs and games)

[This laptop has all of this.]

The graphics card for this is a 960m. It's average 3d benchmark is almost 1700 (all posted Benchmarks can be found on the same website if you google it), which isn't all that wonderful when you compare it to a GTX 980 (which in comparison, has the average benchmark somewhere around 9700). This is a micro graphics card, because you just can't install a full-size graphics card into a laptop for a number of reasons. If you want the best graphics, build your own PC. However, this is certainly better than Integrated Graphics (Intel HD 5000 has the average 3d benchmark around 600 - NEVER buy something with Integrated Graphics if you want to play video games).

Let's get realistic, a 970m is going to be much better (average 3d benchmarks around 4200), but wasn't worth the extra money spent for me. A 950m isn't going to be as good (average 3d benchmarks around 1400) as the 960m, but I have seen a lot of laptops offer the 950m for this same price range. Overall, if you are buying laptop for gaming you need to understand this. The 960m, which this laptop has, is a great deal. Heck, looking at some of the other laptops on Amazon, I'm seeing people buy a laptop with a 960m for $1100+. To push this point even further, I'm seeing people buy laptops at $1000+ and they still have Integrated Graphics (which sucks!!!).

In summary, don't be a sucker and buy a laptop with a 950m, 940m, ANY FORM OF INTEGRATED GRAPHICS (Intel HD 5000). This is a great machine, and it's super quick because of the SSD (I'm not exaggerating. Once you get a SSD, you will never go back to a Hard-Disk Drive). It may not be the very best on the market, but that's actually a good thing for a number of reasons.

Think about it this way: Laptops don't have the longest life span. It's not like a desktop PC, where I can just install a new Graphics Card and re-use my old parts. As technology advances, we tend the previous "better versions" of the product become cheaper. Objectively, this laptop is nearly as good as the other $1200+ laptops minus the CPU (which doesn't really need to be the best. You won't ever feel the difference unless you are doing a lot of CPU intensive things) and GPU (which this GPU, or graphics card, is more than capable of running a lot of games at decent settings. The 970m alone is several times better than this but typically is NOT worth paying $300+ more for me). In 5-10 years when you have to upgrade your laptop, you will be glad that you didn't buy that you didn't waste a crap ton of money over a laptop that wasn't that objectively better. Realistically, in the next 5 years, Graphics Cards will be SEVERAL times better than this current generation. Wait, and save that money for something else.

Final notes: The laptop has pretty good battery life, doesn't come with a whole lot of crap software, doesn't have a glossy case finish (I'm not a a fan of glossy), and has a pretty decent touch-pad. It looks pretty attractive if you like black/red, and it has another slot to add in more Storage. Overall, I'm super happy I purchased this. I have literally no complaints as of yet. It's no desktop, but it's a good laptop for the price.

title_x: Meets and exceeds my already high expectations.
text: Ordered this laptop with high hopes for it as the parts in it looked really good for the price. I must say, you're getting a lot for your money. I'm not the biggest gamer in the world but there is one game I play and that is Borderlands 2. I can run at max settings (Physx on low because that drops frames for even some of the best gaming pc's) at 55-60 fps while not charging. When it's charging it just about always runs 60 fps even when I turn Physx up to medium. It does get a little warm in the top left corner of the laptop about where the speaker is when running Borderlands but it's not too bad. Sometimes I can hear the fan decently loud, but it's a really smooth sound. Borderlands 2 is not an easy game to run at max settings by any means. I'm actually in college right now so I didn't even get this totally for gaming, like I said, only thing in gaming is that I just wanted to run BL2 smoothly. This thing is FAST. Very quick start up, obviously having an SSD. Has an empty slot which I plan to plug the 1tb hdd from my last laptop in to. I personally am not sure why everyone is talking about screen bleed because I don't see any and that was the one thing that scared me when reading the reviews. The screen is BEAUTIFUL and the colors look amazing. The keyboard is pretty decent and I like how quiet it is. I usually type pretty hard, but I don't hear much out of this keyboard other than the spacebar but that's normal because it's such a big key. The backlighting of the keyboard is amazing. It doesn't just stay on, the light actually fades out after about 30 seconds (haven't timed it) and turns back on as soon as you hit a key. For a laptop, the speakers are actually great quality and can get pretty loud for laptop speakers without losing quality. I never really used my pc/laptop speakers before this, I have just used my Bose headphones but I can actually stand the speakers in this. The battery lasts about 6+ hours with moderate use with it leaning more towards performance so I know if you set it to longer battery life you would get more than 7 hours out of it. But heavy gaming drains the battery real quick as in about 3 and a half hours from full down to 10%. The build quality is really nice, I love the way it feels and looks. It doesn't LOOK like a gaming laptop. No one else even knows I bought what FusionTech considered a gaming laptop, they just think it's a really good laptop (Which it is.). But I didn't buy it to be a gaming laptop, and before I bought it I thought of it as just a great laptop, with great parts, that will run fast. Especially for the money. But now that I've had it for a few days, I know that you could call it a dedicated mid-range gaming laptop. It seems to compete with gaming laptops priced at about 1100-1300 from what I've tested of them (Never really owned them so I can't say anything about long term. I've only tested some out.). I honestly don't have an complaints about this purchase so far. As far as laptops go I've had an Asus and an HP, both of which I had to send in within a month after I got them for having issues that were noticeable within a days. If I run into any issues I'll update but as of now, this thing is a very reasonably, maybe even under-priced, beast that is definitely worth taking a look at and comparing to other options. The other laptop I was looking at was the ASUS K501UX (which is a little cheaper as of right now, but not by much.) because I really did like my last ASUS, but I'm glad I bought this as it is MILES better than my last rig. I chose this one because it was newer, and it is quad-core instead of dual. Also, I don't need an i7 especially with these 6th gen cores, and this is a really good i5 core. Not worth getting an i7. Plus the ASUS looks like my last one and the build quality on that didn't feel nearly as nice as this. Anyways, I think that's enough praise for now. Good luck with your shopping and again, make sure to take this laptop into consideration.

Absolutely love this laptop. This is my first laptop, and when I went in, I wanted something that could handle gaming, but was below the $1000 price point and wasn't too bulky or obnoxious looking. My experience with it has been great so far.

I went ahead and installed Google Chrome, since I've got bookmarks synced to there, and web browsing has been snappy, with the SSD instead of the hard drive. I also downloaded LibreOffice 5.0, which is a free alternative to Microsoft Office, and it gets the job done.

This works great as a gaming laptop as well, running more demanding games like GTA V, even with maxed out graphics settings. It can also handle whatever you throw at it for casual gaming, running smoothly overall.

I would highly recommend this laptop to those who are willing to spend $800 on a great laptop that gets the job done, for both gaming and working.

text:
I just received this beauty a few hours ago, and all I can say is that it is a beast of a laptop. Super fast and quiet, beautiful screen, (I dont think there is any bleed on my screen. If I have, it is really not noticeable) great sound overall.

I'm a graduate student and consider myself a gamer, although I dont have much time for it anymore. This laptop is perfect for my needs, bc it has a great cpu and gpu, so I can throw all kinds of programs and games in there, and it shouldn't be a problem. I didn't have time to install any games yet, but I'm soon gonna be able to do it. (I can't wait to play The Witcher, Far Cry, Skyrim, Fallout 4 in some weeks, and a few others)

Those are the features that are standing out for me on the first day:
+ Beautiful IPS screen
+ Super fast (it takes 15 to 20 seconds to boot up, which is ages ahead of my 5 year old Toshiba Satellite)
+ Good battery ( I have been using this for 4 hours and a half setting up the laptop, watching videos and listening to music, and I still have 50% of the battery left)
+ Great sound (Although I use my headphones almost always, I was impressed by how loud the speakers are. But have in mind that the bass is not gonna be very strong, this is still a laptop we are talking about)
+ I like how the audio jack and the charger goes to the left side of it, so I have my right side free to have a mouse and play my games
+ I love how easy it is to open the back of the laptop and install another SSD and/or Memory. I havent done it myself, but will be upgrading it soon.
+ It doesn't look like a gaming laptop, so I could take it to work or classes and people wouldn't be looking any different (as they would if I show up with an Advance or MSI for example lol)

Now there are a few things that could be done differently, but they are very small annoyances, nothing to be worried about.
- I use a mouse always, but I wasn't impressed by the touch pad. I have found better ones on cheaper laptops. But hey, if you are using the touch pad to play games, you are not a serious gamer lol. Another thing is that I think the touch pad should be more on the right side. I still have space for the left hand to press W,A,S,D while playing, but its not very much.
- Although the backlit keyboard works wonderfully, I was't impressed by the keyboard itself. It's not bad, really! But it's not amazing also. It's an OK keyboard.
- The laptop is a little bit on the heavy side, but again its not too bad. I'm still gonna be able to put it in my backpack and go to work and classes just fine. I just wish it would be lighter. The battery charger is very heavy, I had never seen one so bulky before, but I'm still OK with that.

Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with my purchase, I searched a lot for a good gaming laptop under $1000, and this was the best one you could find. If you consider everything this baby has to offer, $800 is really cheap. If you are not sure about getting it, I would say yes, go ahead! I don't think you will regret it! Way to go FusionTech!!!

title_x: Good Computer, but Received Bad Hardware
text:
A great laptop by all means for the price point. The new Skylake, 6th generation i5 processor coupled with 8GB of RAM and SSD booted Windows 10 very quickly. However I unfortunately landed some hardware problems with my unit.

I quickly replaced Windows with Xubuntu (Linux distribution) as most of my work is done on Linux. It worked for a few hours, but then, when I restarted the computer, a FusionTech BIOS alert quickly popped up saying that some hardware was going to fail soon. I pressed continue, and then Linux started reporting hardware failures. Finally, when I booted into the actual operating system, I ran a disk assessment check using gnome-disk-utility and it too reported that the SSD would soon fail.

The moral of this story: run a SMART test on your SSD when you get your laptop to make sure everything is really OK, otherwise you may run into problems as well down the line.

I will update my review when I get my new unit.

I can't believe how fast this thing is. I'm also very impressed with the 960m graphics card. It performs far better than I expected: SWtOR @ ultra, TW:Attila @ ultra. If you want a budget gaming laptop, this thing is top of the line.

Pros:
quad core i5 SKYLAKE processor (latest 6th gen intel processor)
960m dedicated card with 4 gb graphics ram
M.2 SSD (fast fast)
Subtle good looks.

Cons:
Not overclockable.
A little too wide to fit in my old 15" laptop bag - wish it were 1/8" less wide.
The 8 gb RAM isn't DDR4 (mobo doesn't support it?)
m.2 ssd is sata, not pcie (awww, shucks)
^^both of these things would probably raise the price by $500.

Thoughts:
--Some people have complained about the track pad, but I have little problem with it. Yes it behaves differently from a Macbook, or HP laptop. Different brands are... different.
--The matte screen is perfect. If you like glossy screens, then you may hate it. Personally, I don't like reflective, glossy screens -- they make sunlight and bright lights your greatest enemy.
--Windows 10 has wonky scaling issues. Win10 defaults are set to 125% scale in settings, which makes some text look really, really bad (particularly my browser). I set the scale down to 100%, and it's much better. (Users must be smarter than Windows)

title_x: Please connect the correct FusionTech AC power adapter for best system operation
text:
At this point Amazon customer service gets 6 stars out of 5, but FusionTech customer service was very disappointing. Based on all the positive reviews that I read before ordering, I took a chance on returning my order for a replacement.

Here's what went wrong at FusionTech -- the cable that came for the brick provided kept falling out of the brick and couldn't be pushed on far enough to be secure while the other end would less frequently fall out of the laptop. Though it had a blue light at the laptop end showing that it was live, it did not charge the computer and resulted in a message that said "The AC power adapter is not recognized. System performance will be impacted. Please connect the correct FusionTech AC power adapter for best system operation."

After being told the estimated wait time to talk to customer service was 15 min, I spent more than 40 min on hold waiting to talk to a FusionTech rep before I got, "Sorry, customer support is now closed, call back tomorrow." After about 20 min on hold, I'd also tried to initiate a chat. After being lured into thinking that would work by seeing a countdown of the number ahead of me in the queue, the door was slammed shut with me and 50 or so other folks still in line.

So this AM, I wasted all morning trying to get to someone to tell me what they could do and to get a pdf of the warranty that had to be agreed to but couldn't be printed or saved when setting up the computer. The last FusionTech rep I spoke with suggested returning the system -- at last, an honest attempt to help.

Another problem was that the Wifi I'd turned off randomly decided to turn itself back on. (I'd turned off Wifi to use an Ethernet cable as I was too lazy to dig out the password for my router and a connected cable was right at hand.) Then, the computer suddenly decided that it couldn't see the Ethernet cable that was plugged in and that had been used all along for web access. ???

And then again, the name change for the computer that was supposed to take on reboot didn't take after 2 or 3 cold boots.

On the positive side, I found the touchpad much more manageable than I'd expected based on other reviews here, until that is, every program in the world decided to try to update itself, then it became a total mess, even though windows Task Manager showed memory use never over 39% and only periodic spikes up to about 80% in CPU use. Not sure what may be Windows 10 problems rather than hardware problems.

I will update after I receive the replacement box. I appreciate everyone who has posted reviews here. I found all of them most helpful in my buying decision.

UPDATE: 12/10/2015
I received the replacement several days ago and it came with a brick that plugs into and recharges the computer. However, the cord from the outlet to the brick(A/C adapter) still falls out all the time. The touchpad goes haywire when some program sucks up most of the computer resources, but its been hard to pin down which of the pre-loaded programs tend to cause the problems. WiFi now working fine, haven't tried Ethernet yet. Haven't put any other software on the system yet as am still evaluating the computer itself, but so far, seems Ok aside from the problems noted. Upping the rating to three stars for now from previous one star.

title_x: Great laptop, but beware the weakness of plastic laptop casing
text:
Bought this laptop earlier this year (February or so I believe). It worked great for a while and I didn't have many issues. I used it to play Overwatch, League of Legends, as well as do video editing, audio editing, and photo editing using Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Lightroom, and Audition. I never had any real issues software-wise.

There is one very big con though that is forcing me to get a new laptop within 10 months of buying this one. The case cannot hold up the weight of this laptop. Back in July, I sat down in a chair while holding the laptop open on the right side with one hand. As soon as I sat down, the weight of the laptop and the lack of support on the left side caused the grating near the fan and the left screen hinge to crack and the case to permanently sit open exposing internals and the left hinge. I made zero contact with anything, it didn't bump anything. All I did was sit down normally. Replacement parts for this model are incredibly difficult to find (I was unable to find any). As a result, the gap has only gotten wider, causing my mouse to have issues it wasn't having before. The left side of my keyboard from the edge of the case to the F3 key is permanently slanted upward and every time I open the laptop, I have to press down on the exposed part to keep it from getting worse. Unfortunately, for regular use, it's gotten worse. I actually can rarely get the trackpad to register an actual press. Only tapping the pad works regularly now. I can't tape the case closed because if I tape it, the fan vents are covered or the charger port is covered. This issue has convinced me never to get a plastic-cased laptop again. I've attached three photos: one of how I was holding it when the incident happened and two of the split casing.

It's a great laptop, but be very aware you are getting a plastic laptop casing and amazing for the price. I fully understand that sacrifices have to be made to keep great specs at a low cost. This is reality and I am not holding FusionTech at fault. The laptop is heavy, so the plastic, over time, may have the same outcome for someone else as it did for me. Had I realized sooner to make sure I was balancing it more intentionally when transporting it, this might not have happened, so I am warning everyone else!

The seller advertises that the laptop is very good, yet it was anything but good. I'd like to list it in a diary format with the four short days that I have been using this product.

Day 1:
Package arrived late, but no problem, it came in at least. I was extremely excited as this was my first high quality gaming laptop. I set it up, transferred some files, and generally had zero problems playing games like Dark Souls 3. Called it a night, and prepared myself to lose myself to laziness and obesity.

Day 2:
The laptop was still working fine! Got to play it for hours on end, and customized it even more to match my preferences. It was like a beautiful lady that was willing to do everything for me. And I was ready to commit to this lady for as long as the video game industry doesn't leave me in the dust!

Day 3:
And the beautiful lady had a beautiful body, but her face began to freaking melt. To clarify, the screen essentially bugged the hell out. It flickered very often and would just sometimes show static. I treated this laptop right, I didn't do anything to damage it. It began to become so bad, I had to connect it to a different monitor just to see what I was doing. It was hard to write an email to a professor or talk to my friends when the screen flickers like the TV from "The Ring". However, I decided to tough it out. Turned off the computer, put the screen down, and then caledl it a night,

Day 4:
The screen flickering only got worse. Instead this time, the screen had to be kept at certain angles so the flickering was kept calm. The unfortunate thing was that the screen had to be pushed way back or I had to just put it out of view so I have the monitor to use. It's like you discovered that the beautiful lady's face had stopped melting below her chin so you had to talk to her with her head flung back. If you wanted to see her face, you needed her to play the worst game of Limbo. At this point, I primarily used my wonderful monitor. But then, I decided to turn off the laptop as I wouldn't be using it for a couple of hours. Then it didn't turn on. The screen didn't turn on. The face of the lady completely melted off. The monitor could not connect as the computer didn't display anything anymore. The laptop was as good as dead, the lady was dead. I had a faceless lady with a beautiful body. I didn't have a responding partner, I had a mannequin.

Overall, I could understand why a used laptop would have some problems. But to label it as "Very Good," is misleading since the one problem I had should have been in a laptop labeled "Very Bad; Don't Buy". I wish that more testing would have been done, since I feel like all the seller had done was just hard reset the laptop and considered it good enough. As of now, I thought I could be saving money buying used and trusting what seemed like a good alternative. However, I learned from this experience to only buy new. A new partner will be less likely to disappoint you than a used partner.

text:
This is a review as well as an opportunity for me to ask some questions, which I hope would get better answers in the comments section than in "Customer Questions & Answers".

I've had it for two weeks now. Overall it's a very solid laptop. I don't really game, and mainly got this to do office work, so in a sense it's an overkill, but the deal is good, and the specs are spectacular. I'll keep it simple, and divide the reviews to pros, cons, neutrals / undecided, and questions.

Pros:
- Speed: It's a fast computer. Startup is in seconds, and waking up is almost instantaneous. Basic everyday work a normal person performs on a laptop, e.g. browsing, viewing videos, office work, etc. happens with blazing speed. Very occasionally there's a slight lag (with "program not responding" notification in the title bar) when opening HWMonitor, which tracks stuff like temp, but I suspect that's a one off.
- Value: I think it goes without saying, but you can't find a better laptop for the money.
- Upgrading Ease: The back panels opens by unscrewing only one screw, and even a novice like me was able to add 8 GB of RAM easily. I plan to add a second SSD soon.
- Speaker: I'm no laptop audiophile, but the speaker has good volume to say the least.
- Lack of Bloatware: I think only some FusionTech stuff and McAfee come with. I did a clean install with Windows 10 Enterprise, and I suggest a clean install for everyone, just to be safe.
- Lack of FusionTech Root Cert: Unless I got a used laptop, and someone else already removed it... No FusionTech Root Cert found on this machine.

Cons:
- Weight: It's on the heavy - side for a 15.6" laptop. Not sure if the specs warrant the heaviness, but don't buy the laptop for portability.
- Fingerprints: Honestly, I think most laptops show fingerprints easily, so maybe it's symptomatic to all laptops.
- Slight Imperfection on Top Panel: Upon arrival, on the top panel (back of LCD), there is a very slight nick, as if someone used a very thin needle and poked the panel at one spot. It's very noticeable to the touch, but mot much so to the eye (although you can see it. I might upload a photo later, at work right now). Doesn't bother me too much though, and it's obviously just my machine that has the issue.

Neutrals / Undecided:
- Track Pad: I see why some may find the texture and location of the track pad bothersome, but I personally have used it without issues. Occasionally I feel like it doesn't register a tap as a left - click, but that could be me rather than the track pad.
- Keyboard: It's okay. I'm not too particular on keyboards. No sounds when you type.
- Build: It's plastic, so just know what you're getting, but overall it looks / feels more sturdy than not, in part due to the heft.
- Battery life: I haven't done a comprehensive testing, but I'm getting about 1 hr per 10% battery drain (100% to 90%, etc.) from basic browsing with lowish (but not lowest) dimness. However, even when playing a very basic game like Dominion online, battery life is under 3 hours. So I suspect you can get 8+ hours from very basic use, but not much at all when gaming. I will say, I did a test against my girlfriend's newly bought ASUS K501UX with a lower - capacity battery, where we turned off the screen and continuously played YouTube videos without volume. In about 3 hours, this FusionTech drained to 77%, however her Asus only drained to 81%. That did cause me some concern, so if anyone has any comments on that, I'd appreciate it very much!
- Heat: I've never had it get "hot", but it does get noticeably warm even from basic use on the table. I think it's more than lukewarm, but it's not "hot" by anyone's standards I don't think. Again, my girlfriend's Asus does MUCH better in this sense, where the Asus never gets more than lukewarm. From HWMonitor, the CPU temp hovers from 40 - 50 Celsius from basic usage (sometimes lower, and occasionally higher), and can get above 50 from basic gaming like Dominion online (although it doesn't necessarily stay above 50). I think with heavier gaming, it has the "potential" to get "hot", but that's just my conjecture.

Questions:
- As previously mentioned, are my concerns regarding battery life and heat warranted?
- If my concerns regarding battery life and heat are warranted, is that a problem with the model, or a problem with my machine only? So should I try to get it exchanged for a different machine?

Thank you for reading!

[[VIDEOID:b59c3fcefb85db221b9541409c0e9f2a]] FusionTech G7 7790 is the model I am reviewing.
FusionTech has been well known for Advance products for quite some time though this isn’t formally an Advance product this is more or less and Advance computer. It has the Advance software preinstalled and that is where you are able to customize things like the color of the backlit keyboard.

So let’s look at specs:
i7-9750H. 9th generation i7 is a great touch
RAM 16GB DDR4. I would have expected more at this price point but that is an easy upgrade if you want it. This is a dual bay with two 2x8GB 2666MHz sticks from the manufacturer. It is upgradable to 2x16 or 32GB total. I will end up upgrading this because I love having as much RAM as possible. Chipset is Intel HM370
Storage is a 512 GB SSD which is fantastic I will only use SSD because the speed for reading and writing is insanely noticeable compared to standard hard drives. This is a decent size drive though if your storing games this may be a little on the small side.
Now for the dedicated graphics. I am glad this comes with Nvidia as I prefer it over AMD. This model comes with the GeForce GTX 1660 Ti. Beautiful graphics off the bat. I haven’t customized or overclocked anything at this point.

This is also the 17” screen model and if your going for a gaming laptop let’s face it, you want the big boy. I was a bit surprised to see that it’s not a touch screen. I will say out of the box your benchmarks will seem low and disappointing. It takes some system updates and tweaking to really optimize this computer but for anyone getting a gaming laptop you shouldn’t have any issues figuring out what to do.

title_x: Good for gaming, not great for basic everyday stuff
text:
UPDATE: Happy to say this laptop works flawlessly with Oculus Rift! (Once you update your graphics card drivers.)

Keep in mind you'll only be able to plug in two sensors unless you get something to give you extra USB ports, but otherwise I was very impressed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Before I get into the details, I want to note - because this laptop is primarily made for Gaming, I'm giving it 3 stars. If I intended to use this for work or other computer tasks on a regular basis, my rating would be lower.

-GAMING-
When it comes to gaming, so far my experience has been quite positive. That said, I was really disappointed when I realized how quickly this laptop gets uncomfortably hot. Given that it's a LAPtop, I feel it's fair to expect that it be usable without getting unreasonably hot while using it on your lap.

However, I think at least part of this problem is related to how quickly the computer gets overwhelmed. In fact, even during menial tasks like browsing the web or even using the file explorer, the fan will come on because the computer is so overwhelmed. That's something I've never experienced with my main computer unless I have multiple windows with several tabs open that I haven't closed out for a few days, along with a few other applications that have also been left running for a while.

Needless to say, for a computer whose main purpose is performance, I was shocked at how easily I could get it to a state where it was overwhelmed. And yet somehow despite how overwhelmed and hot it gets, it still manages to perform really well when you’re gaming on it. Just don’t play with it on your lap without something to protect your legs! (I may be a little repetitive on this point, but when they brag “an outstanding dual-fan cooling system”… I think you deserve to know it’s not going to protect you!)

Graphically, games look beautiful, and that's definitely one of the best things about this laptop. However, the fan runs so loud when you're doing anything that you'd better have some good headphones so you can still hear the sound over the fan. Given that they say “Experience faster load times and a quieter system”, I have to wonder what they think “quieter” means.

-PHYSICAL DESIGN-
This computer is about as attractive as I’d expect for the brand that made it, which is not very attractive. That said it is on the nicer side out of the computers they make.

It's quite heavy, so I suppose making the body out of plastic is one way to avoid adding to that weight further. However, the plastic is extremely concerning if the laptop were ever to fall even a couple of feet. While I'm extremely careful and don't expect this to happen, especially to a 17 lb. laptop, I have to wonder exactly what the product designers were thinking. "Ah yes, let's make it a 'laptop' so it's portable... but an inch thick with a 17" screen so that that no one can actually find a case for it. Then let's give it a plastic casing so if anyone is foolish enough to transport it without protection, they are incredibly nervous about it."

It just doesn't make sense to me! Maybe there's something I'm missing here as my gaming is usually more focused on consoles, both ones connected to the TV and handheld consoles. That said, for a computer that costs over $1,000, it's concerning to me that there doesn't seem to be a safe way to transport it, despite it being a laptop. I just don't see what the benefit is if you can't feel confident bringing it with you somewhere.

On to my next point, which is... stickers. Why are there stickers on such an expensive product? I know this has been a thing for a long time on PCs, but why? And perhaps more importantly, why are they so hard to take off and why do they live so much sticky residue behind?

The keyboard is really nice and probably the one redeeming feature of the physical design. It feels good to type on and the fact that it can light up different colors is fun. Sadly when trying to use the built in software to adjust the colors so I could have multiple colors at once (more like a rainbow), I couldn’t find any way to get the colors to be as vibrant as the basic default red, blue, and green. Instead they look pale and washed out no matter how much I move around the color wheel.

The trackpad is unfortunately way too easy to hit accidentally and I’ve been looking for a way to disable it completely as it’s really frustrating how in the way it is. I also find it awkward the way it’s positioning off-center, especially because I’m used to laptops with the track pad in the middle where I have space for both hands to comfortably rest while still being able to access the whole keyboard easily.

The area around the keyboard and trackpad also picks up the oils from your skin very quickly so you end up with shiny smudges all over it. Pity since otherwise it would look pretty nice.

Overall it's not the ugliest laptop I've ever seen, but it's not something I'd show off to anyone. And that's saying something given that we've had sleek, beautiful computers publicly available for quite some time now. The only conclusion I can come to is that this brand just doesn't care about design.

-GENERAL USER INTERFACE AND EXPERIENCE-
Having grown up with computers made by this particular brand, I was surprised to see just how many things *haven't* changed in the last 20 years. For example, some of the screens I saw while getting the computer set up for the first time could easily have been designed 20 years ago, and in reality, some of them probably haven't changed in that time as far as their design goes. Rough, pixelated blue and black was not something I expected to ever see on a new computer at this point in my life!

Perhaps more disappointing somehow was how ugly the set-up screens were and how even the default background for the desktop ended up looking obviously pixelated in areas where there are gradients. For a high-end computer that's meant for gaming, I would expect the user interface to at least seem like it's trying to look like it was designed in the last ten years?

In using the computer for everyday tasks, I've had random things pop up at me that I did nothing to trigger, as well as fun little error that come out of nowhere even when all I'm doing is browsing the internet.

Recently I was in the middle of something and the computer started updating itself out of nowhere and didn't give me the option to opt out of it. I'm sure there's a setting somewhere that turns on automatic updates, but to have no chance to prevent my computer from being taken over for nearly an hour when I was working on something is incredibly frustrating to say the least.

Right after setting up the laptop, I went to run the updates that were recommended. Everything was downloaded, it restarted, took a while to get through it, and then I saw a screen pop up with a nature-y background, which promptly disappeared. Then the screen went black and the fan was running really loudly. I sat there for 15 minutes with the screen black and the fan running wondering whether I should be concerned. Eventually I pressed something (had already tried moving the mouse and no luck) and the login screen popped up. After a while I discovered that the login screen doesn't show up automatically. You have to do something to get it to appear. And maybe this is just me, but as someone who hasn't used Windows 10 before, it would have been really nice to have some kind of guidance on how the login screen worked the first time I used it so I wasn't sitting there wondering if my brand new laptop was broken.

In general, this laptop just… seems to have a lot of problems? Both in poorly designed user interface and in actual errors and it not running well at times. I find this pretty concerning given the price and the fact that it’s brand new. I would expect some odd issues here and there maybe 5-8 years down the road, but practically out of the box with hardly anything installed? I expected better.

Also, how is it that in 2019 it’s a several steps long process to take a screenshot that’s not just the whole screen? Instead of having a built-in way to do this, you have to use the ancient “Print Screen” function and then open up an editor to crop the image. This is a huge pain if you ever want or need to take screenshots that are more focused rather than your entire screen.

-CAMERA AND AUDIO-
If you're hoping to use this for any kind of online meeting, please just go look for another computer. The webcam quality is downright awful and the speaker feeds back directly into the microphone because of its placement. Just... don't.

Also, the sound from the speaker in general is just… meh? Things sound kind of flat like there’s no dimension to them.

I’m honestly not a sound person at all, so I can’t say much more. The speaker is just not impressive.

-PORTS-
I really appreciate that this laptop has an ethernet port, an HDMI port, 1 USB port on the left, 1 on the back, and 1 on the right. Dividing up the USB ports in particular is really handy.

There’s also your basic headphone jack, a security lock spot, a DisplayPort, and an SD card slot.

-BATTERY-
This battery is pretty poor for a laptop. As mentioned above, it doesn’t seem to actually be intended to be very portable (except maybe from room to room at home). I suppose if you accept that, it’s fair to assume you can plan on having this plugged in basically all the time, particularly if you’re planning on actually using it for gaming. I believe it lasts around 4 hours with basic computing tasks like browsing the web. My guess is that it’s more like two when I’m gaming.

-THE INSIDES-
I know some people mentioned getting the G5 instead of the G7 in the reviews here. I can confirm that I did get the 17” inch screen, the 16GB of RAM, the i7 processor, and the 512GB hard drive promised(well, 476GB after everything that was pre-installed).

-VR COMPATIBILITY-
I plan to test it with an Oculus Rift soon and plan to update here when I have the chance to do that. From what I can tell, the specs should be high enough. I recently ran the Vive and Oculus test software to make sure it , it's just a matter of which Graphics card is physically set up in the spot that can be accessed by the VR headset? (I'm sure there's a better way of explaining that! But that's my rough understanding of how it works.)

Sure, this may be overkill when it comes to content creation but when the turn around times are short having all this power to compete it quickly is great. Plus being able to create HD video quickly is awesome!!

If you're debating whether or not you should go with a laptop on the pricey side, just buy the pricey one. In the 3 laptops I've bought and run through due to subpar components I spent more money than this 1 laptop cost.

text:
This replaces my Advance 17 which was deployed in 2014. How's it stack up? Well....

The BLUF statement: The G7 (and I did receive a G7, not a G5) is a very good "right now" gaming laptop. By that I mean it will play (with two exceptions, see below) pretty much everything out there with high-level video settings. There are some caveats there which I'll get into, but bottom line up front: it may come across as a budget Advance but the performance is really very good.

Now then.

The G series is replacing the Worktops in this space. The idea is that if you aren't looking to go whole hog into the Advance world but would rather have a very easy Stock Spec Is All I Need gaming machine, the G series is there as an option. That FusionTech owns Advance does allow for some supply chain efficiencies (indeed, the G7 uses an Advance 4 cell battery) so there's some good crossover, but make no mistake - if you want the absolute cream of the crop future proofed expandable gaming laptop, the G7 isn't going to be it.

But that's not really the point of the G series. It exists as an easy way to play today's games, and at that it does a very good job. I'll hit various components in turn below and talk about some of the design decisions and compromises FusionTech made to bring this laptop into being. I'll also have to point out that the 5 years separating my Advance 17 and this G7 is very noticeable....new games that my Advance struggles with are a breeze for the G7, all the more interesting since the G7 is, in my opinion, a 2019 mid-range gaming laptop where as 5 years ago that Advance was upper tier.

Physical design: It looks like a mid 1990's laptop, but that belies the power under the keyboard. When closed it doesn't look like anything special, and certainly doesn't have the attitude that an Advance has. It would not look out of place in an office. It's about as thin as something like this can be (what with the dual cooling, heatsinks, etc) and the materials are...largely plastic. There's a bit of heft to it but nothing outrageous. In other words, typical FusionTech laptop look and feel. The tradeoff here is that with case volume being minimal, there are some cooling issues since there's not much free space in the case for air circulation. Cooling tubes help this somewhat, but know that you'll feel the heat after about an hour of gaming.

There's quite a bit made of the port placement on this laptop, with the ad copy saying major ports are placed in the back to stay out of the way. Power plugs into the back, as does a USB 3.1 port, HDMI, security port, etc. BUT there are ports on either side as well, whether Thunderbolt/USB-C or a SD card reader. For controller use there's enough flexibility there to keep mice or other devices out of the way, as well as a (recommended) external keyboard. And why do I recommend that external keyboard?

Because this thing gets warm, hot even. After an hour killing Trinity thugs as Lara Croft, the keyboard was really quite hot, especially in the middle. Fans were working, and working quite loudly I'll add, so it never got to boiling hot but it still was more than noticeable. I got to the point of hooking it to an external monitor with a external keyboard for real marathon sessions. I did notice that the majority of the heat did seem to be coming through the keyboard, so the heatsinks on the side and back do very well in those immediate locations, but I'm not sure they are up to keeping the entire chassis cool.

Processor - ninth gen Core I7. It screams. I'm frankly surprised to see a processor of this caliber in a laptop in this niche. Nuff said.

Screen: On this I've been spoiled with my Advance 17. The G7 screen is....fine. I mean, given the spec sheet (Nvidia GTX, etc) this is NOT a 4k gaming machine. Because of that, I think FusionTech may have chintzed a little on the screen and went with a standard 1920x1080 knowing it would never be pushed. I won't say that colors are washed out, but in comparison to the same resolution on my Advance, neither do they really pop. Blacks aren't as light-sucking as the Advance either, something that's kind of a big deal in gaming today. Don't get me wrong, it's not BAD...but it's not the best screen I've ever seen on a gaming laptop either. Again, it's becoming clear to me that FusionTech's focus on this series is to make a laptop that appeals to a wider chunk of gamers than the top .05% who demand top tier screens and don't mind paying for them.

RAM: Not the sexiest part of the computer, but pretty important especially for graphics-intensive gaming where the video memory may be stressed (a potential consideration with the Nvidia GTX...more on which in a minute). 16GB shipped, which because I'm a worry wart seems to me to be on the lower end of the required scale. 2 slots, and I'd say if you're looking forward to Cyberpunk 2077 you may want to put this near the top of the list to upgrade. Don't waste money on LED-blinged RAM either...you won't see it in the laptop, and the physical clearances are a little tight for them anyway. That said, 16GB is a solid amount for a good chunk of games and pretty much every Indie out there. I will be going to 32GB on this machine though. UPDATE: I went with 32GB of Corsair Vengeance (CMSX32GX4M2A2666C18) memory...works perfectly with slightly lower but still comparable latency. It makes streaming on Twitch or doing video capture much more stable. Another point: out of the box 16GB doesn't provide a very comfortable environment for video/photo editing, so the extra memory here is very needed for those tasks.).

Graphics: The G7 has the Nvidia GTX 1660 Ti, which is an interesting choice. This is the first upgrade to the GeForce line that Nvidia has put out for, well, years and uses the new Turing architecture. The card is up to the task of high performance graphics from 97% of the games I've played, including Shadow of the Tomb Raider. What it is NOT is a future-proof graphics card...and specifically, it does NOT handle 4k well if at all, nor does is allow for ray tracing (outside of DirectX via a driver update). Whether ray tracing is going to be a thing or not (I only know of two games that use it...Battlefield V and Metro Exodus) is something the user has to decide and whether to insist on the Nvidia RTX series. Sadly for the FusionTech G series and unlike the Advance, the graphics card is soldered in there so any upgrade is going to hinge on your comfort in performing surgery on the laptop. And this is the first part in my opinion that this is a good Right Now gaming laptop...there is NOTHING wrong with the GTX for the current crop of games, but if in a year or two we start seeing developers embrace ray tracing or other highly advanced rendering techniques, the GTX will be out of its depth, and with this laptop an upgrade will not be easy. Video memory is sufficient for high settings on the games I've tried, but more system RAM would help my comfort level. Last point - since you're pretty well kept to a sub 4k resolution ceiling, little surprise you can get most if not all games running well at high settings with this hardware. But to keep hammering the theme, if not having 4k isn't a dealbreaker, this is a good rig.

Keyboard: Weak. Keys are flat and small and while there's a nice generous palmrest, the keypad is a bit too close to the rest of the keyboard which makes general typing somewhat uncomfortable. There's room in the case to spread the keyboard out a bit more, so I'm a bit frustrated. The trackpad is shifted a bit to the left, but in a gaming laptop that's to be expected. Key travel is very short and while I get tactile feedback when the key is pressed (again, expected for a gaming keyboard) it's not what I call a very easy to live with design. It's adequate for general gaming, but for the real deal again I recommend an external purpose-built gaming keyboard. The built-in keyboard does have backlit keys that can be changed with the included Advance FX application, so you can change the color. My big nit there is you can only change regions of the keyboard (left, center, right) and not individual keys. I like having the WASD keys be a different color than the rest of the keyboard, and I cannot do that with this laptop. I also use an Advance gaming mouse and the FX application on the G7 will not recognize the mouse to change the colors there.

Sound: Two speakers in the front. They are on the small side and do deliver decent response, but because of their size you aren't going to get much if any bass off of them. They do about as well as they can do given the form factor, but again for Real Deal Gaming I'm more likely to use a headset instead of relying on the on board speakers anyway. Call this a good feature, good speakers, but not something that's going to take the place of a proper sound system.

Battery: It's a gaming laptop. Battery life is not a selling point. With a power-hoarding profile (performance cut down as much as possible, Intel graphics instead of the Nvidia card, etc) I got about 5-6 hours off it it with regular use. Pumping all performance to maximum and using the Nvidia card, I got 90 minutes. Given the dimensions of the case and the use of a 4 cell battery, the constraints keep it from going higher. A six-cell battery is available in this model, but you sacrifice the SATA bay if you want it. My take: I don't use battery much if at all for gaming, and if I'm doing real world work I have a power profile set up to get me my 5-6 hours. I like having the second drive more than a six-cell battery.

Performance: It ships with Windows 10 Home, which is fine BUT in true FusionTech fashion (and very unlike Advance) there's a buttload of bloatware on this thing. I took about an hour after initial setup to uninstall all of it. This is even more important because the unit I received shipped with a 512 GB SSD, and with the games I play I can use up that space pretty darned quickly. This unit DOES have the ability to accept a second internal SATA drive, which I used for a 2 TB SSD (installation was quite easy...not as easy as the Advance, but not a PITA either...). SATA is a little on the slow side for data-intensive gaming, though a SATA SSD seems to minimize the bottleneck. Not the most elegant solution (I'd prefer a PCIe 1 TB SSD as the primary instead of a 512GB, or better yet have 2 M.2 ports!!!!) but this isn't an Advance where I have a ton of choices for expandability. Another note - if you're going to put a spinny SATA drive in here instead of a SSD, you have a choice of using the M.2 port for Intel Optaine *OR* a SSD drive. Again, this speaks to the low expandability options of the G series in general.

Anyway, with my Tomb Raider game hitting about 70-72 FPS at highest (for the hardware) settings (use the Nvidia experience app to really dial in the video settings....and thank me later) it's easy to overlook a lot of my nits. Play was solid, the system architecture with the Core I7 (six cores) along with the Nvidia card did not create any unusual bottlenecks, and aside from the heat issue I was very happy with the gaming. The screen keeps the bezel to a minimum (though the top bezel is still a bit thick...) which is appreciated.

So overall - it's a good laptop well able to play pretty much anything out there today and do it well. BUT, it's not very expandable. Two memory slots, taking off the bottom to add/change components is a bit of a pain compared to the Advance, and there's not a lot you can do to add to it anyway. Add/upgrade a SATA drive or the PCIe SSD, increase RAM...and that's really about it. It's at its core an off-the-shelf easy gaming laptop that, aside from removing the bloatware, doesn't require a lot of extra effort to get it running decently. If you like tinkering and working to coax every last bit of performance out of a computer, you will be very frustrated here. If on the other hand you want a good turnkey gaming-focused laptop that doesn't stutter when running graphically- or processor-intensive games, this one fills that niche quite well.

text:
I picked up this laptop to run a CAD program and be able to occasionally work someplace besides just being chained to my desk/ desktop computer.

Overall I have been very satisfied with the laptop! The display is clear and bright, and it doesn't lag or crash as a previous laptop did when running this intensive program and doing ram-heavy tasks. (I do landscaping and so there are a lot of complicated figures and layers of photos used in my CAD program).

The only issue I have noticed is that when I am really using it heavily for the more intensive tasks, the battery drains faster than it is being replenished by the plug, which seems a really big oversight on a laptop.

It hasn't been a huge issue for me because by the time I need to let it rest and recharge, I also usually need a rest and recharge, but if I had a different work life or if my recreation was also computer-intensive, I could see that being a fatal flaw.

Beyond that, the feel and presentation of the laptop is super nice. Everything's comfortable to use and works smoothly.

title_x: Very solid machine that can replace your desktop.
text:
There is a lot to like here from FusionTech. This laptop isn't inexpensive but it really shouldn't be. You get a really solid component spec sheet here. A powerful newest I7 processor, the newest (and highly sought after) Nvidia 3050 graphics card, 16gb of RAM, a 1tb solid state hard drive, an infrared facial recognition camera, a power button fingerprint scanner, and more. All of this is attached to a big 17" FHD screen. This screen is worth noting here as it isn't the best screen you can get from FusionTech on this laptop but it is a bright (500 nit) vibrant screen with tiny bezels. The trade off here is you get almost double the battery life at just over 9.5 hours of use. That is perfect for me and I don't miss the extra pixels. It is also worth noting that you don't have a touch screen here. Again, I don't mind that as I hate the fingerprints, but some might miss it. I have been using this for work for two weeks now. This laptop is fast. Really fast! It is able to handle robust graphics. All really good. It really is a joy to use. For me, there are a couple of things that stand out for me. First, this laptop knows when you open it so it is booting up as you do so. Combined with facial recognition, I am usually working almost as soon as I can get it open. Love this! I also love the build quality here. It is a real pleasure to work with. The carbon fiber platform is great and houses a really big touch pad. The keyboard build quality is also outstanding. All of this is housed in a full aluminum chassis. As I said, it is expensive but it earns the price tag. Lastly, while this is a 17" laptop, by slimming the bezels down, this laptop is actually the same size or smaller than a good percentage of 15.4" laptops on the market. I included a picture with my wife's 15.4" HP laying on top of it. FusionTech has been very efficient with their use of space here.

While great, this isn't perfect, and at $2,000, I feel like it should be or close. I love the inclusion of four high speed Thunderbolt ports. The laptop can charge through any of them and transfers are really fast. That said, there are exactly zero traditional USB-A ports or any other port for that matter. They do include a dongle to convert but still this seems like an oversight to me. I actually use the function keys for work. If you need to here, you will need to hit a function key to use them. Not a deal breaker but not convenient. In spite of it's slimmed down size, this laptop is also quite heavy. My work backpack isn't happy with me since this acquisition. Battery life is okay here for me but, even with the less impressive screen, you will need to have a battery back up handy for travel.

FusionTech has made a heck of a laptop here overall. It can handle gaming and probably almost anything you can throw at it for work. The speakers here are good (not groundbreaking but solid) and the web cam really makes a Zoom meeting look good. I am still working on Windows 11 but it is here. For $2,000, you are paying a premium but you are getting a premium experience in almost every way.

Well done FusionTech.

title_x: Pricey for a productivity-based laptop. Also, NOT a touchscreen.
text:
Keep in mind that if you want a battery efficient laptop, one with an AMD 5000 series or an Intel 12th gen CPU will be best. I can't really justify this laptop's price margin with regards to the specs sheet. An Intel 11800h isn't the fastest laptop CPU, but it's still pretty fast for most people's use-cases.

For gaming, I would NOT recommend this laptop unless you're fine with 60hz and the graphical performance of a mobile Nvidia GTX 16 GPU w/ ray-tracing and DLSS. This can technically double as both a gaming laptop and a productivity machine, but it's mainly the latter. If you want one that's geared towards gaming, you could find one for much cheaper and with better specs. To put it into perspective, I bought a Lenovo Legion 5 Pro for $1400, and it had an AMD Ryzen 7 5800H processor (which is about equivalent to Intel's 11th gen mobile processor), a 140w Nvidia RTX 3070 mobile GPU, and a 165hz 1440p IPS display w/ HDR 400.

The display panel on the FusionTech ABC is definitely IPS. I could initially tell just from the viewing angles as there was little to no color shifting when I moved the screen around. This makes it decent for light photo or video editing as the color accuracy on IPS displays is phenomenal. The contrast isn't too bad, but it's not the best. It does not have HDR, which is pretty disappointing given the price point. The webcam quality is awful, but at least you get Windows Hello facial recognition.

The power button doubles as a fingerprint reader, but I personally don't like the location of it being in the upper right corner of the keyboard. I would have greatly preferred the power button being outside of the keyboard. However, I really liked the huge trackpad since it's a lot more ergonomic than most other laptops. The material quality feels very premium. The chassis appears to be brushed aluminum while the interior is carbon fiber.

I'd also like to mention that I was expecting this to come with a touchscreen, but that's apparently limited to the version of this laptop that has 4k resolution. Aside from that misnomer in the original product listing, I would recommend this laptop if it's within your price range. Otherwise, there are much cheaper laptops out there with similar or better performance and specs.

title_x: Do NOT use if you take online classes, easy setup, nice size
text:
I like to stay versed in PC, plus I don’t want to take my crazy expensive MacBook Pro to school and risk it getting stolen or dropped. I’m taking the price difference into account for the review, as expecting a $825~ to perform or look like a $3,500 one would be unreasonable.

Here are some details on how this computer performed:

Once set up, I like to test computers with nothing on them to see how they do in a best case scenario where the hard drive isn’t loaded with a lot of files, videos, music, pics, etc.

Setup was fast and easy, and the option to have a semi touchless setup with Cortana was very cool.

The size is great, making this work as a desktop or laptop, and for its luxurious screen size, it weighs very little and is quite streamlined, taking up as much width as a medium sized notebook. Screen resolution is ok. It’s not a retina or high definition screen, by any means, nor is it great for reading small text, but for everything else, it works fine!

The issue is speed. I compared watching a simple video online with this computer versus my iPhone X on the same network, and it took this computer Massively more time. The same video took a few seconds to be able to fully play seamlessly on my phone and literally over 2 minutes on the PC on the same WiFi network with stops for buffering. I had to sit and wait or it would play a little then buffer and stop repeatedly. No good!

I take online classes, and since I saw how slowly this was performing, I opted to only try timed quizzes and items when at home with my laptop on standby. Glad I did. I tried to start a timed quiz, and it wasn’t loading, but the problem is that it opened the page, initiating the quiz. I watched with anxiety as the buttons sloooooowly appeared without text. Since I’d never had to refresh the page for one of these in the years I’ve done online classes, I wasn’t sure what would happen, but I had no choice. I refreshed...and waited again...and the timer started, but there was no text. I am so grateful it let me pick up from my Mac, because after minutes of failed attempts on the PC, it loaded effortlessly on my 5-year-old Mac. What’s more, this dinosaur of a computer is almost full of videos and music and files (I’m in entertainment, so the MacBook Pro is a necessity more than a luxury). The 1 terabyte hard drive has a handful of gigs, maybe 30-50, and yet it had no problem loading this page.

So yeah. I don’t trust this computer. title_x: Very nice laptop for the price
text:
Design wise, the FusionTech Worktop 1500 laptop resembles the MacBook Pro with its silver case, lighted keyboard, and large touch pad. The Worktop comes with 8th generation Intel i-7 processor, which handles tasks very well. The laptop comes with 8gb of DDDR 4 memory which works well for every day tasks. This particular model comes with 128GB SSD drive and a 1TB hard drive. With plenty of space and great speed on the SSD drive, applications open up and responds very quickly. Graphics are handled by Nvidia MX250 with 2GB GDDR 5 memory.

The screen is a 15.6 inch IPS running at 1920 x 1080. The screen has a matte finish, which I like very much. There are no glare issues and the screen looks crisp with text easy to read and colors look good. The screen is not a touch screen. I like the screen on this laptop. Watching video is smooth and the screen looks good for watching movies. Pictures look good, clear, and with good color. For a laptop at this price point, all aspects of video are good for my use.

The laptop is 6.5 lbs so it is not the lightest laptop for travel but works well for home and occasional travel. For ports and slots the laptop comes with a SR card reader, 1 USB 2.0 port, 2 USB 3.1 ports, 1 ethernet port, HDM1 1.4b port, and headphone and microphone jack. Overall the case feels solid but at this price point the plastic case is not on the high-end but is very adequate and I don't expect any issues with casual use.

The laptop comes with Windows 10 Home edition. The laptop handles Windows very well with quick bootup time, good response to opening applications, and multi-tasking. FusionTech includes their Mobile connect software for linking your iOS or Android mobile devices to the laptop. Mobile connect allows you to make call and send/receive texts from your pc. It does require you to download a FusionTech app on your mobile device and to keep it running. So while it is a nice little add-on, it may not be what you are looking for in mobile integration based on having to run something from your phone for it to work.

Overall, for the price this is a nice laptop. With an i-7 8th generation processor and a dedicated Nvidia graphics card, the laptop is very responsive and handles things well. The screen is great for everyday use and provides no glare when using outdoors. The keyboard is responsive and feels good when typing. The touch pad is a nice size but can be a bit sensitive at times. I recommend this laptop based on its processor, graphics handling, screen, and overall responsiveness with Windows and applications.

title_x: Powerful & Fast i7 Processor, Look & Feel of a High-End Computer
text:
I've used my share of laptops in my life. There are several in the house, not to mention the ones I've had for work. I know a quality laptop when I work on one, and this FusionTech is a winner--speed, quality, and feel of a premium computer at a price that won't break the bank.

Let's start with setup. This computer comes in a brown, nondescript box--nothing fancy, but it serves the purpose. What you get inside the box is basically the laptop, two tiny leaflets (who needs a manual anyway?!?), and a power pack to plug into the wall and the computer. That's it. What else do you need? Nothing. Setup is what you expect, and more. It's simple, and it's even simpler with the Cortana personal assistant giving and receiving voice commands through the process. Lickety split, this laptop was fully operational. Along the way, I was prompted to log in to my home network and into my Microsoft account, which already existed from other personal computing.

The feel of this computer is wonderful. The low-profile, quiet keys are very premium--like those you'd expect on a Mac. They are flawless, and the feel is crisp and precise. The large wrist rest areas on each side of the touchpad are comfortable as I type. The touchpad is large, but not obtrusive--I didn't find myself accidentally hitting it. In addition to the lower left and right click on the touchpad, you can, of course, perform such functions as two-fingered scrolling easily and selecting with taps on the touchpad. It's precise and premium, just like the rest of the computer.

The screen is beautiful with a matte finish--no built-in glare like those that come with a shiny screen mysteriously. It's not a huge screen, but it's a laptop. This is a standard-size screen for a laptop--neither big nor tiny.

As for preloaded software, I am not a fan of McAfee antivirus. I quickly replaced that with a free download of Avast, my personal favorite. Nicely, the Chrome browser was already installed, since I cannot stand Microsoft browsers and the Microsoft Edge browser is also preloaded.

I'll admit that I didn't do anything too taxing to test out the processor, but an i7 processor is a powerhouse--the same processor used in gaming laptops, which this is not. I have no concerns about the processor here. It's super luxe.

Complaining isn't my specialty, but if you twisted my arm to complain here, I'd say they should have put the speakers on the top side of the laptop or on the screen, not the underside of the laptop, where the sound will be somewhat muted by the desk, your lap, or whatever you happen to sit the computer on. Other than this minor detail, I'd say the computer is pretty much flawless.

I'm a fan of the computer, and I'd recommend it to anybody looking for a high-end computer at a great price.

text:
I have had this FusionTech ABC 9500 for six months and it's a disaster.

This is my third or fourth FusionTech laptop and both this one and its predecessor (a FusionTech Sharp) have BIG problems. The biggest problem is that the battery swells. As you can see in the photos, as the battery swells, the touch pad starts to lift up and you can no longer click on it. Eventually the whole front of the case separates so you can no longer properly close the computer. More importantly, this is extremely dangerous because if the pouch of a lithium ion battery ruptures it will likely result in an explosion. This is totally unacceptable and never happened in the other brands of laptops I used over the years.

Second, with the FusionTech ABC 9500 I have had frequent problems with the screen going mostly black, and I have to push down on the screen or wiggle it to get the screen to come back up. A FusionTech service person said they fixed it by updating my drivers but the nature of the problem (and the fact that wiggling the monitor makes it come back to life) makes me think this probably isn't a driver problem. Only time will tell (I just had the drivers updated a few days ago).

Third, the headphone jack doesn't work. It only had hissing and static, and then I had an in-home FusionTech service call and they replaced the bottom of the computer and now there is no sound from the headphone jack at all. On top of that, the person lost three of the screws from the bottom of the computer and only screwed in one of the other five about halfway.

Last but not least, this computer was chosen for me by my employer and when it arrived I discovered it only had USB-C ports -- no regular USB ports. Since all of my peripherals are USB (microphone, mouse, tablet, ring light, MIDI keyboard), I have to use an adapter dongle for absolutely everything, and the dongle won't power the MIDI keyboard. It's beyond frustrating.

All in all, this computer has been way too much trouble and I'm going to try to have my employer return it and I will avoid FusionTechs until there is some evidence they have solved their quality control problems.
