text:
This laptop is fantastic, and overall I am very satisfied with this purchase. But let's talk about the elephant in the room that a few reviewers have already pointed out: "Is this a new product?". Given the $2000 price tag, it's only natural to be concerned about the integrity of the product you are receiving. I understand that entirely as I was very concerned myself.

For me, the laptop itself was inside its original packaging and showed no signs of being opened before. With that said, the box was a little banged up upon arrival. The laptop itself was wrapped around plastic, and everything inside seemed in place.

Now, there is a shipping label on the original packaging box from "FusionTech Returns" located in Lebanon, Tennessee. So I did some quick investigating. I read that most returns for FusionTech products will get shipped to this Return Center in Lebanon, Tennessee. These returns include order cancellations and unopened returns. FusionTech Outlet, in turn, sells these "new unused" products at a cheaper price tag. So yes, I believe this product is "NEW", but it is new under the FusionTech Outlet standards. This is just my assumption but is the most logical reason I can think of.

For me, I have no problem receiving a FusionTech Outlet product, but it should at least be advertised as such on Amazon. Now, considering all of these factors and even if this is a FusionTech Outlet product, getting a FusionTech ABC 15 (2020 model) at this price (~$2000) is a STEAL! You are getting FusionTech's UHD+ touchscreen infinity display, latest i7 CPU, 1 TB of SSD storage, and Windows 10 Pro. If you were buying this same laptop configuration off of FusionTech's official website, it run you close to ~$2500. On top of the cheaper price tag on Amazon, there is a 10% back for customers who purchase this laptop on a Amazon Prime Visa card (~$200 back).

The laptop itself has solid specs and is built very solidly. The aluminum casing and carbon fiber finish gives this laptop a premium feel. The display is gorgeous and crisp. The touchscreen is super responsive. The track pad is honestly the best I have experienced on any Windows laptop. I personally have NOT had the wobbly track pad issue some users were having.

Some issues I do have with the laptop is that it does heat up quite a bit, and you can hear the fans spinning pretty hard at times. FusionTech has a weird adaptive brightness feature, but you can easily turn this off in the settings. Battery life is less than impressive when you are doing more intensive tasks. I hear the pre-installed McAfee software plays a role in draining the battery, so you could disable it and use the built-in Windows Defender. And while I love the carbon fiber finish (because it gives it an even more premium feel), it is definitely a fingerprint magnet lol.

All in all, this laptop is absolutely stunning. The amount of features you receive for the price that you buy this laptop at outweighs the minor issues that I have pointed out.

title_x: Terrible trackpad, battery life, and temperature control
text:
As others have mentioned, the trackpad is atrocious and this computer has some serious temperature control issues. I actually bought this computer specifically for its large trackpad. Having used various MacBooks as my personal computer for the last decade plus, I’ve gotten very used to never carrying around a mouse and keyboard with me, due to the MacBook’s fantastic trackpad. So, when I was told I’d need a Windows laptop for work, I chose this one specifically for its large trackpad. Unfortunately, the trackpad is completely unusable. Unlike others, mine actually has no wobble to it, but it is incredibly erratic and inconsistent in response. The mouse hiccups and stutters all over the place when using the trackpad, whereas it’s super smooth when using a mouse. Luckily, I use a dock with mouse and keyboard most of the time when I’m in my office at work.

Hilariously, the FusionTech dock I purchased with it doesn’t actually work correctly, as I get a warning every single time the computer boots up telling me the dock it’s plugged into is not to correct spec to provide full power and functionality, despite it being the dock FusionTech sells for this very computer (the highest watt one). It works fine, honestly, but I get hit with the error constantly because this computer is ALWAYS shutting down due to low battery power overnight, despite putting it into hibernate (not sleep) mode every night before I put it in my bag. The battery life in general is not great, but the fact that neither sleep nor hibernate mode will prevent it from dying overnight is unacceptable.

Perhaps worst of all, for most people anyway, this thing has really serious temperature control problems. It frequently sounds like a jet engine (PS4 Pro owners will know the sound well) while performing pretty simple tasks (like using Microsoft Office apps or browsing the web) and more intensive tasks require messing around with the power and fan settings to avoid the computer suddenly going black from overheating, something I experienced many times when I tried to play Civ 6 on it.

I truly cannot believe that this laptop costs what it does and has the reviews it does, because it is borderline unusable for many applications. Unfortunately, I cannot afford to be without a work computer for long enough to have it looked at, so I’m stuck with this thing until it drives me crazy enough to buy something else.

Two stars (instead of just one) simply because it does have a really nice screen.

I received my laptop on 10/1. But I was too nervous about opening the package after having read several negative reviews about the trackpad. Finally, I opened the box a few days later because I was curious to see what I had bought.

Like in several other reports, the first thing I noticed was the FusionTech returns label. So that was the first red flag. And just for that, I was ready to seal the box and send it back. But then I decided to check out the trackpad. If it turned out to be okay, then I would keep the machine.

After powering on the laptop, I tested the trackpad in every way possible by pressing and clicking. I wanted to know if I would get the wobble or rattle effect that others have experienced. I didn't. But as I tested out the trackpad, I noticed something else--the erratic cursor movement.

No matter how hard I tried moving the cursor, it had a mind of its own. It would not go in the directions I wanted. So I quickly Googled and found that it was also another issue others have reported. One even mentioned FusionTech sending a technician to replace the trackpad.

I don't have an issue buying a "refurbished" laptop, given that the seller had stated in the descriptions clearly. But FusionTech wasn't willing to do that, of course. They needed to rid as many of the problematic units as possible. I knew the price was too low to be true. I had even compared it with the same configuration on FusionTech's website.

Too bad. The laptop even got the thumbs up from many YouTube reviewers as one of the top-notch video editing computers. I didn't have the time to look for other potential flaws. So I packaged it the same day and sent it back.

I finally received my refund nearly three weeks later. Not sure why it took that long to process. I vaguely remember someone else mentioning the slow refund as well.

FusionTech has lost my confidence in buying their laptops online. So off to the other reputable sellers I go!

I can't recommend this laptop at all. It should be usable past the two-year mark.

I've bought my last FusionTech.

text:
Personally, I love it so far. I am primarily using it as a 'desktop'. I have it hooked up to a large monitor and a USB 3.0 universal docking station, so I can use a mouse, KB, and printer easily.

I also slapped 8 more gigs of RAM into it (can't go wrong with that; it's just another 30-35 bucks).

I did have some issues with Windows 10 at the start. Some of my old software (PS CS2, a few games, etc.) required tweaking to work properly. But, all that stuff was running on my outdated desktop with Windows Vista. I am still having issues with Netflix for some reason, but I think that's also Windows, not the PC itself.

For gaming, I do have to lower the screen resolution to 1920x1080. Not a problem. But I do run photoshop in 4k, which is awesome. I don't do anything more intense than large file image editing and some gaming, so everything seems tight and fast for me. I could see a user having difficulties with 4k video editing, 4k 3D modeling, and running games like Witcher 3 on high/ultra. I don't think this machine could handle that.

My only complaint is the 8gb SSD built into the 1TB HD is pretty useless. Why is it even there? It also got in my way...For some reason, when transferring my image files over to this machine (I make big pictures, the unflattened .psd files are ~300-700 MB.) the SSD defaulted as the save drive, and I quickly filled it, thus getting "not enough memory" messages. That was annoying.

I haven't used the touch screen, or the touch pad...So I cannot comment on their quality or usefulness. I can say Win10 took some getting used to. I use 7 at work, and I was using Vista with no problems at all for years. But, I like it now. For the most part.

But for my purposes (and a desperately needed upgrade from a circa 2007 desktop) this machine rocks.

FusionTech's customer service is notoriously bad and it's more of a headache than anything. I would have given this laptop 5 stars but for these reasons I can only give it 3, and that's being generous. Still, it's not a bad laptop, it just has problems that are very annoying.

UPDATE--Last month (September 2018) my left hinge got to the point where it was literally drooping down and the plastic covering the red vents started breaking off. It turns out that the only thing holding up the massive screen is a tiny little screw that randomly comes loose and causes the left hinge to loosen up as well. Fixing this requires you to open the back and tighten it again. But the screws are so tiny and cheap that they always loosen again and cause more damage to the frame every time the hinge droops. I'm at the point now where I have to replace it all together because it's falling apart now. A lot of other people have this issue with this particular model, too!

This is a case of bad design--period. A frame that is made of cheap plastic that breaks off easier than split ends with a big, heavy screen that is held together by two little screws is a bad idea. I say this as an industrial design student with a basic understanding of physics and mechanical engineering.

It's a shame because we paid good money for these and expect them to work and function normally long after 5-12 months. I do not recommend that anyone buys this. It's a piece of garbage that overheats, will start to fall apart months after you get it and has a battery that only holds a charge for 2 hours tops. There are better options out there with a better track record than this model.

title_x: A powerful machine fraught with really stupid design problems.
text:
I've owned this laptop for one year now. I bought it from Microsoft Store, not Amazon, but it's the exact same model. Although the CPU power is great, and video card nice for a laptop, there are issues. Specifically 3 issues I'm frustrated with.

(1) First, I almost immediately started having the "hinge issue" you see many people having with this laptop -- look for the reviews with pics. The right hinge is ok, but the left hinge became loose within the first month; and I don't open/close it every day... but only maybe two or three times a month since I leave it with the lid open for 98% of the time. In other words, the laptop left the factory floor (I'm guessing) with a loose left hinge. Anyway, yes, it's separating the lower-half from the upper-half of the laptop body (not the screen, but the rest of the laptop) just like you see demonstrated in the other photos in these reviews. I really don't want to deal with sending it in and being without my laptop for 3-4 weeks, even though I purchased a 3 year warranty... so I live with the problem.

(2) The trackpad/touchpad SUCKS! Wow! I've owned a lot of laptops in my 25+ years of computing. (My first laptop was a IBM Thinkpad in 1991.) I'm baffled as to how a team of engineers could make such a terrible and hard to use trackpad. Why? Because they got rid of the buttons as being separate items; and now they're just the "lower portion" of the entire single surface touchpad. This causes two problems: (a) you can't feel them to use them naturally without looking and so often (unless you're in the very very lower left-hand or very very lower right-hand corner) you'll click one button, and the touchpad will think you're clicking the other button! Then, and possibly worse, (b) THEY ALSO ACTIVELY WORK AS PART OF THE TOUCHPAD SO THEY MOVE YOUR ONSCREEN POINTER WHEN YOU CLICK THEM! Half the time when you try clicking an onscreen button, as you depress the physical touchpad "button", your onscreen pointer jumps off the onscreen link or button you're trying to click. Truly insane! I just want to smash the damn thing. Bottom line... it takes two hands to use the touchpad--one on the physical trackpad button (ready to click) and the other moving the pointer on screen. The solution: you just always end up using a wireless mouse instead.

I've gone through (meaning they short out and break near the end that plugs into the laptop) two connectors in slightly less than one year. In fact, that's why I'm on Amazon now... I'm looking to buy a 3rd one. The original, and the replacement, were both genuine OEM FusionTech transformer power supply. And although the pretty blue light on the end of the cord is nice because you can visually see that the power adapter is plugged in, the problem is that the plug going into the computer is long and stiff, meaning that it's incredibly susceptible to leverage and as such is prone to stress and breakage. Bad design. A very short "L-shaped" plug holds up so much better. My last laptop has the L-shaped type and has (so far) lasted well over 6 years; that's ONE power adapter with exactly the same weekly usage as this FusionTech! But with this FusionTech, I've burned through 2 already in my first year! What a piece of junk this FusionTech connector is.
Furthermore, they're EXPENSIVE, at over $50 each! And you can't just change out the end cord coming from the transformer to your laptop like some transformers do. No! They've engineered it so that the cord is hardwired into the expensive transformer unit! Why? Well of course to get more money from you. Hey, at this rate, if I keep this laptop for 6 years, at 2 transformers per year, that's 12 power supply units at $50/each = an extra $600 ! Good business FusionTech!

To heck with you FusionTech. I used to recommend you, and have owned a hundred FusionTechs in my company over the years. I'm done with FusionTech.

Edit 3: 2020 the laptop cannot be moved--it stops and must reboot. The monitor cannot be opened or closed due to split on the side. The speakers went out. The machine still runs hot. My three other FusionTechs were fine. This model is a very expensive lemon.

Back in 2017, the seller sent the laptop on time in well protected packaging. The seller kept up their end of the purchase with a 30 day warranty. The screen was large, colors were bright and touch screen was a nice option.

TECH COMMENTS: However, cracks quickly began to show when running programs: the discrete graphics (bear in mind that these are far weaker than their desktop counterparts) aren't powerful enough to run any remotely intensive programs, and that's saying nothing of Intel's poor integrated graphics. This means that the computer will rarely use all 4 of its individually low-speed cores. As an added bonus, none of this is remotely powerful enough to run typical 4k programs (though if you're streaming content, it's acceptable).

Aside from issues with technical specifications, the product worked without incident through the sellers warranty period. However, 5 months later, the laptop shell split at the seam in the left rear corner near the hinge. FusionTech said the problem is not covered under their warranty. After a little searching online, there are others who report similar manufacturing flaws with this 7559 model. I've owned two FusionTechs and never had this sort of problem. I wish I had known this was a common flaw with the 7559 model; I would have purchased a different model. I knew some users said it ran hot and that there were sound issues; I didn't know it might split apart at the seams.

title_x: So far it seems a bit mediocre due to relatively low performance, terrible touchpad design*, and short battery life when gaming
text:
I've had it for a couple of weeks and admittedly haven't been using it too much since I usually sit at my desktop. However, I do have some complaints that keep bugging me:

it seems a bit underpowered when I'm playing Overwatch (the only game I play). I know that expecting a laptop to run a game at 4k at 60fps is unfair, so I reduced it to 1080p settings (1920x1080 specifically), and the game had screen tearing. I was surprised to see that coming from a 960, even if it IS the mobile version. So I lowered some of the graphics settings, and still... screen tearing. Even with VSync on (and a huge FPS hit), I still get tearing unless I reduce it to like 48 FPS. I feel like a $1000 computer should be able to handle overwatch on 1080 when on high (not even EPIC settings) without tearing.

the battery also seems to die a little too quickly to me. Perhaps I'm spoiled because my last laptop was the Qosmio x505 and was originally twice the price of this laptop when it first came out (I bought it for about a 70% discount because it was a display model), but I feel like since they're both i7s (albeit first or second generation vs like 6th generation), they should both have comparable battery lives. I believe I could get about an hour and a half of gaming on my old 18 inch laptop [1080p max] that sported a comparable 460 gtx m GPU. However, I think I made it through two rounds of Overwatch on 1080p before I had to connect my charger (so about 30-40 minutes, I believe?). It could be that the 4k screen is super power hungry even in 1080 mode, but I feel like the battery is a little too weak. Although to give credit to the FusionTech, it's also a much thinner and lighter laptop than my super heavy Qosmio, so it likely has a physically smaller battery to conform to the rest of the laptop's form factor. Regardless, chances are that if I'm gaming, I'll be sitting near a power outlet anyway, so I just need to run a few tests for regular usage of the laptop - where I take notes and surf the internet, but not turn on any intensive games. If it lasts ~3 hours doing that, I will be a happy camper with the battery aspect.

The other problem is a really huge one to me. I am used to non-apple touchpads where you have a touchpad and then two physical buttons underneath where you can right click and left click. As such, my right hand's thumb normally rests on the left click button and the rest of the hand hovers a centimeter over the touchpad and the index finger comes down whenever I need to move around on the touch pad. Unfortunately, the touchpad on this laptop is just a single giant one that allows the whole touchpad to be treated as a giant clickable left click button (aside for the bottom right corner). The problem is that my thumb and index finger will both register movement, so the mouse is difficult to control at times. I understand the logical answer is "well then don't rest your thumb on the touch pad and adopt to the apple style of touchpads!", but the thing is... I've been using this style for about 20 years so it's kind of ingrained. I'm all for keeping up with the times, but plenty of touchpads are still designed with two physical buttons. I was hoping they'd offer a simple software fix where the bottom 15% of the touchpad can be set to ignore movement that doesn't originate from somewhere in the rest of the touch pad. That way, I can leave my thumb there without it picking up any movement, while still being able to click (since clicks don't count as movement). I found out this very solution does exist for synaptics brand touchpads, but I cannot for the life of me narrow down what model touchpad this laptop uses, and it seems very likely that it's not synaptics. This issue is pretty annoying to me since I actually prefer to play some games using the touchpad instead of a mouse (somewhat of a humblebrag, but I managed to get myself to the top 1% in Awesomenauts using my previous laptop and used the touchpad exclusively... and stayed in the top 5% consistently. So I was VERY comfortable with touchpads). Unfortunately at the moment my only solution is to make sure I have a mouse with me when I decide to go gaming, and this is a hassle at times when I'm at school and was thinking "I'm not going to do any gaming today", but then find myself with like an hour free between classes and am like "Damn, I wish I had disconnected my mouse from my desktop and taken it with me!".

Aside for these complaints, it isn't a terrible computer. It has a pretty screen. The touch screen feature is neat, though I don't really use it. It doesn't seem to get obscenely hot when being used for things other than gaming. The keyboard feels good. It's small, and the lack of a blu ray drive is actually somewhat of a plus, since it makes it smaller and look nicer (you can buy an external Blu Ray burner for like $100 now I think, assuming moore's law has been keeping up since I last looked at drives like 3 years ago; actually, just confirmed, I see some for $80. Neat). And it has the ability to play any game you throw at it, even if it doesn't seem to be able to run them at full power (this complaint might actually have to do with me not playing with the bios and putting it in super performance mode or something, now that I think about it).

So for now, due to the uncomfortable touchpad and the bad battery life and the suboptimal game performance, I'll give it an above average 3 star rating, but I feel like I might have been better off buying a non-4k laptop for like $800 that had better processing power and better battery. I will definitely change it to a 4 or 5 if I find a way to fix the touchpad issue via software (if anyone could tell me what brand the touchpad is, that would help immensely with finding a solution; or even finding a universal program that can deadzone the bottom 15% of the touchpad), figure out why the battery seems to drain so quickly compared to my previous gaming laptop, and figure out why the screen tends to tear so much when playing on 1080p, even with vsync on - and how to fix it.

title_x: So far so good. Nice computer
text: So far so good. Nice computer. Love the picture quality, and plenty fast from what I've seen so far. Like a lot of the others, I also added the extra stick of ram and SSD. They really did make it easy to add the extra hardware. The Samsung migration software was also pretty quick and smooth, save for a couple minor issues. Some of the articles I read did not mention disconnecting the original drive after moving over the OS, and before booting from the new SSD. I read this was the cause of some errors. I also read that a fresh install of the OS was a better idea than to clone. In the end, I decided to try the migration software, and clone the main drive. Figured if I ran into issues, I would then reformat and do a fresh install. Here's what I did. First thing was to run all windows updates. I then created a bootable USB drive in case I needed to start fresh. After installing the SSD, install the samsung data migration software, run the program to copy the OS from the HDD to the SSD. Once it copies over, shut down the computer. Disconnect the HDD, start it up, and it should now boot from the SSD. Confirm everything works, shut it down again, reconnect the original drive, and start it again. I should note. When I did this, I noticed the original drive wasn't automatically showing up. After checking, I noticed it was due to an error/conflict with the disk volume serial number, because of this, the drive was offline. I just went to disk management, selected the drive to go online. The error then seemed to go away and I was able to read and reformat the drive. After doing this, everything seemed normal until I tried using the windows search (taskbar) function. In some instances, it would show up, but the actual function would not work. I.e. windows update wouldn't work. Tried multiple "fixes" including the command prompt SFC repair tool ( sfc / scannow ), but none seemed to work. The one fix that finally worked was to create a new ADMIN user. Once I logged in under the new user, everything seemed to work fine. I then deleted the other user account, and now everything appears to be in order. The one thing that needs improvement is the sound. There's distortion at about 90%, and it's not even close to being "loud".

text:
The reason I got this laptop is that I am a senior engineering student and was looking for a laptop that could run engineering software such as MatLAB, Solidworks, etc. When I first received this laptop from Amazon it came dead on arrival luckily enough there were still more of these models left in stock so I opted to receive a brand new one as long as I sent the broken one in within 30 days. Before contacting Amazon about the problem I spoke with FusionTech tech support and I have to say that they have some of the best customer service I have ever come across. This was a very nice surprise. Once I received a working model ( which took about 4 days) I was very pleased with this laptop. I see complaints about screen bleeding, but with the 4K screen on this laptop I have not seen any bleed coming from the screen at all. Another complaint I had seen about this laptop is the touch pad, and in some sense I agree, the touch pad has a gritty feeling which I don't like, however I do not see any issues with the responsiveness of the touch pad. The sound from this laptop is very loud. The last laptop I had was an HP that had Beats audio and this laptop is significantly louder, however the sound quality isn't the best. The touch screen on this laptop is a nice feature but really isn't necessary for me. So if you're like me and were thinking "Do I really need a touch screen?" most likely the answer to that will be no. With this considered the touch screen is quite accurate. I downloaded a note taking app and used it to take hand written notes using the touch screen and I was surprised how well the notes came out. Now for performance, this laptop runs Solidworks and Matlab very smoothly with fast boot up time. I can run multiple programs without seeing any dip in performance.

I compared this laptop to a few others in the same price range with similar specs, and the reason I went with this laptop is the design of it. Most laptops that are considered "gaming laptops" have a gaming look to them. This laptop looks very professional which was definitely important to me.

Overall I would say that if you're an engineering student looking for a laptop that can meet your needs through college, this laptop is a great choice.

This is an excellent laptop in true FusionTech fashion. Couple of very minor issues that I believe can be solved easily as I believe it involves Windows 10. What should be explained is that after you purchase this on Amazon you can contact FusionTech and purchase an extended service plan directly from them and extend the factory warrantee that comes with the computer. That one is a little longer than a year and is a premium service. I purchased the warrantee that was offered on Amazon, but if you have an issue you must send the computer to them and wait for its return. You do have 30 days to effect a refund, but I lost track of the time and don't know if I can now get any credit at all for that warrantee. I did, in fact, purchase the premium one directly from FusionTech. An excellent buy and does offer tech service. If you purchase their best, which is inexpensive for what it is, they will diagnose on the phone and if not solved, they provide in home or office tech service. That is the way to go.

This is a follow up to my original post above. I have been in constant touch with FusionTech Techs on a freeze up issue since this post was listed on Amazon. FusionTech Techs, from India, have been most cooperative and have accessed my computer more times than I can count. Finally they replaced my mother board on site per their warantee and the problem was not solved. They again accessed the computer on line many more times without success. Their next move was to have the computer shipped to their tech facility in Houston. They had the computer for a couple of days and sent it back supposedly repaired. Not so. Again they accessed my computer on line many more times without success. It still continued to lock up. Once again they asked it to be shipped to Houston. They kept the computer for several days, returning it with the comment "replaced logic board". Here it is 10 months later and the computer still locks up. The only difference is the addition of a new lock up. On boot up which it didn't do previously. Today, my patience is finally exhausted and I have sent an email to the Techs who are in India tell them I am through with this as I feel they at this time should replace the computer with a new one or see to it that my money is refunded. text:
This is for the i7559-7512 version. Purchased on 6/26/16 $1255

I'm mildly disappointed with this computer. We upgraded from our 3 year old Toshiba that had begun acting a bit slow. We been playing more and more PC games lately and wanted something powerful that could handle larger games. This computer seemed like the perfect option as it had all the specs of a gaming computer without the gaming computer price (it also has a touch screen with is nearly impossible to find on a gaming computer.)

Pros:
-It's handsome
-Beautiful picture
-Nice feeling keyboard - the backlit keys are a nice touch
-has lots of power (supposedly)

Cons:
-SLOW downloads
-Finicky touchpad

Issue #1 SLOW DOWNLOADS
I was expecting a lightning fast PC as this PC is much more powerful than our old one. Really, the response time isn't much better than our old one. I can't tell much of a performance difference. I haven't gotten to play anything yet because the download of games is SO SLOW. Also, the downloading of games almost makes the computer unusable as it has trouble handling two things at once.

Issue #2 FINIKY TOUCH PAD
I figured while the downloading of my game is using up all my CPU I'll do something simple that doesn't take much memory. I figured minesweeper is a fun enough game to play for an hour or so and not take up too much CPU. For those who don't know, Minesweeper requires you to use the left and right click buttons on your touch pad. Turns out that about 1 in every 6 RIGHT CLICKS registers as a LEFT CLICK making the game impossible to play.

I'm annoyed that I paid almost $1300 for a computer that doesn't seem to be performing much better than my 3 year old $600 computer.. Just bummed.

title_x: ... this laptop a week ago and have been very pleased with it in most respects
text:
I just purchased this laptop a week ago and have been very pleased with it in most respects, I had set range of Specs I wanted in my purchase and set brands I was looking for, and though I got it from Fry's this was the one laptop they had in stock that fit the bill.

The Requirements ~ NO(HP, Toshiba, ASUS) 4th or 6th gen i7 (No Broadwell), 12GB+ DDr3+, NVIDIA GTX (I usually prefer ATI but they run hot in laptops) So

So the Good: Of the 2 other Worktop laptops I have owned, the 8500 & 1545 this is by far the best feeling in respects of Quality, It feels solid, the Palm rest doesn’t feel like hollow plastic, the design is sleek, and the red accented exhaust vents give an appealing touch. The design is slim and sleek and keeps up with the current fashion of portable devices. The Bezel around the Multi-touch screen is almost non existent, while the screen hinges are firm and sturdy.

The Keyboard is what some would call "Spongy" But I take it they haven’t used an Worktop before? I have the 1545 & 7559 side by side and I honestly cant feel much of a difference between the two, regardless its responsive and large for a laptop with light up keys serving its purpose.
The touch Screen works, and if going back to Windows 8.1 As I did makes for an Awesome easy experience, Not sure why you would necessarily need it for Window's 10 and with the additional cost might not be worth it for some users.

So aside from physical features I decided to do Benchmark tests using PassMark's PerformanceTest which compares against baseline statistics and other user PC's and got a score of 4100~ (Yes that’s High) Just ensure you have the gtx 960 Selected as the designated video option and not the onboard Intel 530, the only test it seemed to Lack in was the 2D Graphics, the rest were excellent.
I also did another test in which I decided to Install Dolphin and to play Mario Sunshine & the Wii Twilight Princess, both ran flawlessly staying 60FPS occasionally dropping to 59FPS But never any lower than 99%. That in itself proves its capabilities.

So the Bad: well it was what I was worried to begin with when purchasing it but really had no other option available, and that is the 4K screen. While Windows 8+ is great at utilizing the new UHD Resolution, Legacy apps.... Well just aren’t so well off. Windows Scaling is pathetic and the only realistic solution I could find was adjusting the Resolution to 1920X1080. If you are unfamiliar with this let's just say if you use any applications outside of Windows & Microsoft Office Like adobe products, when you go to launch them on your beautiful 4K display which is 38??X???? Pixels, your copy of Photoshop is going to be a bit hard to see... and a 'bit' is quite an understatement, you will need a magnifying glass as the developers didn't design the program to "Scale" with windows but rather to their own preferred dimensions. Then when adjusting your resolution, the pixels are still physically there, you are just up scaling the entire picture to fit the umpteen millions of pixels available. This leaves a slightly blurry effect especially when it comes to in-app text.

The only other issue I have is with the Touch Pad, though its not terrible, it works, it just feels a bit "clunky" if that’s a word? at times and sometimes needs an extra click to perform the action, I also find it difficult sometimes to get the mouse centered correctly on scroll panes If they are unusually narrow and that can get frustrating but aside from that many people are using Bluetooth mouse’s anyways.

So in conclusion, I have had this for about a week and I was lurious to begin with buying an Worktop with these Specs, as it sort of feels like buying a corolla loaded to the brim with Camry features. Something I would expect in the ABC line but the Price point for the Worktop explains the build. The laptop feels solid and the hardware is now on the upper end compared to the Middle road they usually take and I think they did a fantastic job in implementing it. I am not a gamer but rather needed a better machine fore development, so I don't know what Fallout 4 looks like on this machine but I do see a massive improvement on Visual Studio 2015 & Eclipse IDE's. While the price is a bit steep for some It should go without saying you get what you pay for. I hear allot of people putting down particular brands or fan boy’s righteously defending their last purchase, Laptops with specs like these simply run in this price range, while ones boasting similar or exact specs with huge reduction in price..(just do your research first) I am not a Gamer nor do I have any interest in labeling this a s a "Gaming" Laptop, I am a user that likes to have a laptop that will last me 7~8 years and will still be relevant when that time comes, so I try to ensure my hardware will be capable in advancements in software when the time comes. To conclude I am happy with my purchase

I have yet to actually open the computer up but the system believes that it is running the "Intel HD Graphics 530" card. I have yet to try running a game on this laptop and I have yet to google this specific graphics card to see if I'm actually upset but I really chose this laptop for the specs that were described. This was my dream laptop and the news that I have the incorrect hardware after all this time has really hit me hard. Thanks for reading and I wish the best of luck for everyone else. title_x: Great Computer, but a few quirks need to be worked out.
text:
I've been using this new FusionTech computer for a couple of weeks now and for the most part I am pretty happy. The screen is amazing. Not enough can be said about the UHD 4K display and how great it looks once you get it adjusted properly. Fortunately windows 10 has the tools to do it. A lot of programs and web pages are not ready for 4K displays and the text can be hard to read. By changing the display settings to 250% everything looks great and easily readable. I'm not sure why this wasn't set correctly from the factory since windows even says that 250% is the recommended setting, but it wasn't. Windows 10 has taken a little getting use to, but the learning curve hasn't been too steep coming from Windows 7. Microsoft office applications work flawlessly. Adobe Creative Cloud products have been hit and miss so far. Premier pro works great and the Nvidia graphics card really speeds up video encoding. Adobe Light Room on the other hand has been a real pain. When reviewing photos in the catalog, the system memory fills up and the program is shut down by windows (hard shut down). A warning dialog is given, but once you click "OK" Lightroom is just shut down. Fortunately I haven't lost any work yet. After this happening a couple of times, I started keeping the Task Manager open and watching the memory usage. What I observed is that when the memory usage exceeded 10 GB the issue would occur. Keep in mind the system has 16 GB installed. I don't know if this is and Adobe problem, or a Windows problem, but I'm pretty sure it is not a FusionTech problem. Hopefully an update will resolve the issue. Speaking of updates, I have received several updates in the past 2 weeks. Some were from Windows, and 1 Bio's update from FusionTech. The build quality of the computer seems very nice and durable. Some reviewers complained about the red accents on the speaker grill and and the rubber feet, but I think it looks very nice. The computer fans are very quite most of the time and you only notice them during heavy tasks like video encoding. The vent covers on the fans are a little rough and look like they could break over time. The bottom gets warm, but not as hot as some laptops I've owned in the past. The battery life seems very good for the processing power and running a UHD display. HDMI port works well for running an external display. The touch screen is cool, but honestly I don't use it that much. I'm not a huge fan of the track pad mouse, but it seems better than others I have used in the past. 99% of the time I use a Logitech external wireless USB mouse. They are just better for accuracy and speed. The keyboard is responsive and seems durable. My biggest pet peeve so far is the magnetic sensor used to detect that the screen is closed. The issue is that if you get something magnetic too close to the palm rest (like resting something there) it will turn off the computer and put it to sleep. His is very annoying when it happens and it took me a while to figure out what was happening. At first I though I got a dud computer and was going to have to ship it back. Luckily a little detective work on Google turned up the issue and I was able to replicate and confirm it. So watch putting anything magnetic on or near the pal rest.

Pros:
Amazing Display
Great Video Card
Quiet Fan Operation
Good Battery Life

Cons:
Magnetic Lid Switch
Windows 10 / Adobe Lightroom Memory Issue
Rough Fan Covers Likely to Break Over Time

In Summary, I'm very happy I bought this laptop. It should hold up well for 2 or 3 years. Two thumbs up.

title_x: Great Laptop, Driver problems, and Scaling!
text:
Almost One year Update
I bought this Laptop last black Friday ( 2015) , I bought the i5 model with 4K touch screen, and let me tell you that the screen is the true star of the show for this laptop, my brother just bought a new Sager with 4K non touch and GTX 1070 8GB, his laptop crushes mine in every aspect, except for the solid feel and the Screen, the Screen is just amazing, brilliant colors , amazing white, deep black, and a very few bleeds on the edges ( Specially the lower corners). The downside of this laptop is the serious issue with the case getting split ( Upper part from the lower one) when someone accidentally pushes the Power Jack downward, I have kids and they keep step on the charger wire, so finally the case started to split slightly whenever I lift the lid (Open the screen), I kept tightening the screws ( easy to access, just one screw on the downside) , until the screws stopped fully tighten the case, so I used very small drops of accelerated super glue, and the problem is gone! The other issue is wit the speakers, they can be nice and loud at times, but a lot of times the music get static noise, sometimes using the laptop on a hard surface ( not on your lap) solves the issue, due to the subwoofer on the downside of the base, but it can be a real issue though sometimes. I used to get lots of crashes of the ( Intel integrated graphics driver) , but this issue got totally solved with the Win10 Anniversary Update. Finally, the battery life is not that great for the 4K Touchscreen, some users with the Full HD non touch reported up to 6 hours of battery life watching a Full HD MKv Movie, medium screen back lighting and Plane Mode activated, I couldn't get more than 3 - 3 and a half at most, still not bad for a gaming laptop One advice , if you want to buy this Laptop, buy and M2 SSD ( Non NVMe) with it right away, the included SSHD is not bad at all, just you will feel a huge difference in programs and Games loading, besides, this Laptop is really serious when it comes to easiness of adding RAM- SSD, just one screw at the under side, and you will get a full access to the Ram slot, SSHD drive bay, and the M2 SSD slot, so easy and efficient, even upgrading your wireless AC is not an issue at all, besides this ( Smart Door ) allows for easy access to clean the fans ( Which I need constantly) . Over all, this is a solid entry level Gaming Laptop, there is no Laptop in the market ( at that time) can beat it in regards to Value for Money, solving the minor issues I mentioned, adding GTX 1070 8 GB, selling it for 1400 $ will make it a real easy sell, no brainer at all, at its current condition, I think the price is fair between 750 - 800.
Changes from Last Review

- The Scaling issue ( win 10 thing) much improved, still exists in many programs though.
- The crashing ( Intel Driver) issue got fixed with the anniversary update
- The static sound issue much improved, still exists, specially with some movies when using MPCHC
- I fixed the creaking issue with some super glue ( For real, a few small drops fixed it)

Am currently typing this replay from the reviewed laptop , I bought the configuration with 4K touch screen and Core I5 , 1 TB SSHD , Matt black featuring grey finish:
For more than a month now, this Laptop proved to worth the money I paid ( 965$ from Amazon), still there are some serious problems need to be addressed:
1- the Audio has a huge driver-hardware problem, at times there is noticeable and really annoying interference sound, it is specially noticeable with high bass levels, I thought the speakers were flawed , but using my Philips headphones n this terrible sound still there!
2- Every single owner of this laptop complains from the same ( Intel HD Graphics 8 driver Has been crashed and recovered) , this happens a lot , alottt , and it can really get annoying during gaming as it suddenly makes the game unplayable ( MGS V Phantom Pain , SC2: Legacy of the Void , AoE : Casatle Siege) , so you might need to restart the PC when this happens , or disable the Intel HD graphics altogether and risk losing battery life!
3- 4K only problem : Scaling , Scaling , Oh God MS! Scaling!!!!!! please???? and not only things get really small, performance takes a huge hit, for unknown reason!
4- 4K looks amazing , and it worth every penny of the extra 170$ I paid , but I hoped for a deeper black and better contrast, still it is really bright and color are amazing.
5- Battery life is much less than expected, almost 3.40 hours on medium backlighting , no Wi-Fi ( Airplane mode), hoped for almost 6 hours, but I guess the 4K panel is to blame for the short battery life.
All in all, this a solid performing - budget gaming laptop, MGS V = 1080 P all maxed out and smooth gaming , Legacy of the void = 1440P all maxed out and smooth gaming, add an extra 265 GB M.2 for 120$ and an extra 8 GB for 30$ and you will end with a beats machine for the money,the Keyboard experience needs some time to get used to, but it is not bad at all (Coming from an amazing Lenovo Keyboard, so everything seems less than acceptable at first), touch pad is rough, it is sensitive but rough and alson needs some time , like 3 days, to get used to, but it is not bad at all, gestures work perfectly, but I have a Touch Panel, so yeah , I paid extra for it and I should use it :) , other than that, it needs some drivers attention from FusionTech to end as a real competitor for much more expensive machines.

text:
I've had my computer for about a month now and I'm still trying to fix all of it's issues. The most annoying, for me, being:

1. Serious app scaling issues- Many of the art programs that I like to use appear tiny on screen because Windows, even with their latest updates, have found a way to give all low resolution programs the ability to scale properly on a high dpi screen. I now have to either lower my screen resolution 1920x1080 to use the program or manually go into the programs themselves and create an external manifest file.

2. Stuttering speakers- The Realtek speakers will occasionally crackle and stutter. I've done various troubleshooting and driver re-installations, but nothing seems to be helping. It only happens every now and then, but, when it does, it's impossible to ignore.

3. McAfee Virus Protection- This one is not so much the laptop as it is the free virus protection software that comes with it. The program continuously flagged programs and files that I had already given permissions to. I was getting so many notifications popping up on my screen that I uninstalled the program completely by day two and switched over to Windows Defender.

Every laptop I've had in the past has been essentially perfect to use straight out of the box, but this one has me going through it almost everyday, deleting useless programs and changing settings. I don't usually write reviews, but since I didn't see any of these issues pop up in any of the other amazon reviews, I thought I should make them known.

text:
This laptop does not actually have a 4k screen. It uses the RGBW pentile instead of the standard RGB matrix to get away with having a much worse resolution while still advertising as 4k. It makes your graphics card work much harder too because it still has to render a 4k resolution, and then downsample it to the display.

I just bought this laptop from the Microsoft store yesterday, only to find out today that it uses this fake 4k technology. The screen stutters a lot, and for some reason the entire bottom left of the screen lags when playing any sort of game. Its like there is a line going diagonally across the screen where I get 1/4 the FPS.

I was excited to find such a great deal on a laptop like this, and I liked how it felt when I got it out of the box, it is nice and sturdy (except the screen, which feels like its made of soft rubber and bends anytime you touch it). The touchpad could use some work, but it is decent, and the keyboard feels okay. But when I found out it uses this fake technology, I was pretty upset. I was still going to keep it though until the issue with the whole bottom left side of the screen lagging started, now I will be taking it back to the store tomorrow and asking for a refund.

title_x: Good Laptop for the Price but Beware of the Nuances That May Irk You
text:
I'm an incoming medical student who was looking for something that had the power to be a desktop replacement. I know a reasonable amount about computers and was looking for something to run the anatomy software that I'll be using and also serve as a do-all device.

Overall (UPDATE 8/18/16)

Originally I was convinced that I'd be able to stick with this laptop and ignore the little defects, but after a few weeks I realized I could not and decided to return it. Ultimately, if you're using this for gaming purposes or need to run some kind of photo editing software then I'd still recommend it based on price, screen, and performance. As a student my biggest sticking points in deciding to return it were:

1. Keyboard - The "key depth" depth issue I originally mentioned wasn't a key depth issue - it was the keyboard itself not registering strokes no matter how hard I pushed. It became impossible to take coherent notes. I've had this problem with one other laptop before and updated my keyboard driver to fix the issue. It didn't work with this particular unit and negated one of the biggest reasons I bought it.

2. Fans Noise - This model has a 128gb SSD in addition to the 1TB HDD, was only two weeks old, and sounded like it was going to blast into outer space when I was running ONE lecture video, two other tabs, and Microsoft word. There performance was never an issue, but the noise created a distraction to those around me particularly in testing situations and became too much of a burden.

Pros
- Beautiful screen. I've seen many complain about brightness but in general the brightness has been fine for me. It would be difficult to take this out on a rooftop on a very sunny day, but I've never owned a laptop that I'm trying to use in that kind of light so I'm more than satisfied.
- Touch screen is very accurate and responsive
- Gorgeous design. I know some have complained about fingerprints but I'm yet to see anything after using this consistently for almost a week. Maybe it takes longer for it to be noticeable
- Incredibly fast and very powerful. You can stream two HD movies at once without missing a beat productivity-wise
*this became problematic when the fan began to act up and I could barely open three browser tabs without it ramping up. The performance never suffered inspite of the fan defect

Cons
- Keyboard is a little hinky. Occasionally, the stroke depth you need to register a key is problematic and I find myself leaving out letters in multiple sentences as I type which has never happened to me before
- Track pad is adequately responsive and comfortable, HOWEVER, there is an incessant "clicking" sound even when scrolling WITHOUT trying to register a click. It's light and you'd never notice it unless everything around you is quiet but when you do it's incredibly irritating
- I know it advertises the 128GB SSD and I bought this specifically because if I have it in the library or class I don't want the fans running consistently to cool down the HDD. Many similar models advertise the 1TB HDD but no SSD. Unfortunately, the fans are slightly more annoying than I had anticipated. They turn off fairly quickly but if you're looking for an extra quiet laptop then this may not be the machine for you.
- It's definitely heavier than any other laptop I've had. I think their listed weight is pretty misleading. I don't personally mind it, but it's something that I can see as an issue in the case of portability

title_x: Best laptop I could find for less than a grand.
text:
Model: i7559-7512GRY 15.6 Inch UHD Touchscreen Laptop (i7 (2.6GHz 6th Gen), 1 TB HDD, 16 GB RAM, 128 GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960M)
I've only had this for about two weeks, but I use it heavily enough to have a good feel for it. The title of the review sums it up for the impatient, but read on for more detail if you're interested.

The Good:
Wow, this laptop is blazing fast. I am coming from an I3 that's about 5 years old and there just isn't any comparison. I run very demanding programs such as MATLAB, SolidWorks, Mathematica, Visual Studio, and LabVIEW. This laptop handles them all with ease, often simultaneously.
The NVIDIA GPU with 4GB of DDR5 not only makes sure the display is keeping up, but many programs will off-load other functions to it as well. That means that you get even more processing power and RAM to chew through the toughest renderings or scientific calculations with ease.
Speaking of displays, the UHD screen is amazing! Not only is it crisp and bright, it is multi-touch capable. This was a feature that I wasn't concerned with when purchasing, but it is handy (no pun intended) although I only use it occasionally. If the touchscreen is important to you, be aware that this is a traditional laptop and cannot be used as a tablet. In fact, it only opens about 135 degrees.
The keyboard is back-lit and is the "chicklet" style where there is space between each key. It also has the full number pad. The keys have a slight resistance and give a satisfying but barely audible click when pressed. I've read some reviews that say the keys are too hard to press, but I think the resistance is helpful considering my tendency to "fat-finger" nearby keys.
The existing reviews also made me wary of the touchpad. Since I seldom use it anyway, I figured it would not be a deal breaker. I was pleasantly surprised at how well it works. The bottom area of the touchpad is "split" by a vertical indent that divides the right and left click area and the pad actually depresses when you click. Of course, you can still tap to left click and tap with two fingers to right click because the touchpad is multi-touch as well. The touchpad is not centered on the chassis, but instead centered on the keyboard home positions (or the 'B' key if you prefer).
The USB ports are all 3.0 and one has "power sharing", which means that power is available from that port even with the laptop turned off.
The speakers are quite loud and sound surprisingly good with a pretty full range.
There is very little garbage installed on the laptop. My last FusionTech (some 8 years ago) had so much "bloatware" that I had to do a clean OS install right off the bat. Not so with this one. It comes with trial subscriptions to McAfee and MS Office and a few FusionTech "service" apps. I haven't HAD TO uninstall anything yet, but I did uninstall Candy Crush just so I wouldn't be tempted...

The Bad:
There is no VGA, DVI, or display port, only HDMI out. I thought with the GeForce graphics GPU, they would offer more connectivity options.
The one HDMI output is only FHD, not 4K. :-(
Heavy! It weighs in at a hefty 6 lbs (NOT the 4.6 that Amazon shows), but there is quite a bit packed in this machine.
The memory card reader slot is only compatible with SD and MMC, so NO memory stick (Sony) or compact flash.
There is only one audio port, so you can't plug in headphones and a mic unless they are integrated and use the same plug.
At just over 15" wide and 1" thick, it barely fits in my laptop bag. No really, I have to remove my Logitech mouse receiver (sticks out about 1/4").
Older camera technology doesn't allow face recognition login to Windows 10, at the moment. Crossing my fingers that FusionTech can address this with a driver update???

The bottom line is...
I bought this laptop for $999 and other brands were selling for 200-300 more for the same specs. It does everything that I need it to do and does it very fast. I don't think you can go wrong with this laptop at that price.

text:
Don't buy if you plan on using it for more than a year. The reason this is so cheap is because they clearly cut costs on construction to provide for the internals. After about a year, the left side hinge just completely broke. Never dropped it, and it's only left the house a few times. After opening the lid, it'll create such a gaping hole you think you're just completely ripping the frame off. After the lid is up, you can kind of snap it back into place, but it will never go back to where it's supposed to be. Other reviews have said that this particular issue isn't even covered by warranty, and they will charge for repairs. After looking inside, there are two small screws that hold the hinges in place on either side, and the one on the left side was completely popped from its thread. I would recommend using some thread locker, and checking every month or so to make sure they aren't loose. Either way, that's an issue you absolutely shouldn't have to worry about with such a high end laptop.

That issue aside, this is a nice laptop for casual gaming. It has good speakers, a relatively okay graphics card, and a good CPU. I love the matte screen, but it has bad tinting and I would not recommend it for color intensive work.The trackpad is definitely nothing to scream home about and can be very frustrating to work with. It even pops out a bit from its frame (out of the box) and is a little unsightly to look at. The end of the cable tends to fray a little over time, but it's only the plastic jacket and not the wire itself, so it shouldn't cause any real issues. Those construction issues as well as the absolute fingerprint magnet of the exterior does not make this a very pretty laptop after some use.

Overall, I don't recommend this laptop. I would say to shell out the extra hundred to get something with adequate construction that still has good peripherals and internals.

title_x: i7 6700Hq and UHD display and Signature Edition Windows 10
text:
I really really love the price and performance of this machine, it handles CAD work, gaming and editing projects like a dream with it's 6700HQ and 4gb 960m. The 4k screen is vivid and even at 15.6 inches with display scaling in windows 10 it is very usable. The laptop does not get too toasty even while gaming at 4k with lowered settings, but while rendering a project in Maya I do make sure to prop it up a little bit more so it can get a bit more ventilation. The SSHD is passable, with livable latency at the moment, I will definitely be purchasing my own SSD to put into the MSATA port in the near future. The keyboard could be better, the touchpad is not great, but once you adjust to it and it's strange acceleration curve is usable, but not reliable for productivity like what you see on macbooks. Overall build quality is pretty good, I've never had a laptop this expensive before, but even made of plastic, it feels sturdy enough for how I treat my products, I don't feel like I need to baby it. I have the flat grey model, it still has red accents on the speaker/exhaust grill on top, and the exhaust on the back too, just the subtlest hints that this isn't just a web browsing and youtube watching machine.
Now, onto the the couple of cons that really stood out to me.
I received my laptop not with Signature Edition Windows 10, but with the bloatware infested OS from FusionTech, I love FusionTech hardware, I use their ultrasharp monitors exclusively in work and gaming, but my god their software is annoying. Many things have forced their way onto my startup and required use of CCleaner to get rid of, the worst of them being Mcafee and their ecosystem. This caused me some time and headache to get rid of. Now that I've gone through solving it, everything is kosher, but coming from a custom built PC that I put together with a fresh operating system and no bloaty drivers, this left a sour taste in my mouth.
Rehashing on the touchpad and keyboard, these are the parts of the laptop I use most, and to skimp on them was pretty bad, the keyboard less so, as chiclet keys can only be so good, but the touchpad really should be better, my old HP dv7 from 2006 or 7 has a better feeling and more responsive touchpad.

Update:
I'm not sure if this was present before writing my review or if I failed to notice it until now, but there is a slight yellow discoloration along the bottom and right edges of my screen. I will be attempting to seek an RMA to resolve this, the yellow discoloration is shown in the included picture.

text:
The laptop has been perfect for me when it comes to both games and school. I have a dedicated desktop for gaming, however, this came in handy and could easily handle titles such as Grand Theft Auto, Battlefield, and The Witcher 3. School work was near perfect, I could have 20 tabs open while researching/writing papers, as well as extremely quick responses during online homework programs such as Pearson Connect, etc.

Battery life is expected to be bad due to the more powerful components of the PC. New the battery life was around 5-8 hours depending on how intense the load was. I bought the laptop in 2016 and currently, at (1/13/19) the battery almost stays around 3-5 hours which is bearable due to how often It has been in use for the past few years.

However, the one major flaw I have with this laptop that discouraged me thoroughly is the build quality or lack thereof. FusionTechs newer Worktop models have adequately fixed the notorious plastic hinge issue with a large stretching across the screen rather than the laptops current placement on the sides. I do not throw my laptop around, I have not stepped on it, or sat on it. I have intensely babied this laptop for 3 years and I expect it to be slower, I did not expect it to legitimately crack at the hinges and begin to split. I cannot move this laptop nor do I take it to school due to the fear of it getting worse. Regardless of trying to be careful, more and more plastic begins to separate and crack. I am not the only one who has this issue and it has been reported by multiple consumers on FusionTech's forums. If it begins to crack while under warranty ( 1 year) they will fix it however most of the time it's usually out of warranty. As much as I love the performance of this computer and appreciated how well it's worked out for me and still continues to do so ( kind of) I cannot recommend this to anyone who is looking for a long term computer. Considering this costs about $1000, I cannot fathom how the build quality can be this dispicable on such an expensive laptop.

text:
This is a very solid gaming laptop, despite not being advertised as one. There is no reason to pay hundreds of dollars extra for a "gaming" branded laptop, when you can get something like this with a decent dedicated graphics card. For some reference, I usually play Overwatch at medium settings and get well over 60 fps at 1080p. It may even go higher but I value the consistent fps more than some slight graphics improvements.

The actual build is fine; I usually just keep it at home and don't take it out much so I can't comment too much on its durability. The keyboard, trackpad, and screen are all okay. It's not going to win any awards but they do the job.

I highly recommend you buy an SSD, as the internal hard drive is honestly unusable and slow at least for gaming. You're going to need an M.2 SSD, not the standard 2.5" kind. You just need to remove the single screw holding the backplate and pop the drive right in. Also, instead of just cloning the OS to the SSD, I recommend that you do a fresh install of Windows. That way you won't have all the FusionTech bloatware that comes with it, and will have a nice snappy booting experience. Two birds, one stone.

Anyway, this laptop has treated me very well. If you know what you're doing, give it some upgrades, and treat it right you'll be fine. It's a great machine.

text:
The machine isn't quite strong enough to support UHD, but it runs smoothly enough. The display is bright and vivid as well. The keyboard's backlight control comes in 3 levels (bright, dim, and off), which is suitable enough for most tasks.

It runs modern games smoothly at 1920x1080 and even 2048x1152 (I haven't tried higher, except 3840x2160). One thing to be wary of, though, is that it can get quite hot, especially in hotter climates, such that games and such start slowing down a little. One effective solution is to prop up the rear end of the laptop with 2 granola bars (or similar) to unblock the air intakes from the bottom of the laptop. I'm not sure if that's how this laptop works, but it certainly is effective. Alternatively, for those without access to granola bars, buying a dedicated laptop cooler or even laptop stand can help.

The 1TB hybrid drive can be slow at times, but still starts up fast enough for most tasks.

Overall, I am very satisfied with this laptop.

text:
This is the perfect laptop with the addition of M.2 SSD and 8GB system memory. Near perfect as it comes out of the box.

I read every single review from multiple sites before buying. I can say that most of the "cons" are utterly ridiculous. Sure, hardware defects happen and they are annoying, but they are not cons.

This machine is well made. The 4K screen is crisp and responsive. The CPU and GPU combination easily handle everything I task them with. The easy-access panel is great, and rare these days.

Do yourself a favor and buy the M.2 SSD and extra 8GB memory, install both and then spend an hour updating drivers and Windows 10. Then migrate the OS to SSD - for this I recommend Paragon "migrate OS to SSD" as there are some tricky issues with UEFI BIOS and boot drive (trust me on this). Their software makes it simple and it took about 10 minutes. Reformat the 1TB hybrid drive for storage and you have yourself an absolute monster of a laptop. Nothing in this price range can touch this thing.

title_x: Makes some compromises; Good, not great, gaming laptop
text:
I've been needing my own laptop for a while now. I have my work PC, but it's nice to have my own system that I can do gaming on without having to worry about questions from IT or my supervisors about what I'm doing instead of the work that I should be doing, so this was a great grab.

The design of this is relatively simple, fitting the design schematics of most modern non-Apple laptops. I am not a huge fan of the color scheme, but it was the only color available when I picked it up, so c'est la vie. Regarding the form factor, I am a fan of the headphone port being on the left side; my work PC has it on the right, which makes it awkward to use on small tables since my mouse often has to cohabitate with the headphone cable (I don't like Bluetooth headphones, so if you do, YMMV). The lack of ad additional HDMI port on the back of the system really marks this as not really intending to be used as part of a flexible desktop dual monitor/portable setup, which contrasts with its relatively high weight (~5.5 lbs) for a machine intended to be carried around or its relatively small screen size. It also has a screen bezel that is, in my opinion, obnoxiously thick. The platform itself is a bit thicker than I like, particularly for systems that I am going to type on regularly. I *think* that this chassis was necessary, however, to accomodate the relatively robust video card that is onboard. And I do say relatively. The 3060 is not a bad card, but it is considerably underpowered compared to the 3070Ti. Perhaps thermals were an issue here, but I suspect the choice of card for this system was based on availability (3060s are supposed to have on-board firmware to limit Ethereum mining, which should make them easier to acquire, even for OEMs), rather than performance. This will probably still run most 2020's era games, but perhaps not at max visual settings; you may get some minor tearing in the vertical if you are running things at their highest levels. The onboard sound is okay and the system speakers are reasonably powerful if you're not wearing headphones, but I'm not sure how often people do that now. If you're going to watch a movie on it, it is probably plenty loud; given the small screen, you won't be sitting that far anyway.

The keyboard is a good size and includes numerics, which means that if I need to do something that is not gaming on this (like prepare my taxes), it should be comfortable to use. Sensitivity across the touchpad is pretty decent.

The battery life is not great, whether doing relatively low-drain things like watching a movie or using more video-card requiring purposes. I was unable to match the claimed battery life; I got about 5-6 hours of use when not running anything intensive. When running something more demanding, it was closer to 3-4.

It comes with Windows 11, which is probably part of the reason the battery life isn't great. You might have better luck if you dual boot into a UNIX-based OS for non-gaming needs. I haven't bothered with that, though, since I usually don't get many opportunities to game for more than an hour or two, and I generally do it from a place where an adapter will work, so it hasn't been a priority for me.

Overall a relatively solid, dependable system. Not great, but sufficient, particularly if you are not interested in a particularly powerful and non-moving desktop setup. The cost is pretty reasonable, given the components. The color isn't my cuppa, but...you get what you get and you don't throw a fit, as they say.

I needed a laptop with a decent RTX graphics card as I do 3D rendering with my home desktop and I wanted to be sure I got a laptop that would at least let me set the scenes up okay while I am away from home. This laptop does that great, but it does fall behind a bit when it comes to trying to preview the renders or do a full render. Not the fault of the laptop, rendering requires a very beefy GPU, and you can only do so much with a RTX 3060 from a laptop. It's not as good a true RTX 3060 that you use in a desktop.

Anyway, aside from rendering, so far it has worked great for the few games I play. I am not much of a gamer, but I do play several games like Guild Wars 2, Fornite, and a few other Gacha and Idle type games, and they are all working great. Even bench-marking with 3D Mark 11 is giving respectable scores. I did also replace the initial 16GB of memory it came for this [[ASIN:B09S2QLBWC Crucial RAM 64GB Kit]]
with as 16GB just was not enough for a power user like me and the newer memory is faster, but the memory it comes with will be fine for most buyers.

My only complaints so far is similar to what other reviewer have mentioned. The 256Gb SSD it came with is decent and has a okay speed (at a bit over 3000Mbps), but it is just not large enough for my needs, so I ordered a 2Tb replacement drive. Like others mentioned, if you want to install a new SSD, you will need to buy a [[ASIN:B09N7BSPQZ 3rd party bracket and heatsink]] to allow the SSD to be secured down because the existing drive is a 2230 size and the parts it comes with won't be enough to secure a 2280 SSD.

Another complaint is the motherboard and casing of this laptop were clearly designed to hold a second NVME drive, but the board itself does not have the related components built onto it to add one. I just don't get why they did not give us the ability to use that 2nd NVME slot for a slightly higher price. I cannot imagine it would have the manufacturer much to have that 2nd set of parts for another drive and would have greatly increased the value of the laptop. I am forced to use a single 2TB NVME drive installed (supposedly it can support up to 4tb, but was not willing to spend that much), and a combo of a few USB external drives for storage of my 3D assets and all that.

The only other things of note would be the mouse pad can be a little tricky to use (but most will use a external mouse anyway so not a huge thing), and I don't mind the keyboard much, but I do wish the arrow keys were a bit more regular size, but this is a minor annoyance.

If there was one other thing I wish it had, it would be more USB ports. It only has 2 x USB 3.1 ports on the right side, and 1 x Thunderbolt/USB-C and 1 x USB 3.1 port on the back. While this is good for most people, I would have liked to have at least 1 more USB-C port for data use only (since most will use the thunderbolt port for a dock), and/or another USB 3.1 port on the left side of the laptop (which currently has the LAN port and Headphones/Mic port).

Other than 1 BSOD I have gotten so far (GPU related), this laptop is working great nad it not super heavy (which is a big plus for me). I did decide to get a nice little [[ASIN:B09NRTVV3M cooling pad]] for it to assist with keeping it cool while I work on rendering (since it is very CPU and GPU intensive, causing a lot of heat), and while I don't plan to use it on the go much, as many others have pointed out, the battery will not last a super long time.

Most people don't realize just how much power this little laptop needs and the size of the battery just won't allow it to last very long. This is pretty much expected for a gaming laptop. If you want a longer lasting laptop, then you better expect to get a much more expensive laptop (which will also weigh a lot more to accommodate a larger battery), or a less powerful one.

My only real regret is that I did not buy the i9 version with the RTX 3070 Ti GPU since I do use it for rendering. This would have greatly improved my rendering ability, but the extra cost and the fact that I could not get it on the payment plan are the reasons why I did not go that route. If I was not in such a hurry to get it, I would have preferred to get the better model. Maybe some day I can go on eBay and get parts needed to replace the board and CPU to get those specs, but that will be a down the road thing.

title_x: Beautiful design, but there are some issues
text:
Let me begin by stating that we are a FusionTech family. I've had several ABC laptops and an Worktop desktop over the years, and my children all have Advance desktop computers. So, when I was asked to review the FusionTech G15 5520 15.6 Inch Gaming Laptop, I went in expecting to fall in love with it. Regrettably, I did not. I waited two months to write this review, hoping that the problems I was having were software-related and that installing all of the updates I could find would solve my problems. There have been two BIOS updates and a slew of other updates since I received this laptop. I installed every required and recommended update, and I kept other software installations to a minimum. I only installed a video conferencing app and a pdf reader from trusted brands. But this laptop keeps crashing. I have had at least 10 blue screens. Furthermore, I had to reinstall Windows because when I started the laptop, it would state that Windows did not load properly, and restarting the PC only helped for a short time.

I've had a number of problems since the beginning. For example, even though the settings are set so that the laptop should sleep when I close the lid, it appears to keep running as the battery drains. I'll go to bed with a fully charged laptop, only to wake up with one that's at 0%. I tried leaving it plugged in, but it gets so hot that I'm afraid it's dangerous. Speaking of how hot it gets, even when doing simple tasks like editing a text document or slides, it appears to work so hard that it is burning up. It's better when it's not plugged in, but I can only get about 2.30 hours out of it on battery power alone, which isn't great. So I've been using this laptop exclusively with a constantly running cooler pad. I can see why this is required for serious gaming, but for light text editing? On top of everything else, my screen began to display multicolored lines last week as well. I thought that was it, but I haven't seen any this week, so fingers crossed.

There are a few features on this laptop that I do enjoy. The design is wonderful. My husband is in the army, and the design is identical to his uniform, so I thought this laptop would make an excellent gift for him. I also like that there is a separate numeric keypad. That was missing from my ABC laptops. It took me a few days to get used to typing more to the left, but once I did, I was hooked. I also like how simple it is to turn the keyboard lights on and off. When I try to work at night, the light definitely helps. Another feature I appreciate is the FusionTech update app on the laptop. You don't really need to go to their website to get necessary updates anymore. Overall, if it weren't for the technological issues, I think this would be a fantastic laptop. However, based on my recent experiences as well as the weight of this laptop and the power brick, I still prefer my ABC, even if she is a little older.
