text:
9/4/2022: FusionTech G15 5520 15.6 Inch Gaming Laptop - FHD 120Hz Display, Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA RTX 3060 6GB GDDR6, Intel Wi-Fi 6, Windows 11 - Spector Green

I ordered this to replace my 12 year old desktop computer, which has been showing its age now for quite some time. I never want to sit at a desk anymore anyway, so I've been looking at laptops to replace it for a while now. I've had this one a few weeks now and I am very happy with it so far!

It is very fast and very quiet. I rarely hear the fans at all unless I put my ear right up to it. I have never had a computer this quiet before. It has a nice bright screen, and the keyboard has a numberpad on it! I like the backlit keyboard a lot too.

I don't have any modern PC games at this point (gave up on PC gaming a long time ago since my old desktop couldn't play very many of them) so I can't really review the gaming features yet, but I'm very excited about the opportunity to play games once I get some good ones! It has handled everything else I've tried to do very well - it is faster than my work laptop and MUCH faster than my ancient desktop.

It does eventually get kind of hot on the bottom, enough that it hurts when resting on my legs -- it's still summer so I'm mostly wearing shorts and I have had to put a blanket between the computer and my bare legs. Long pants will solve this problem, but I'm probably going to get some sort of cooling pad anyway so I can be sure it has proper ventilation. It doesn't get hot in the touchpad area on which your hands rest, which is really nice.

It is pretty heavy compared to my 14" work laptop, although I do like the big bright screen a lot. I'm not that strong so this laptop is a lot less portable than a smaller one would be. I can move it from my desk to my couch though, and the big screen is really nice when I'm not near my external monitors.

I have only two (possibly 3?) complaints so far:

1. Very minor complaint with the keyboard layout. They made the arrow keys very short and then put the page up and page down keys just above the left and right arrows.. I'm constantly hitting page up or down when trying to move the cursor left or right. I'm hoping I get used to it. The rest of the keyboard layout is fine, I have no trouble hitting the correct keys aside from the arrow keys.

2. The power cord keeps coming out just enough that the computer won't charge. It looks like it's still in, but then I'll be surprised by a low battery warning. I have to keep pushing it back in to make sure it keeps charging. I don't know if this is an issue with the laptop or with the power adapter, but it doesn't seem like other people are complaining about this very much, so perhaps something is wrong with mine. It doesn't actually have any trouble charging though, just physically keeping the charger plugged in all the way. Not a dealbreaker for me, and I still like the computer just as much.

3. I have not actually tested this yet so I can't say if it's a complaint or not, but according to the specs it appears that the thunderbolt port does not support power delivery, only power share. So I can use my laptop to charge other things, but I can't get a thunderbolt dock that will also charge the laptop. I didn't know anything about thunderbolt ports before so I just assumed they all worked the same way. I can't take off any stars for something that it never promised it could do, and/or for something I can't actually test yet... but if you're looking for a laptop that can be charged by another thunderbolt device, you probably should do a bit more research first. It is very likely this laptop doesn't support that.

Regardless of these complaints, I'm very happy with this laptop! I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could, as 4 stars seems a bit low. I reserve 5 star reviews for when no improvement is necessary though, and I do think the charger or charging port could use some improvement. So, 4 stars it is! I still highly recommend this laptop!

title_x: Gaming Laptop with quite a bit of bloatware and no touchscreen
text:
As per what I've come to expect with FusionTech hardware, it comes installed with quite a few things I don't really need, however, it definitely does its job for gaming and is decently comfortable for typing as long as you have a laptop desk to protect your lap or use it on a desk.

The orange backlit keyboard is pretty nice for typing (using it to type this review right now) and doesn't feel super mushy like some laptop membrane keyboard, though I'm not yet sure if that'll hold up to long-term hardcore gaming, so even if you're playing at LAN parties elsewhere, I'd probably bring a dedicated keyboard (and of course a mouse) and that brings me to the peripherals.

Basically, this has enough USB ports for a mouse and keyboard and 2 spare ports for other items, or if you happen to use one of the wireless keyboard/mouse combos that use 1 dongle, you'd have 3 available. As well, it does have a standard headphone/mic jack for gaming headset needs along with an ethernet port, and it only has 1 HDMI or you have to use 1 of the USB ports as well for another monitor. I'd say if you're going to use this as your main gaming machine, it would probably be best to invest in a USB dock that can help you solve your port problem, though you'll have to check those specs on them especially since not all of them support high refresh rate gaming, so watch out for that.

Another thing that this does well with is sound quality. I won't say it's super amazing, but you won't be disappointed with the experience, though you'll definitely want a headset when you're not at home with this.

I will also say that this thing gets HOT. Even when it's only using the onboard graphics this thing can kick out heat so be careful when letting it sleep as sometimes it doesn't completely sleep and can get quite hot, so make sure it's well vented when plugged in so you don't have any hot surprises! The brick also cooks as well at times so be careful of that.

Overall, it's a decent gaming laptop, though I'd say it's better as a mobile gaming machine over your main machine, but I'm blessed enough to have a gaming PC that outclasses this laptop but is a royal pain to travel with over this.

title_x: Perfect for a creator - a lot of hardware for the money!
text:
I got this exact configuration directly from D e|| (Core i9 12800H, RTX 3070 Ti, 32GB RAM), and thought I'd share impressions here.

As a creator (and not a gamer), I do video and photo editing on this machine, mostly connected to an external monitor and plugged into wall power. In this context, this machine with its specs is probably the best value of 2022 from a major brand name that is broadly available online.

You can find various online reviews of this machine (or its closely-related 2022 G15 relative), so I won't rehash anything really here. But I would just offer these salient points that aren't immediately obvious in some reviews:

The (major) high's for me:
(1) The CPU and GPU are allowed to run high in their power thermal envelopes, so you're getting a lot of performance for this combination of hardware.
(2) The 2022 G16 has a 16:10 screen, which is superior for creation and productivity versus the 2022 G15's 16:9.
(3) The included 2x16GB DDR5 RAM sit in two slots that are user-upgradeable to 2x32GB when I'm ready.

The (minor) low's for me:
(1) The single USB-C Thunderbolt port does not support Power Delivery, so you're stuck using the included brick and barrel power jack for power.
(2) There is no connector on the motherboard for a second M.2 PCIe SDD. They seemingly removed this capability in 2022, though the 2021 G15 did have this.
(3) The trackpad is laughingly small given how big this laptop is. They could have pushed the keyboard higher on the deck to make more room below the keyboard for a bigger trackpad.
(5) When using high performance settings, unsurprisingly, the fans sound like a passenger jet taking off.
(6) The included FusionTech and Advance configuration software are unsurprisingly slightly buggy. For example, settings don't always "stick"; the laptop charges up to 100% even when I set it to stop charging, say, 80%; and pressing keyboard backlight button sometimes doesn't do anything until I load up the Advance config software again.

In my view, the high's far and away outweigh the (minor) low's, especially for how I use the machine.

title_x: This is a beautiful piece of computer engineering at a price I could afford
text: I replaced my faithful, dual boot, 2013 MacBook Air - which served me well for nearly 10 years and still runs today, albeit with some technology lags and failures that are more related to its capacity to keep up with OS and software advances over the intervening years.  I needed to have something portable, not too heavy for my personal mobile computing.  However, I work in complex and advanced 3D design, modeling and AI, so ideally, my mobile personal machine had to have a dedicated graphics adapter.  This meant compromising some of the weight and battery life so I could flick over to a work assignment right there on my laptop when the need dictated.  The G15 is a perfect machine for this.  Fits perfectly in a small carry bag.  Sports a nVidia GeForce RTX 3060 (6GB VRAM) with amazing heat management features that have obviously developed from their exceptional Advance stable. What is really amazing is taking a personal mobile computing machine out of the bag and experiencing the modern Windows11 experience and changes!  Oh my gosh, it is so fast and beautiful.  The changes since I last upgraded from Win7 to Win10 and now Win11 are incredible.  Being a Chrome browser for years, I thought I would experience what MS has done with Edge on this new hardware and latest OS - incredible!  The experience has been amazing.  Microsoft under Satya is to be commended - I am loving it!  My G15 sports a 12th Gen, 14 CORE i7.  It is lightning fast and with some of my work requirements, having access to 20 threads will be a huge advantage for those times I need to browse alongside my work!  Finally, this little, Prime Day powerhouse steal, came with a full keyboard!  Do you know how rare that is in this, lower-end price range, personal computer that doubles as a 3D graphics Workstation when needed!?!?!?  Just take a look and see how hard a full keyboard is to find on such a machine and it is really important for me and everything I want to do on my personal machine.  Amazing!  FusionTech and MS - I am loving my G15!  Thankyou. R

text:
I'm a designer whose primary hobby is photography. A few years back, I switched from Mac to PC, because I work in VR and Apple had yet to produce a system capable of the heavy lifting that technology needs. While it was certainly easy to construct PC desktop machines that were far more capable than an iMac, finding proper laptops to meet or exceed Apple's standards hasn't been as easy. Until now...

This FusionTech ABC 9570 is a gorgeous, powerful machine. Don't make the mistake of thinking that the 8GB or i5 spec make it less robust. Each component is the latest generation and has been designed to do substantially more with less, all while keeping the machine cool and nimble. In fact, when compared to my two-year-old Surface Pro with twice the memory and 30% more numerical processing power, this machine is substantially faster. The newer RAM and processor are more efficient, if they look less powerful on paper.

As for the build quality, you'll notice it immediately when you unbox the machine. FusionTech has gone out of it's way to hone the look and feel of everything from the charger to the box it's packaged in. The unboxing experience says "we're proud of this machine and you will be too".

What strikes me most is the high quality of the screen. It's absolutely gorgeous. Edge-to-edge brilliance. As a designer and photographer, I care about color and accuracy and this screen has that in spades. This model is not a touch screen, which I do miss (as I got used to it on my dated Surface Pro), but I also appreciate that I'm not putting finger prints all over the screen either.

The keyboard and touchpad are comfortable and tactile. I love the Windows Hello fingerprint reader. The fact that it's also the power button makes it super easy to login to the machine. With an SSD drive, you're up and running moments after turning this gem on.

Aside from all of the hardware goodness, this machine just works. I love how nimble it is with Adobe Lightroom CC. This is always my test software and the ABC 9570 edits complex, large-file images quickly and efficiently. I selected the option to "Use Graphics Processor" and Lightroom takes full advantage of the machines NVIDIA GPU: edits are quick and renderings in grid view are fast enough for me to scroll quickly through older images that aren't saved locally and must render from the web.

While the machine has a smaller 256GB hard drive, using modern storage management built into solutions like One Drive and Lightroom CC, I'm able to keep the majority of my files in the cloud to preserve space and only keep local copies of what I use regularly. So it works out just fine and the speed is well worth it.

All in all, I highly recommend this machine. It's a gorgeous piece of hardware that works perfectly for substantially less cost than a similar Mac. If you're a visual creative, you can't go wrong.

text:
I have had several laptops supplied by my employer and have gotten used to sub-par machines that consistently disappoint for too long. The FusionTech ABC 15 is like trading in a Ford for a Ferrari. I will take a quick survey of the features I like the most.

Display - The graphics card is really what takes this PC from Good to Great. I am not one who can spout off all of the specs that make it excellent. But, just watching streaming services and playing a few of the newer PC games I see an incredible difference in clarity and smoothness. This machine cuts through these tasks without lagging or any signs of difficulty. I haven't found a graphics task yet that it hasn't handled perfectly. I didn't realize how crappy my other machines were until I had the pleasure of witnessing this one.

WiFi - I have had a top of the line router for a while now and wasn't really able to take advantage of it with other machines. My kids loved it because their gaming systems perform well on our network. But this machine runs on the network with complete fluidity, zero lag times and flawless streaming. It takes all of the frustration out of the process. Get the password set and off you go.

Look/Styling - Apple has set the standard for sleek machines. This is just the fact of the matter. But this FusionTech has a very stylish look and feel. The case is a matt stainless steel, a black and silver motif. The profile is thin and the weight is light. I expected the screen to be much smaller, but it has a large feel to it. The panel the keyboard sits in has a rubber coated feel and a sort of graphite compound look to it. I really like the simplicity to it all. There was a time when PCs thought having a bunch of bells and whistles was the way to go. They have finally realized less is more and this FusionTech is a beautiful example of that concept.

Keyboard - I am so relieved the keyboard on this machine is top shelf. I am a writer before anything else and having a sensible keyboard is inegral to my happiness. I had one machine a few years back where they decided to make the Shift key half the size of the normal configuration. Chaos!!! I had to sell the thing to retain my sanity. This keyboard is perfect for all of us who are standardized and used to the traditional set up. The keys are backlit and have a very satisfying mechanism. They aren't too loud, but give sufficient feedback as you work. I don't find myself wondering if I actually clicked the key or not. You can work in low light or even the dark very easily if you must. Also, there is sufficient space for the wrists and hands on this machine. As I said before, other machines put so much junk on the surface that the seat supplied for your hands was small or cramped. Not here.

Battery Life - I cannot yet give an honest assessment of the battery life as I have not pushed it to the limit yet. If it doesn't live up to the listed claims, I will be sure to update my review.

Sound - Another pleasant surprise. My perspective here may not be the most up to date as I am comparing this machine to some pretty lame competition. But I was very satisfied with the sound as I watched movies and shows on this machine through Netflix and Amazon. It wasn't on par with high performance audio, but it was dynamite for a laptop sound system. Most people would want to use a headset, so it will depend on the quality of that unit anyway.

Ease of set-up - This is pretty much standard across the industry these days, but for those of us who remember taking a day or two to set up a machine, 15 minutes is outstanding. Also, if you have a microsoft account, it is even easier.

Overall Performance - I love this machine. It does everything I need it to do: stream, game, look cool, have sound keyboard mechanisms, speedy wifi, the works. I couldn't be happier with it.

For the price point, this is a very fast computer which plays games quite well and has a beautiful display. I used this to play 3D RPG games and they looked amazing and played without any hiccups. Web pages also loaded rapidly and without hanging. System operations (moving files, doing searches on the hard drive) are also brisk and I'm guessing that's because of the SSD. While the hard drive is smaller than typical, it is more than adequate for the system and apps and the speed is worth the smaller size. The RAM seems quite sufficient for the system and most apps to run. I didn't experience any problems running anything on it, though I didn't run any RAM-hungry powerhouses.

The claims that this is viewable from any angle are true. The color if beautiful, but it's a bit dark on the default setting and needs a bit of adjustment. The screen is small, of course, but it's not stressful to look at or difficult to read from. It does also run edge to edge as promised. I hooked it up to an external HDMI display with video mirroring and found that the port worked well and there was no lag between what was on one screen on the other. I also found that the laptop can be closed and you can still use it with an external keyboard, mouse, and display without any tweaking or changes.

In terms of the keyboard, I liked that the keys are underlit so they're easy to find/read in dim light conditions, but even in full light, it's helpful given that the keyboard and inside of the body of the computer is black.

I didn't have any problems setting up the internet using wireless WiFi nor were there any problems connecting some bluetooth speakers. title_x: Features, likes and dislikes, test results, known bugs
text:
The ABC offers many professional capabilities in a small, sleek package. The 9570 is the 2018 and still current 15" version. The main differences from past models are:

-- Can do more faster. The i5 in this is 6-20% more powerful than the fastest processor available in the previous model (9560).
-- The screen (FHD = 1920x1080) is about one third brighter than before, though still not as bright as the 4K one (UHD = 3840x2160).
-- The Thunderbolt port now has four PCIe lanes, twice as many as before. That only affects powerful PCIe devices you might plug into your machine, but if you're going to use an eGPU, it will be a significant improvement.

This one differs from the current base (cheapest) configuration in three ways:

-- Has a dedicated graphics processor (GPU), the 1050, which greatly increases the level of video processing or gaming you can do (though it doesn't really make this a "gaming laptop").
-- Has the larger battery, 97Wh, which offers 50% or more battery time than the 56Wh one.
-- Has a smallish solid-state drive (SSD), 256GB, instead of a slower but four-times-larger spinning hard drive (HDD) "hybrid" that includes 32GB of fast SSD.

Unlike the first two differences, the last one you can upgrade at home later if you want, all it takes is a couple screwdrivers. But you can't have both the larger battery and an internal HDD because they fit in the same space: if you get the larger battery, you can only use an SSD inside. You can also upgrade the amount of RAM. These upgrades (and some other things you can do to improve performance that I'll mention below) don't affect the warranty.

Personal reactions

I have a 2016 MacBook Pro 15 that fills a similar niche. While I prefer the Mac overall, the FusionTech offers more power for the money, and Windows does some things that are harder or impossible to do as well on Macs--that is, run software optimized for Windows. Of which there's a lot.

I like this ABC for some of the same reasons I like the MBP. It's very easy to carry around and looks good. It feels solid and durable. It operates well on the whole. Some of the things I don't like are limitations of Windows, at least as implemented by FusionTech.

For example, to listen to streaming from a radio station while not otherwise using the machine, I have to disable sleep in the system controls or it goes to sleep and stops the stream. And then I have to re-enable it afterwards. (And why do I have to use DOS commands to do simple things like find out what battery is in this?)

Anyway, battery life is excellent for the mostly light work I do. I can go all day on battery, over 12 hours, doing web browsing, writing, some Youtube, etc with power to spare. (Because I usually leave it plugged in, the battery only charges to 87Wh, which is supposed to be better for a plugged-in battery. It can be made to charge more fully if you don't leave it plugged in much.)

As mentioned above, this machine can be easily owner-upgraded, or repaired, unlike the MBP (or Surface Book).

The screen has good color and brightness, and is sharp enough in some ways, but I'm used to higher resolution and notice the difference often in small type and in increased jaggies in graphics.

There are advantages to having a lower-resolution screen, though, takes less processing power and saves battery life. With the same battery the UHD/i7 configuration will give you on average about 25% less battery life. (The UHD screen also has less color accuracy, that's in addition to a color bug mentioned below. On the other hand, it has a larger range of colors.)

This screen is anti-glare, which I prefer. Glossy (like the UHD) looks sweet until you have a glare issue, when the matte finish saves eye strain and battery life, since you don't have to turn it up as bright to see clearly.

Based on tests, this screen (like the UHD) has slower-than-average response time (quickness in changing from one color or shade to another), which matters for gaming and watching video, but I haven't noticed.

The lower corners show a little backlight bleed, visible when the screen is dark there.

The screen is longer and less tall than I'm used to.

The speaker grill/cooling intake vent is on the bottom, causing partial blockage issues on a soft surface like a lap. A flat platform helps.

The speaker quality isn't great, fairly tinny, but it's usable for casual purposes. (I haven't had any of the popping and clicking some people report--see below on that.)

The fan noise isn't bad to my ears, about like my MBP. (But see below on that too.)

The keyboard seems very nice but requires a firmer touch than my MBP, so I keep missing letters. The keys are quiet and have good travel up and down.

The keyboard backlighting leaks at the bottom of the keys, especially if you're at an angle. It goes off after ten seconds, more quickly than I'd like. There are only two settings for brightness besides off, both brighter than I'd prefer.

The wifi and Bluetooth are working well. There are complaints about them in the forums, though. If that becomes a problem, the card for them can be replaced by the owner. A good card costs $20-30.

The dark gray interior looks nice but it's more of a fingerprint magnet than most silver colors. You can clean it off with a soft cloth.

The fingerprint reader often doesn't work for me on the first try, but it's never failed to work after a couple tries. Probably I'll get better at putting my finger on just right.

I haven't had any of the coil whine the ABC series is famous for, though there are still some reports of it.

This isn't too unusual for a metal laptop, but at least while plugged in there's a tiny electrical charge in the chassis. It feels like a tiny prick when a sensitive part of my finger like around the cuticle just barely touches. Not dangerous.

The 9570 isn't really as thin as advertised. The 11-17mm (.43-.67") figures are for the edges, which are thinner than the middle. The true thickness is about 19mm (.75"), 22-23mm (.87-.91") if you count the two (suitably grippy) rubberized strips along the bottom.

With the larger battery this weighs 4-1/2 pounds, 1/2 pound more than my MBP.

Fortunately I don't use the web cam, or nostril cam as I call it, which is located below the screen.

Notebook Check found PWM (pulse-width modulation = screen flickering) at 961Hz at 10% brightness and below. That's a higher frequency than bothers most sensitive people, but if it's an issue for you, you'll have to keep the screen above 10% brightness. I keep the screen at its minimum most of the time inside and can't detect it, but I'm not among the sensitive.

Benchmarks and tests, gaming power

If you like this kind of stuff, I ran a few tests for the CPU, graphics, and SSD that can be used for comparative purposes, and I checked other benchmark and gaming reports for this and the the other 9570 configurations.

The i5, now that it's quad-core with hyper-threading, is impressive. Naturally the i7 in the current model is even more powerful, usually 10% or so, sometimes more. The i9 may add another 10% (maybe more if you take the special measures to control the operating temperature mentioned below). You can use the usual office and other productivity apps without worry with any of the current ABC chips.

For gaming, the 1050 is a capable chip that will play games that aren't too demanding at high settings and frame rates and almost any game at low settings and over 30 fps. The 1050Ti Max Q that's also offered on the ABC, coupled with the i7, will give you 10-25% more frames.

No ABC configuration is enough to do much gaming at 4K resolution. If you use an external monitor you can do some games at 144 fps and low settings.

You can edit 4K video fine.

For the best gaming/graphics performance you have to plug this in, which gives you about 30% more speed/frames. (You can also increase the performance significantly by replacing the thermal paste that helps cool the insides of the machine, by "undervolting," and by limiting the turbo speed of the processors. The last two are done with software to reduce the power going to the processors a little and thus the heat coming out.)

The tests I ran on my machine:

Geekbench 4
-- Single-Core CPU: 4750
-- Multi-Core CPU: 15186
-- OpenCL for 630 (the integrated GPU): 20121
-- OpenCL for 1050: 76397

PCMark 10
-- Overall: 4397
-- Essentials: 7578
-- Productivity: 7164
-- Digital Content Creation: 4250
-- Web: 7754
-- Apps: 8875
-- Chat: 6324
-- Photo: 4402
-- Video: 3724
-- Writing: 5761
-- Spreadsheet: 8909

Cinebench R15
-- OpenGL: 103-111 fps
-- CPU: 781-799

CrystalDiskMark doesn't recognize the SSD (it's made for FusionTech by Toshiba), so I couldn't run that test. ATTO and AJA tests showed that for typical file transfers read speeds range from 1.3 to over 1.9 GB/s, and ATTO had them up to 2.4-2.6 GB/s for the mid-range of its test. That's not the best but not bad either. Write speeds range lower, from 325 MB/s to over 1GB/s. That's typical of the reports I've seen. It's not terrible, but it's not as good as one expects from an SSD of this type.

By the way, you can't entirely trust the performance tests from most of the reviews for the 9570 because after a couple months FusionTech updated the BIOS (firmware) so that the machine throttles (cuts its performance) at a lower temperature than before. That probably helps protect the machine, but it makes it slower under load.

Known bugs: sleep, fans, speaker popping, BIOS

Every computer has bugs, often ones that affect only some users. So far I don't have trouble with any of these, but they're worth knowing about.

For this model FusionTech has disabled old-fashioned sleep, where it's basically dead to the world in a very low-power state but ready to come back to life very quickly when a key is pressed. It wasn't working right, causing excessive battery drain, and they say they're not going to bring it back. Instead you get a kind of sleep called "modern" or "connected" standby, which leaves the machine ready to receive messages and updates and such. It also uses more power than it should, as much as 2% an hour.

Another disadvantage of connected standby is that it seems your machine can be awakened while it's sleeping in your backpack or case and turn into an oven with fans going full speed trying to cool off because the vents are blocked.

FusionTech is working to fix this.

With the default settings, your machine should usually transition from connected standby to "hibernation" after a certain amount of time. In hibernation, the machine uses very little power and won't wake up accidentally, but it takes longer, 10 to 20 seconds, to wake back up. If you don't mind that, you can disable sleep and just use hibernate, which does work as it should.

Some people have had speaker popping and clicking from something called DPC latency that FusionTech has been trying to fix for ages but still hasn't figured out. It doesn't go away with headphones or external speakers. It's especially problematic for live music.

There are many complaints in the forums about the fans coming on when they shouldn't while the machine is in use. The most recent BIOS update, version 1.7, either caused or worsened it. That version did fix a problem introduced in an earlier update (1.4.1?) where the machine would throttle when the graphics card wasn't warm enough. (Yes, that makes no sense. There's also a bug that came in with an update that makes the color of the UHD screen worse, not an issue for the FHD.)

Mine came with BIOS version 1.3, and I haven't updated it. If yours comes with 1.3 you might want to just stick with it until the troubles caused by later updates are resolved, if that ever happens. Once you update past a certain point (about 1.3 I think), you can't go back.

Besides using the older BIOS, the lack of trouble I've had may be due in part to the minimal number of apps I use. Each app you install and use increases the chance of trouble of some kind or other for any computer.

I love love love this laptop. Why? Glad you asked :)

1: It has all the power of a gaming laptop but at half the weight. It is sleek, elegant, transportable, and packs one heck of a punch with that graphics card.

2: It's fast. Plenty of RAM, and the SSD hard drive is bananas.

3: THE SCREEN. The screen goes closer to the edge of the bezel than with any laptop I've ever seen. You get an insane amount of screen for a 15.6" laptop.

5: The keyboard. They keyboard is so satisfying to type on. It's much nicer than my Lenovo or my previous FusionTech.

6: The touchpad. The touchpad is super responsive.

Here are the cons.

Sound. The sound is pretty mediocre. Speakers take space, and they cut down on those. That said, I pretty much never ever use my laptop speakers. I use external speakers or I use headphones, so this doesn't impact me at all.

The webcam is in a slightly weird spot. It's worth it because you get way more screen. But it just means the video is at a not-dead-on-angle, which again, totally doesn't impact me.

And that's it!

This laptop is totally amazing, and the trade-offs they've made with sound and webcam placement are inconsequential and so worth it.

title_x: Runs great, when it runs at all...
text:
UPDATE:

After three or four years of life, I experienced an evidently common issue with FusionTech laptops: the DC power supply shorted out and the thing turned into a brick. The problem is with the motherboard, which unfortunately may mean a very expensive repair. I'm happy with FusionTech's customer service responsiveness, but frankly this is a stupid quality control problem that seems to have been a calculated business decision for them. This episode makes me seriously question whether I'll ever go with a FusionTech product again.

Original (naive) review:

The Advance AW17 is a great value for basically top-of-the-line hardware (at least as far as a laptop is concerned). I have been fortunate, as I have not really had any problems with this laptop whatsoever. Evidently the "Killer Wireless" ethernet adapter had some driver issues in the past, but mine seems to be working fine after downloading and installing the latest driver directly from the vendor. I suspect that some of the other unhappy customers were directing their anger at FusionTech/Advance whereas they probably should have been directing their anger at Microsoft/Windows 10, although your actual mileage may vary...

I got the UHD 4K monitor and have zero regrets there. Windows 10 does not scale very well, true, but the 4K screen is great for web browsing and even some games, although the GTX 980m does struggle to get above 30 fps on many recent titles @4K resolution (not a probem for X-Com 2 though!). The GTX 980m runs essentially without bottlenecking with this setup, and I'm happily running the Witcher 3 at around 30 FPS at 1080 resolution with all settings maxed out (a bit faster if you turn NVIDIA Hairworks down a notch), and Far Cry 4 at around 35 - 38 fps (as far as I can recall).

The real reason this deserves 5 stars is the option to add the graphics amplifier (sold separately) and drop in a desktop-spec GTX 1080 (or whatever else they come out with), which I fully intend to do. FusionTech is really the only game in town for this. I think I need to look into buying some stock...

My only gripe is that all the flashy AW trim seems to be aimed at the juvenile/teenager set, and I'm in my mid-30's and ashamed to be playing videogames at my relatively advanced age, so whenever I take this thing into the office and my coworkers see this thing, I get outed as the true Gooberish Geek-Nerdling that I actually am. Oh well... When you have this laptop, who needs a girlfriend?!? Not me! :-p Now back to p3wning n00bz with a bag of Doritos and a case of beer! ... Which reminds me, don't use alcohol to clean this thing, it will slowly eat the rubberized coating on the keys. Use this stuff instead (trust me, it's the right product): [[ASIN:B000AMLWH8 Meguiar's G13616 Quik Interior Detailer Cleaner - 16 oz.]]

The machine lacks a DVD/BD drive. Obviously, these are not as relevant as they used to be, but there are still plenty of games that arrive on DVD. You'll be doing a lot of large downloads of Steam.

title_x: A fantastic notebook at a great price (for Advance)
text:
Ok, I've had this for almost 2 months and I'm ready to write a review.

I'll cut to the chase, I love this notebook and would highly recommend it, but I'm not giving it 5 stars and this is why.

It has 2 video cards, but not in the classic "Advance" way in which you've got 2 matched gpu's in a crossfire or sli interface, it instead has a nice nvidea gpu and an integrated pos Intel display. It "switches" to the nvidea display when it needs the performance, and it uses the Intel chip the rest of the time. There is no way to completely not use the Intel chip and only use the nvidea card.

I assume they did this to extend battery life, but lets face it, if you've got a 17" Advance, you didn't buy it to carry on a plane with you, battery life is not really the reason for having this beast. There are drawbacks of having the Intel chip at all, the biggest of which seems to be that the HDMI port is dedicated to the Intel chip, so if I'm using an external hdmi display and I want to play a game which wants to use the nvidea gpu, everything goes bonky and it doesn't work. I've since learned but haven't tested that the Thunderbolt output may be tied directly to the nvidea gpu, so if I get an HDMI adapter for it, I may be able to do it that way, but since I don't have that adapter yet, I'm annoyed that I can't use an external display. If they simply had a way of disabling the Intel display completely if you don't care about battery life (or when it's plugged in), then this would be 5 stars.

The only other negative I have is that for whatever reason the soundblaster sound card in this does not switch automatically between speakers and headsets when you plug them in or unplug them. You have to run the soundblaster control app and manually switch them. I have never seen another notebook that needs this, it's really kind of a pain in the butt, but it's manageable.

Now, as far as everything else goes, my last Advance notebook was a M17x-r2 with crossfire HD4xxx ati video cards. Even though it was a great notebook for it's time, I still did not really ever use it as a "gaming" platform. The cards just weren't enough to match my desktop and it would get so hot it would start to burn you if you had it on your lap while the fans would become really loud. Plus, while they tried hard with the aluminum casing to try and dissipate the heat, it just wasn't as good as it, and the video cards would cook, and mobile video cards don't depreciate much in value so they're very expensive to replace.

This notebook on the other hand is the first notebook I've every really enjoyed playing games on. It's kind of nice to be able to sit in my comfy chair in the living room while my wife is watching something I don't want to and being able to play a game with the headphones on and not having to go down to the basement to my desktop.

I'm very happy with the feel of it, the look of it, and the performance of it. Plus, I got it for a whole lot less since it's last years model, even though the specs are almost identical to this years model except for the one year older video card. Since I'm not playing games at 4K, this card works great and I'm very happy with it.

title_x: Once You Fix Some Issues It's A Preety Decent Laptop
text:
I bought this laptop recently and I was really looking forward to enjoying improved performance. It was used for about 3 months (before I bought it) and then reset to factory settings. It had been upgraded to 16gb of RAM and a 2tb hard drive using parts purchased from FusionTech. I found it to be slower than my 6 year old dual core laptop. The boot time was slow but what was more irritating was program launches taking from 20 seconds to 2 minutes. The laptop also froze up randomly several times per hour. I determined that the system was only seeing 8gb of RAM so I opened the case and re-seated the memory sticks. This enabled it to see all 16gb of RAM but didn't seem to make any difference in the performance. I made adjustments to power settings, loaded the latest BIOS and drivers, etc. but it was still slow. I discovered that FusionTech's 2tb HDD was a 5400 rpm drive so I reverted to the original 1tb (7200 rpm) drive but it was still slow. I was really getting irritated so I disabled its on board Intel graphics to force it to use the nVidia card. That helped enough that I purchased a USB Blu-ray burner to be able to watch my DVD collection (and load some software). The sound from the speakers is weak and muffled when trying to listen to DVD's but it's a little better with iTunes. The sound quality/volume is much worse than my seven year old Asus laptop. Note: the latest drivers seem to have fixed most of the audio volume issue and the quality is a bit better too. As a final step, I purchased and installed a SanDisk 960gb SATA SSD to replace the FusionTech (Hitachi?) HDD. Now the laptop performs fairly well (without the freeze up problems) but it's still not exceptionally fast. To be fair, some of these problems could have been caused by the "factory reset" and upgrades done by the original owner but, so far, I can't say that I'm very impressed.

Follow-up: I originally gave this laptop a 3 star rating but now I'd say it's more like a 3.5 star rating. The latest driver updates resolved some issues. Hard drive performance was mediocre but I always assumed I'd upgrade to an SSD. Removed WiFi and installed the Killer WiFi drivers from their web site and now WiFi (and Bluetooth) is stable. Had to purchase EaseUS to get a working backup product.

Pros:
. RAM and HDD are easily upgraded
. Tech Support has been a little better than average
. Internal temps seem reasonable
. Keyboard lighting is adjustable

Cons:
. Out-Of-the-Box experience was challenging
. Performance as delivered was unimpressive
. Disabled on-board graphics to force it to use nVidia since DVD playback was freezing. By default, it seems to rely on the Intel on-board graphics too much
. Transferring ownership wasn't as smooth as expected but, after several attempts. it is done
. Bluetooth connectivity has failed three times in the first few weeks
. Unable to create a system/data backup with either AlienRespawn or Windows 10 Backup

title_x: Dont Blame WIndows 10 Issues On Advance
text:
After I finished moping about the fried logic board in my MacBook Pro, I began looking for a replacement laptop. What attracted me to the Advance 17 R3 was the design and the crystal clear screen. This is a BIG laptop. I could place a cup on the keyboard area and still have enough space to type comfortably. The design is awesome. The capability to customize the backlight colors of the keyboard, power button, indicator lights, etc. is a nice touch. Another plus for me was the amount of hard drive storage space. My previous laptop had a 500GB hard drive so this met my needs since there is over 1 TB of storage space. Before I purchased, I did some research and saw reviewers complaining about the intermittent WiFi connectivity and overheating. I felt those were minor issues and purchased anyway. I will say...when connected to WiFi EVERYTIME I closed the laptop I had to manually reconnect to WiFI again. It was a PITA. I did some research and there was a fix published in the forum which involved uninstalling drivers and updating to new ones. I did that and the issue was resolved. There was also a power saving setting set on the driver program which I disabled. As for the overheating, I use my laptop on my lap and its a little warm but not to the point where I can bake cookies on it as some reviewers stated. I am sure you've read this in the specs but it's worth mentioning again there is no CD/DVD drive. Not a big deal to me but to others it may matter.

Something that frustrated me when I first purchased this laptop was the issues I was having with Windows 10. I feel this is important because the laptop comes with Windows 10 pre-installed and to my knowledge there is no way to downgrade to Windows 8 or 7 (for free). So as cool as the hardware and specs are on this laptop, it doesn't override the need for a functional operating system. I understand this is an Advance review and not a Microsoft one but I feel it's worth mentioning the issues I've had with the operating system since it comes default with the laptop. The issues below all occurred in the first 7 days of ownership.

Windows 10 has live tiles which are also programs used for opening pictures, emails, etc. I don't know what happened but I was no longer able to access the applications referenced below. In fact I couldn't open the Windows 10 store at all. I tried many online suggestions from Mircrosoft to resolve but was unsuccessful. Upgrading the operating system also didn't resolve this issue. I ended up doing a hard reset. Since I just purchased the laptop this wasn't that big of a deal. The reset resolved this issue.

On another occasion, I received a "KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE" BSOD error. After several attempts to restart, I kept getting the same error. I ended up booting in recovery mode and restored the operating system. Thankfully there was a backup from about 12 hours prior so that version of the operating system was reinstalled and I've had no further issues.

In conclusion, this is a great laptop. A selling point other companies throw out there is how thin and light their laptop is. If that's what you are looking for this is not for you. This thing is a BEHEMOTH but it's top quality and "appears" to be able to withstand a drop or two. All the specs are top notch and I am pleased with the laptop so far. The only reason I rated 4 instead of 5 stars is because it shipped with such a buggy operating system.

title_x: this thing is striking in a lot of bad ways. First let me say that this weighs ...
text:
I got handed on of these today at the office so I could set it up for the user who only got it because of their obsession with extended keyboards. Since I usually buy my people MacBook Pros or Airs, this thing is striking in a lot of bad ways. First let me say that this weighs a ton. I honestly think it is the heaviest laptop I've ever handled. Beyond that, it is crazy thick and the bottom is covered in deep ridges that make actually having this thing on your lap a bit uncomfortable. Despite its weight and thickness, it isn't very rigid. With a little torsional force on the sides, I could feel it flexing.

The trackpad is terrible. There really isn't any way around that. It isn't smooth to the touch, it is tiny and glossing over the fact that it still even has buttons, the actual buttons are horrid. Rubberized and squishy with poor placement. The backlight on the trackpad actually had me impressed for a second when I thought it was a touch display but no... Just backlit for no reason. Most users probably won't find it as annoying as me but the stupidity of a backlit trackpad just irked me every time I touched it.

The display for its touted resolution is not very good. I'm sure it is technically capable of 4K but the pixels are poorly constrained so there is bleeding between high contrast colors. This makes font sizes that are very easy to read on the lower resolution 15" MacBook retina nearly illegible. Due to the poor contrast, it is probably functionally better than a 1080p display of the same size but not by much.

Last but not least, it is buggy at the hardware level. I had to reboot three times while I was getting it configured and found the post to be really inconsistent in speed. At one point when I was close to having finished configuring it, it just popped "Restarting" on the display for no reason and when it came back up it took over 5 minutes to post. I ended up setting it down so I could go work on something else so I'm not sure how long it took but it was unacceptably long.

There aren't PC laptops that have anything like Mac build quality but some come reasonably close. This isn't one of them.

title_x: The Advance AW17R3 - A Superb Computer Plus It's Not Just for Gaming!
text:
First, let me state that I am not a 'gamer.'

Then why am I reviewing this [[ASIN:B015P3SO22 Advance AW17R3-7092SLV 17.3" FHD Laptop (6th Generation Intel Core i7, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD + 1 TB HDD) NVIDIA GeForce GTX980M]]?

It was offered to me by Amazon Vine™ and, as soon as I saw it, I ordered it.

I ordered it because I know that gaming computers are extremely powerful machines and would be suitable for the type of audio and video work that I like to do. I use several programs for these purposes as well as some photography ones. Some of those programs use a lot, sometimes almost all, of a computer's CPU power.

This one does not disappoint. It has just about all the processing power anyone would need. And everything on it runs FAST!

It does run a bit warm (not hot) but so did (and does) every other laptop computer I have ever used with these programs. The very large and heavy power supply runs warm too.

Normally I use the openSUSE (GNU/Linux) operating system but, for the time being, I shall use this computer as it is, with its Microsoft Windows 10 system, for some months just to make certain that there are no problems which might need warranty work.

After I am sure that nothing untoward is going to occur, I shall convert it to openSUSE..

In the meantime, there are several programs I use which are cross-platform. In other words these programs have versions for Windows, Mac, as well as GNU/Linux systems.

So far, I have installed just a couple of them. One, in its Windows version, is about equivalent to its GNU/Linux counterpart; the other is noticeably inferior (or, as we used to say, "Crude but Usable").

Both programs work well and both work much faster than they do on my "old" (2012 - ancient in computer terms!) laptop (which also has an Intel i7 processor [an older version] and 16 GB of RAM). It too runs very fast but its speed pales compared to this new Advance computer. (I'm sure that when it is converted to openSUSE, it will run even faster. All things being equal on a given computer, GNU/Linux OSes generally run much faster than Windows or Mac OSes.)

I moved all of the data folders (Documents, Music, Pictures, and Videos) to the D-drive (1 TB, 7200 RPM) which, as the computer comes from the factory, are installed on the C-drive (256 GB SSD). (Why isn't this placement done by Advance?)

I added some Internet Radio Station URLs to the Music folder, downloaded the K-Lite codec package, and played a couple of Internet Radio Stations.

It's certainly not ' ultra high fidelity,' but the sound which emanates from this computer is absolutely the very best I have ever heard from a laptop's built-in speakers. Nothing else that I have ever heard is even close!

The graphics are excellent. Plus there are adjustments to the colors on the keyboard and on the lid and body and they can be very 'cool' if you like that sort of thing.

I had what turned out to be a very minor problem: when I received the computer on May 12, 2016, the AC cord which plugs into the transformer had the wrong connectors. It had round holes while the transformer had blade connectors.

As I learned many years ago, you can't put a square peg into a round hole, so I called Advance/FusionTech. Fortunately I had registered the computer (using my older computer) even before I tried to attach the power supply. So when I spoke with a representative, he already had my information at hand.

He asked me to send him pictures so he could show his supervisor the problem.

I did so - and so did he.

He telephoned me within fifteen minutes of receiving those pictures (you can view these pictures below) and, believe it or not, he promised to FedEx Overnight the right cord to me - and he did! It arrived the next day. I couldn't have asked for better service from a computer vendor

I then turned on the computer, went through Microsoft's 'registration' procedure, and started using it.

The keyboard is very well-designed and is a pleasure to use. So is the large trackpad. The 'feel' is just right, at least for me, and I anticipate no fatigue. The display is superb, bright and colorful. (I downloaded and installed a number of Advance HD backdrops.) And, as I mentioned above, everything for which I use it runs FAST, much faster than any other computer I own or have previously owned.

Is it 'perfect?' Of course not. What computer (or anything else) is?

For me, there are three very minor 'nits' - the computer is very heavy (nothing to be done about that) and it has no internal optical drive (can be remedied with an inexpensive external Blu-ray/DVD/CD reader/writer). In addition, it has only three standard USB 3.0 ports (can be remedied with an inexpensive USB 3.0 hub).

But these are very minor points, at least in my opinion, and two of them are easily 'fixed.' (I already have disc reader/writers and hubs.) And my minor complaints may not even be applicable for you.

I'm sure that you can guess by now that I am very pleased with this laptop! I'm very, very happy that Amazon Vine™ chose to offer it to me as I had been planning to replace my 2012 computer (as always, money being a problem!). I shall (hopefully) make good use of this one's very powerful capabilities. I'm sure that it will be even more capable when it is converted to openSUSE, though this probably would not apply to the majority of people reading this review.

So, in conclusion, let me state that, if you need an advanced powerful laptop computer for a variety of resource-intensive uses and also desire excellent graphics and superb sound quality, I believe that this one is one of the best choices available. (I'm also sure that it would be great for gaming!) And if my experience with Advance/FusionTech's service department is any indication, the company stands behind its products, is an easy one with which to deal, and is anxious to please its customers.

Thus I highly recommend this laptop computer.

Thank you for reading this and for considering my opinions.

Lawrence H. Bulk

=====Update: Monday, July 25, 2016

Yesterday I 'wiped' the supplied Microsoft Windows 10 operating system from this computer and replaced it with the openSUSE 'Tumbleweed' (rolling release - a 'permanent' system which 'never' needs to be upgraded) operating system.

As I expected, this computer as well as all its installed programs now operate much faster than previously when it used Windows.

I certainly do not expect many people to do what I did - get rid of Windows and replace it with a GNU/Linux operating system - but if anyone reading this desires to do so, it is quite easy. The openSUSE system will install with UEFI activated; Secure Boot must be deactivated.

Again I thank you for reading this.

Lawrence

title_x: Awesome laptop that runs like a dream
text:
I did a lot of research before buying this laptop and for the cost (right now a new one is about 1350$) your not going to find much better. I had an ASUS ROG before buying this that I had been using for 6 years (ROG's are great laptops as well by the way), but I decided to pull the trigger on the Advance mainly because of the Gforce 970m it had under the hood. First off its a great looking laptop, with one of the best screens I have ever used on a laptop. The resolution is great and the keyboard layout is nice and works well for gaming. It does heat up a bit where the underside fans are so if its sitting on your lap its going to get a bit warm, but that's nothing you can't solve with a cooling pad, or just putting it on something harder. The video card is awesome and I am having no problems running things on ultra settings (battlefleet gothic, vermintide, just to name a few). I bought the entry level R17 with 8gig of ram and a 1tb 7200 hd, which was fine. However right out of the box I installed 16 gig of ram (the laptop has 2 expansion bays so you can put in 2x4gig or 2x8, 2x16 gig for a max of 32gig) and put in a samsug 850 evo 250 gb m.2 in one of the expansion slots for much cheaper than it is to order those things from FusionTech. I also did a fresh windows install over to that ssd and now this thing flies. The one frustrating thing is finding a screw to hold the ssd down (you need an m2xl3, or in other words a screw that has a 2mm thread that is 3mm long). I went over to best buy and asked the geek squad guys for one and they let me look through their loose laptop screws and just take a few for free. Do yourself a favor though and pull out one of the screws that holds the back panel on to use as a guide (they are also the right size to hold that ssd down). After those few upgrades this thing is a total monster and I am looking forward to using this laptop for years to come. I would recommend that you update the bios from FusionTech though, and update the network card drivers to avoid some of the other problems people have had with this laptop. I did not have any problems with mine, but I updated them still just in case. Both of which can be found on FusionTech's website for download. If you do a clean install of windows onto your new ssd make sure to update the video drivers as well for the Gforce970m (or 980m if you get the better model) from Nvidia. I will update this review in a few months to report back on how this baby is running, but I expect no problems.
(Updated 5/27/16)
I am still very very happy with this laptop almost 2 months later. I have had no problems with it and it makes me happy every time I hit the power button and within 4 seconds its up and running. One thing that I did not mention before is that the lights on it can be changed to any color you want, or you can have each area (there are about 9) different colors if you want. I don't game in the dark, or do big network parties like in my younger days, but my kids get a kick out of it as I change the colors around. I broke down and put another ssd in the extra port (500gig this time) and I am installing all my steam stuff there now. Everything loads up fast and runs great. One thing I did notice that I commented on a bit, is that the bottom of the computer gets a bit hot, but also the keyboard itself will get a bit warm. This had not ever been a problem for me and I use a cooling pad but thought I would mention it so no one is surprised.

title_x: It's a tragedy what Advance has become.
text:
I bought a 17" laptop from FusionTech. I got every single hardware upgrade and I even got the extended warranty. After 7 months, the screen started going bad and I had to get service. A bit later, the system wasn't working quite right and I needed some more service done (I've got 20+ years experience in the IT field) and that went south, with the screen going completely out less than a month later. They required me to send the laptop in for service. I use my laptop for work, so I replaced the laptop with another and have let my wife use this laptop since then.

Three months after that previous service, she hadn't used it for several weeks and when she went to verify the battery level before going on a trip, it wouldn't boot up. I called FusionTech and honestly wanted a credit for what I spent on this, but they insisted and sent someone out to replace the motherboard. Well, he replaced the motherboard and when he was done, the motherboard had a password on that they couldn't reset (they sent a bad motherboard).

I've had this thing serviced four times in 14 months. They want me to have it serviced a fifth time. I simply wanted them to give me something else, as when something goes bad five times, it's clearly a lemon. They won't do anything but give me the exact same thing again. I've let them know that I need them to talk to my lawyer, who is pursuing a refund through the court system now.

In the last six to seven years I've bought twelve laptops, between work, my wife and my kids. I have had exactly one that needed service. In the twenty plus years of owning laptop computers, I've only had six instances where I needed service - five were on this Advance laptop. I will likely buy twelve to twenty more laptops in the next six years.

I can tell you that nothing I buy for the rest of my life will be FusionTech or a FusionTech owned brand like Advance. At the place I work, they just replaced thousands of laptops with FusionTechs. I've never seen a failure rate so high and a company so completely in denial about their issues. They blamed issues on everything from the Windows load to the users, even though the issues were consistent and repeating at very high frequency. It's unconscionable the way they behaved.

I bought Advance to get the best of the best. I got a pile of junk. Save yourself, avoid Advance and anything else by FusionTech.

I was not sure whether or not I should buy this laptop,
but I got tired of comparing laptops for so many hours so I said, "Screw this, I am just buying this awesome looking laptop."
I love it so far although I experienced some issues with Wireless Network driver and adapter.

3. Fast booting & loading speed for the HDD

Con:
1. Heavy compared to other laptops
2. Gets really hot when playing games
3. Software isn't the best (I suffered from Internet driver & Wireless network adapter issues)
4. Short battery life (But I guess this is the same as any other gaming laptops)

I don't carry this laptop around that much so I have no issue with it being heavy. Also I lift, so it's no big deal for me.
Here are my TIPS to improve this laptop (tips for the cons).
1) Get a cooling pad for the laptop, it's only $25~35 on Amazon. This cooled down my cpu temperature from 75~88C to 65~78C when playing games. It cooled down my cpu temp from 40~60C to 25~50C when not playing games.
2) Just in case your laptop's wireless adapter goes stupid, download and keep the most recent network driver from FusionTech Support. Restart your laptop if something goes wrong, and if it still doesn't fix it, try this: Uninstall the existing driver, reboot, then re-download, and reboot it again. That's how I solved it.

To sum up, I strongly recommend you this product if you don't mind getting a cooling pad for gaming and know how to fix the internet issue.

text:
Edit 2/07/16
I want to thank amazon for their amazing service. And thank you so much for awarding my years of loyal amazon shopping! The rating of one star reflects my bad first impression with this faulty unit. But thanks to amazon, I'm not throwing in the towel so easy. 5 stars to amazing customer service.

Original review:
2/05/2016
I'm going to post an update of my experience with this laptop every day as it happens, as opposed to one large review. Wish me luck.

On Wednesday (two days ago) I ordered this beauty - the Advance AW17R3-8342SLV - with the highest possible expectations. (Intel Quad Core i7-6700HQ 2.6 GHz Processor - 16 GB DDR4 - 1 TB HDD + 256 GB SSD Storage; 17.3 Inch UHD (3840 x 2160 pixels) LED-lit Truelife Screen).

It arrived quicker than expected, like 1.75 days (THANKS AMAZON!). This laptop really is gorgeous! However, right off the bat we have issues. It takes 2 minutes to boot up after a restart. Tons of google troubleshooting. It's a known issue.

Fix: Device Manger > Sensor I/O Devices > Update Kionic KXCNL Freefall Sensor. After that it takes more like 20 seconds to start. Don't start updating all your drivers willy nilly, however. I updated the Display adapters > Intel(R) HD Graphics 530 and immediate started getting a black screen and the error: "Display driver stopped responding and has recovered." Are you kidding me?! I just bought this laptop for over $2000.

Bummer. I wanted to like this laptop so bad. Call a FusionTech customer service rep for Advance support. Immediately treated like a prospect to be milked for cash. A woman is intrusively presses for email, phone number, first and last. Tries to tell me if I don't buy a premium warranty now, it would cost $800 for a 4 year warranty in a few weeks. What the?? I just need help with my computer!! I hang up in frustration.

I uninstall the Intel Driver that I updated, restarted, then reinstalled the driver from FusionTech here: [...]driverId=XP2MM&fileId=3488566979&osCode=WT64A&productCode=Advance-17-r3&languageCode=EN&categoryId=VI

"Display driver stopped responding and has recovered." has not popped up and no black screen glitches for the last 2 hours. Whew!! Approximately 3 hours after first powering on this laptop, I"m able install Steam and try to play a game. I launch the new game Rise of the Tomb Raider. While it's loading,a strange interference noise cackles from the left speaker. That noise is immediately drowned out a buzzing like a fan thats possibly at the wrong angle, a teeny buzzing mechanical failure noise. It sounds like a tiny lawnmower. At high settings, the game chugs along at 17fps.

I turn off the game and come here to write my first Amazon review.

I'm not sure the cause of all this. The FusionTech woman had told me to only buy FusionTech, because Amazon buys the Advance 17R3s in bulk, and they all have outdated firmware and software. Maybe she's wrong. Maybe it's a compatibility issue with Windows 10 and something else on this Super-Laptop. Maybe the SSD, graphics card, drivers, and speakers are faulty. Maybe I got another lemon. Whatever it is, I have a sore brain and eyeballs, a bitter taste in my mouth with FusionTech.

Pros: Keys are springier and more amazing than any I've used anywhere. The screen is discernibly sharp. The startup is 5 seconds. The restart is 20. It plays the original Bioshock at 60 fps.

Just another reviewer here said, It's not work the risk. I'm returning this gorgeous laptop tomorrow. I'm so dissapointed in FusionTech and my first attempt at purchasing an Advance. I really went out on a limb there and was sorely let down.

title_x: AMAZING LAPTOP, NOW THAT I HAVE THE BUGS WORKED OUT.
text:
Received my Advance 17 R3 a few days ago.
Build quality is great, it feels very sturdy.
Keyboard and touch-pad are some of the best I've ever used on a laptop.
Screen is gorgeous, and the video card is running all my game at high or ultra settings, just like I had hoped.
It doesn't run overly hot, even while gaming.
Battery is decent for a rig this powerful, of this size. I get about 4 hours out of it before I have to plug it in, while gaming (almost all I do).
I suspect it would last longer if I wasn't gaming so much.
In short, this laptop is everything you expect a high quality, top of the line (or close to it), rig to be.
EXCEPT...
I had LOADS of IRQ, BIOS and Driver issues out of the box.
Crashes, blue screens, conflicts...
I spent a day updating and troubleshooting various problems, updating practically ALL my drivers, the BIOS...
I wont go into all of it here, because there was a lot, and these sort of issues will be different with each computer, so a lengthy explanation wouldn't be useful, with one exception.
I had the exact same problem as tons of other people with the Killer Wireless dropping signal constantly.
Seriously, do a search, it's a VERY common problem with this laptop.
After spending some time researching the issue (which will generate a lot of possible solutions), and trying several "fixes" to no avail. I downloaded the newest Killer Network Manager from their website, then uninstalled both the existing suite AND the existing killer wireless drivers. Then I installed the newest version of the Killer Network Manager (which includes drivers). This fixed the issue. I have gone several days now with no Wireless issues. NOTE: be sure to DL the newest version BEFORE you uninstall everything or you won't be able to get online to DL it!

Long story short, after spending a couple days updating, uninstalling and reinstalling, and a 2 hours on the phone with Advance to fix a few issues that updating drivers wouldn't fix, I now have an amazing laptop that runs perfect, and is everything I had hoped it would be.
Having to do all that work was a pain in the ass for sure, but it shouldn't be a deal breaker. None of the problems were defective hardware, etc.

As someone who is fairly tech-savvy, and someone who spent months researching before pulling the trigger on this purchase, I still feel that this laptop represents the best value at this price-point.

title_x: Great on paper, terrible in person. : /
text:
*Update Update*

Amazon acknowledged the issue with this unit, then promptly offered a full refund for an item that was three months past the return period. The refund went through less than a week, absolutely amazing customer service.

*Update*
I'm worse than disappointed. The board completely failed only two months later, starting with the primary M.2 slot, then the fans, then the whole system. Done.

I sent it to Advance for a motherboard replacement, which actually was a relatively speedy process, to say something positive. But come to find out, they used an inferior legacy/previous generation motherboard as a "solution". WHAT THE H?!!! Seriously, a 2014 model. I basically have an R2 in an R3 chassis.

Stay away if you know what's good for you.

Advance is terrible.

*Original post*
I'm very disappointed with this purchase... I bought this beast in hope that I wouldn't have to upgrade for quite some time, yet I'm about to return a second faulty unit in less than a week.

To start - both had firmware issues, and both had driver problems right out of the box. And on top of that, both had physical hardware issues.

The first had an issue with the BIOS, and with the free fall sensor as well, which caused it to take almost three minutes to boot. I fixed it by flashing the firmware, switching from RAID to AHCI, then updating all of my devices via device manager.

Boot time was then about ten seconds, as it should have been in the first place.

The next issue was with the right physical click button, in which it wouldn't detect pressure correctly. You had to press extremely hard, and exactly in the middle for it to work. Which doesn't sound like the end of the world, but became quite frustrating almosy immediately—especially since it is a $2,000+ machine.

Anyhow, I then ordered a replacement when I realized that I couldn't fix the track pad without voiding my warranty. It came unusually quickly, which was nice, though I hadn't even had time to ship the other one back...

I then went through the same exact problem that I had with the first one! BIOS was a mess, and the drivers were corrupt. Well fast forward a few hours, and I've sorted it all out as with the first. I then try to make a call with Skype... No camera! I spent the entire day attempting a solution, only to succumb to the realization that it is physically disconnected. No amount of driver tampering will touch it. Vah!!!

For such a high end model, you would think that you could just turn it on and be ready to go, this is certainly not the case unfortunately.

text:
I have read alot of reviews complaining about problems galore with their Advance laptop. However after recieving mine I'm happy to report that there was absolutely nothing wrong with mine, maybe I'm lucky or maybe they other people citing problems were overclocking or doing other things that risk damaging their laptop. I inspected my laptop closely and found no dead or bright pixels, no scratches or blemishes anywhere. And when i turned it on there were no problems booting, or bugs or crashes or slowness (do note my order was fulfilled by amazon). The only funny thing i ran into is that Star citizen was not recognized by nvidia so Star citizen would use intel graphics resulting in really low frames. To fix this just go into the nvidia control panel and add the game in the right pane, then in the dropdown box select "High-Performance NVIDIA processor" after doing this star citizen runs awesome on this laptop.
anyhoo for the actual review.

The chassis:
I was immediately impressed with how solid this laptop felt in my hand, it felt like a macbook. The outside is aluminum and the finish is superb, second to none. The hinge feels solid and I haven't experienced any flexing or creaking. The unit is hefty but not particularly heavy when in my backpack, after cleaning out a little junk in my backpack it feels great for carrying around. I wouldn't carry it long distances in a briefcase but a messenger bag would be fine. The interior is relatively tame with flat plastic on both sides of the interior. This isn't regular plastic but instead that soft almost rubbery feeling plastic (it's not grippy like rubber though). The keyboard feels excellent and has a little more actuation force than my mechanical keyboard with Cherry switches but it's not too hard to press that I think I will wear myself out typing alot. The trackpad is gorgeous and the best trackpad I've ever used (I haven't tried other high end computers trackpads but this is leagues better than other mid to low end laptops).
The Backlighting on the keyboard is really cool and really useful at night. During the day you can turn off the keyboard backlighting because the keys are white print during the day so you can read them like any other keyboard.

Performance:
This pc's performance is amazing. I was able to run star citizen on the highest settings getting 35-50 fps @ 1080p and this game isn't even that optimized yet. All my other games run at the highest settings @ 1080p no problem. it does produce alot of heat but the fans aren't too loud and they have a good sound to them (not an annoying whine but a calm whooshing sound when they ramp up). Games like league of legends dont even get the fans going and not playing games this computer is silent as death, you literally can't hear it when your not playing games.
The hard drive that came with this computer is unacceptable for such high end hardware and i recommend you get a Samsung 850 EVO when you buy this computer. I was able to replace this computers harddrive with a solid state and did a fresh install. The process i took that had no problems is as follows.
1) go to [...] and use that to make a bootable usb drive
2) swap out the old hard drive with a solid state (i used a 2.5" sata instead of m2)
3) power on the computer and follow the normal windows installation
4) go to [...]=drivers and download and install the drivers, the general principle is first install the chipset drivers, then install the networking drivers (Lan and wifi), then sound driver and video drivers (i got my video driver from nvidia.com instead). Then last but not least the Advance specific programs (command center, airplane switch, onscreen). Windows will automatically activate so you dont enter a product key (the product key is fetched from the motherboard automatically)
after doing this I had this baby purring like a kitten, no crashes, no bsods, no problems. then i just installed some games and they ran fine.

display:
This display is pretty good, i got the 1080P one. The colors are clear and accurate and the matte finish is good to reduce glare. The viewing angle is reasonable, just so so. It gets quiet bright and should work excellent in an office setting, and better than average in daylight (due to matte screen). I personally recommend getting the 1080p version instead of the 4k because windows has poor scaling and 1080p is about the highest resolution that you can do no scaling and see everything fine. Instead buy an external 4k display so you can get a nice large one. However I have read good things about the model with the 4k screen.

Sound:
The speakers are by Klipsch and it has two speakers on the front and a subwoofer on the bottem so it's a 2.1 system. The sound is great for a laptop, the woofer adds base but isn't dubstep by any means, the front speakers are clear and can get reasonably loud but they aren't a bose stereo system. However the real gem in this machine is it's Creative X-FI sound card, THIS IS A BIG DEAL! I've used creative sound cards before and they are the best when it comes to a sound card, realtec is nothing compared to creative. The number one feature of creative is their "crystalizer" what this does is restore sound fidelity lost due to compression, I like to turn this thing up to 100% but you can tweak it to anything inbetween. The crystalizer feature makes music and sound go from sounding like it came through a telephone, to sounding like your really there at the stage, or by that person. To experience this get nice headphones or earbuds with the standard 3.5mm connector NOT USB, if you get usb then the sound will be through their driver and you'll miss out on the ear heaven that is creative X-FI. Also I recommend turning ON the 3d surround when using the laptop speakers but TURN IT OFF for headphones when your listening to music.

also the creative sound card filters out background noise if you turn that feature on and I say turn it on. My room sounded like a warzone off my speakers, but all my friends hear out of the built in michrophone is my voice, nice and clear. The built in microphone is superb but if you want an external microphone make sure it is 3.5mm standard connector and not usb for the same reason as stated above.

Battery life:
This thing has crazy good battery life, which is unheard of with gaming laptops. Mind you if you play games on this you may get 2-3 hours depending on how demanding the game is. Where the battery life really shines is when your using the intel graphics instead. You can expect 6 hours (or maybe even a little more) doing things like web browsing, watching 1080p moves, programming, word documents email etc.

conclusion:
I'm a computer science major and I got this laptop because although i like small ultralight pc's I hate having a slow computer and moreso I hate having a tiny screen when most of my day is spent writing and reading code. This screen is excellent for this purpose because I can do a split view where my code editor is on one side and google chrome on the other (all coders are google addicts lol). I also have to run a linux virtual machine so i can test that my code compiles on it and this computer works great with vmware (I wouldn't recommend trying to boot linux as the host operating system because of not having drivers for this hardware). I also like playing games and this baby does that too. All in all i think this computer works great for my uses, the battery life is great, the hardware is top notch, and the quality and aesthetics make you smile when this is what you get to use for your day.

My previous two gaming laptops have been ASUS, since they seem to offer the most bang per buck (even if they're not top of the line), but decided to splurge and buy Advance after some saving and a nice tax rebate. I regret that decision.
First the good: the laptop is plenty powerful, so serves it's purpose as a high power gaming computer. But...
After only a year and two months the internal hardware burnt itself out, bricking it. Naturally the warranty is only year, and FusionTech's repair services are ludicrously expensive. I ended up having it fixed by a local computer repair shop for half the price FusionTech customer service quoted me. By comparison, both my ASUS laptops still work well, even if the hardware is outdated for gaming (they're now in the possession of some family members who wanted to replace very old desktop computers).
I don't know if I'm just unlucky, but I don't think I'll be sticking with Advance products in the future.
