I've owned a variety of gaming laptops in the past (ASUS, MSI) and this by far is the highest quality. I would say the overall build quality is 90% as good as an Apple. The chassis feels extremely durable and rigid (it's constructed from aluminum and carbon fiber). The keyboard is a 10/10, and the lighting is a lot of fun. I do a good amount of remote work for my job, and this machine has not only been reliable, but it's been a pleasure to work on.

With an i7, 16gb of ram, and a fast 1.2 gb/s SSD, I blow through productivity tasks. This machine paired with the multitasking enhancements built into Windows 10 is wonderful. Work is great and all, but I'm also a gamer (one of the reasons I moved away from a Mac to this).

Gaming wise it's solid. You'll be able to play most AAA titles at high or ultra settings. There are some circumstances where it's better to run the game at medium quality (Fallout 4 for example). For specs , I recommend checking out [...].

The biggest gripe that i have is with the Killer wifi, as it kept disconnecting. The fix was pretty easy, uninstall the card from hardware manager, grab the latest Killer drivers, then reinstall. Not terrible, but wireless internet should be working flawlessly on a high end machine in 2016.

Overall, if you are looking for a laptop that can do medium to heavy gaming, fairly portable (not an ultrabook, but not a 17 inch behemoth), long battery life (5-7 hours doing basic stuff), and is top notch quality, this is a great machine.

title_x: Excellent performance, sketchy quality control (Updated 18 April 2016)
text:
Specs and performance: Fantastic.
- Laptop runs cool and quiet during normal use and has no issues playing BF4 or Titanfall on High Settings. I'm prefer stability/longevity vs quality, so I rarely run games at the highest settings even with robust hardware.
- The sound quality is FANTASTIC for a laptop, with great directional surround at even normal volume. I am very impressed.
- Also, this laptop comes with minimal bloatware. There are a few Advance programs to manage WiFi and the keyboard backlight configuration (TONS of customization possible there), but I was happy that I didn't have to completely wipe it or spend hours uninstalling useless nonsense like with most laptops.
- The screen is adequate with minimal glare due to the semi-matte screen. Some will complain about lack of 4k on this laptop, but this GPU would have problems handling it anyways and it would just degrade battery life, which isn't a priority for me but definitely desirable for the few times I have to go truly mobile.
- Speaking of which, I was also impressed with the battery life. I regularly get 5+ hours on the "balanced" plan doing normal browsing/writing and about 3 hours of gaming, which is worlds better than any other "gaming" laptop I've owned. I don't know if a bigger battery is available, but I'll probably consider getting one later on.
- The keyboard itself has great feedback and is comfortable to use, but takes some getting used to with the row of dedicated hotkeys on the left side and the lack of a numerical pad on the right. I'm a little disappointed that the number pad wasn't included (and it's not an issue of real estate, my last 15" laptop had plenty of room for the number pad), but I also understand the "gaming" angle of this machine, so it's not a dealbreaker.
- Opening the lid on this thing requires two hands because the hinge is "stiff" and the front edge slopes away from you, so you can't just lift the lid without holding the bottom down and doing so takes some concentration if you're in a hurry. It gets a little annoying at times, but I suppose that's preferable to having a limp, floppy screen that doesn't stay where you put it.

Suggestions:

- DEFINITELY put an SSD in this and run the OS from that. Initially everything is lickety split during reboots and normal use, but a few weeks later my reboots went from acceptable to painful at over 3 minutes. All of my desktops have SSDs in them and I'd forgotten just how much faster they really are compared to a HDD, 7200RPM or not. Just remember that this laptop requires the m.2 SSD interface, not the standard 2.5" form. The slot is empty and ready for the SSD, so you don't even have to lose the 1TB storage.
- Also, it comes with a single stick of 8GB DDR4 with an open slot available from the get-go, so I'll definitely be throwing in some more RAM once I know this is worth keeping to get that dual-channel speed bonus.
- Make sure you go into the Nvidia control panel and force Firefox (if you use it) to use the video card instead of the integrated Intel graphics (the default). I had multiple driver failures within minutes of using Firefox with Intel, which is a real shame since the integrated graphics conserve the battery and can easily handle nearly anything in a browser. I initially tried to just uninstall the Intel graphics altogether since I didn't plan on using it, but that left me with no video at all (which I should have anticipated).

Quality: This is where I ran into an issue. The top of my screen had obvious bleeding. You can only see it on a black screen (such as during reboot), but it is very obvious and would be a major distraction during dark portions of games, videos and pictures. I was going to ignore the issue since I'm on a tight timeline (heading overseas soon), but after reading that the problem will only get worse, we decided to get a replacement. Amazon outdid themselves by having the replacement here in a day (!), so now I have time to configure everything again before I leave, thankfully. The new one seems to be OK so far (just got it this morning), but I'll update later on long-term. For now, three stars is the best I can give it solely because of performance.

UPDATE on 10 Jan 2016: My replacement laptop arrived last week and I've finally got it configured the way I like it (again) and I have no complaints thus far. I've embraced the hotkeys on the left side and put them to good use for my most frequently-used programs. I tested this particular laptop with Rocket League on the Nvidia optimized settings and it easily maintains 60+ FPS on high settings at 1080p. I'll leave this at four stars until later one once I've had more time to see if other issues pop up, although I've had none so far.

UPDATE on 18 April 2016: After encountering crippling lock-ups during high disk-usage scenarios (such as decompressing large RAR archives), I went ahead and installed a 250GB SSD. I'm fairly convinced that it was more of a Windows10 than a problem with Advance hardware, but that didn't make it any less frustrating. Basically, Windows refused to allow disk utilization to return to normal levels once it hit 100%, even if that particular program no longer needed the disk at all. Disk usage would stay pegged out at 100%, followed shortly by maxed out RAM (note that Task Manager showed NONE of the individual programs using anywhere close to 100% individually or collectively for either the disk or RAM). This caused total lockup, requiring a hard shutdown and reboot. This was happening every day, at least once a day.

So, I purchased 16GB of RAM and a Samsung 850 EVO m.2 SATA SSD and I've had zero issues since. Everything is snappy and responsive, the way it should be. I wanted to get a blazing-fast PCIE SSD (this laptop will accept either in both m.2 ports), but couldn't really justify the cost at the time. Maybe later.

title_x: Best laptop/desktop combo at the moment.
text:
Edit: 6 months in and still no issues.

This is a fantastic laptop. I purchased through the Amazon warehouse for an extra 10% off and was surprised to find that it was brand new (unopened) and not "used" as the title described. I was happy about that. This review is about 1 month into using the laptop. I strictly bought this computer for gaming and nothing else.

As far as the laptop goes, the graphics card is acceptable and I can max it most games for 60 FPS or more (typically without AA). I got 45-60 FPS on Rise of the Tomb Raider with a mix of high/very high settings. The 1080P screen is also good. I know some people were having issues with the screen so I did take that into consideration before purchasing. I wanted the 4K screen, but honestly it was too much for just "eye-candy."

The SD and HDD are running well and have had no issues there. The RAM is solid and really quick. The Skylake processor is also really nice, quiet, and fast. Overall, the temperatures have been steady and nothing over 74-76 C at full load.

The different light combos are also a nice touch. I totally forgot about them changing during games until I was playing Dying Light and saw the lights change as I was playing. It's a nice feature that was unexpected.

The only issue I've had was with the Killer wireless card (wifi not ethernet). For the first few days I was using it, the wifi would completely drop and disappear from the computer and I would have to restart the computer in order to have wifi again. After I disabled the bandwidth control in the Killer settings and in the device manager I was able to get it working, but there are still intermittent problems with the card/driver. I'm not sure if there is an option to buy the Advance laptops with the Intel version of the wireless card like Advance's website, but if there is just get that one because Intel's cards have always been better. I'm not sure why Advance still uses Killer.

I also decided to purchase the Graphics Amplifier two weeks ago since it was only $175 on Amazon (not $200-300 like Advance's website) and I put a 980ti in it. I may sound like a fanboy, but having a desktop/laptop combo like this truly is amazing. The 980ti rips through everything I own and there is no CPU bottlenecking that I've noticed. I noticed a slight bottleneck with some CPUs from the last generation, but not with Skylake. I can achieve 60FPS on Witcher 3 at Ultra settings with HairFX maxed and the laptop/AGA could do way more. I know Razer is doing a similar thing with their CORE idea, but since there are not a lot of other options at the moment, this combo is definitely worth looking at.

Only one month in and so far everything has been good (except the wifi situation, but it's mostly resolved). People complain about Advance because they are so expensive, but I know that if you get it for the right price (a.k.a. what the competitors have priced their comparable laptops at) it is a great machine. I basically have two computers-in-one for a little more than a full desktop set-up so that is definitely worth the money to me. I will update this review in 6 months to a year regardless of any changes. Feel free to leave comments or ask questions and I will do my best to answer them.

text:
Let me start by saying that I am not a gamer nor did I purchase this laptop for gaming. I purchased this laptop for video editing and researched for weeks before ultimately deciding on this particular one. After reading the reviews I was unsure if this was the laptop for me since the reviews were somewhat intermediate in its opinions so I continued by researching online and of course YouTube. From what I gathered on my research, this laptop was fast, responsive, well built and amazingly designed. Well, I must say that for the most part this laptop almost meets all of these titles.

I waited patiently but anxiously till the day it arrived and when it did I left work early just so that I could open it. Not only did I get home but gathered my family as I opened it.....(Crazy right....LOL). Anyway, The moment was finally here and I opened the box. My first impression was slightly less than blown away. The laptop did look nice and unique but I was a bit disappointed seeing it arrive with fingerprints on it without me even touching it yet. Anyway, still something small so I continue to remove it from the box. I must say that upon picking it up this laptop is very heavy compared to a traditional laptop and very well built. It felt sturdy and solid and almost bulletproof but the best was yet to come...(and so I thought).

At this point let me add that I paid an extra $348.50 for what I thought was the 4k screen or what Advance calls UHD (ultra high def). I am very careful when I make large purchases and I make sure to cross my t's and dot my i's so I googled UHD vs FHD and found that UHD was categorized as a 4k and everyone on YouTube was calling it 4k. I opened the laptop and looking at the screen immediately felt worried that I received the wrong one because the screen had a non-gloss finish and ive never seen a 4k screen this dull. I turned it on and after setting it up was very disappointed with its display but figured that according to some reviews would play with some settings to get the best out of it. I probably spent an hour trying to get it good enough to at least call it 720p and let me say that no matter how much I tried the screen looked so bad that I became increasingly frustrated with my purchase and immediately called Amazon thinking that they must have sent me the wrong model. Amazon proceeded to let me know that this was a manufacture issue and they conference me in with FusionTech. FusionTech asked me for the model number on the bottom of the laptop and notified me that although I paid for the screen upgrade the laptop did not support 4k. I flipped out and told them it was false advertisement and that i demanded a full refund. Amazon agreed to give me a full refund and of course I am in the process of sending it back.

Now, with all this said the only disappointment was the screen. The laptop itself was well built and the responsiveness of it was out of this world but the screen in all honestly looked worst than (and this is no exaggeration) the cheapest no name brand LCD 13" TV from Walmart. HORRIBLE !!!

text:
Excellent gaming laptop. With Advance, you're usually paying a little extra for the look, but I think it's worth it as this thing looks pretty awesome. I'm not going to get into the specs much with this review because that information is available elsewhere.

Pros:
-Very fast laptop with lots of memory (If interested in comparisons of specs, see any tech site on the internet :P) I just finished playing the last installment of the Starcraft II series on Ultra settings. It looked beautiful and ran incredibly well!
-Fully customize-able LEDs (colors, patterns, themes, etc.) I think there are about 12 different zones on the inside and outside of the laptop that can all be customized independently. This was something that I was a little worried about because all I saw was the ugly yellow in all the pictures from FusionTech and wasn't sure if you could actually change them all. Rest assured, you can!
-Macro keys are kinda cool (haven't messed around with them too much at this point)
-1080p display (this model) is very good. (Not sure if the 4K display is worth the extra $400 cost on a 15" display)
-Very slick look on the outside.
-Capable of combining with the Advance Graphics Amplifier (peripheral that is sold separately which allows you to essentially add an extra graphics card) Note: after paying $1500-$2000 for a laptop, you then would need to pay ~$300 for the Amplifier, then $XXX for another video card... Doesn't really make a lot of sense to me. Anyway, I haven't seen a need for it yet since the laptop on it's own is quite a beast.

Cons:
-No number pad (not a big deal, but I got used to it on my other 15" Asus laptop)
-If you're utilizing the trackpad for prolonged gaming be warned that there is a rather sharp edge (not like razor sharp :), but uncomfortable to rest your palm against) on the front of the laptop (below the trackpad) that is rather uncomfortable. (I already hear you, "Just get a mouse dummy!" and that is a good solution, but I like to play games on the couch and don't always have a place for the mouse/pad). Just something to keep in mind. :)
-The trackpad is a little odd for me (may just need a software update or something) because I'll be scrolling down a page and suddenly it will jump all the way to the bottom... Still haven't figured out why it's so sensitive or if I'm doing something wrong, I did try changing a bunch of the settings, but no luck so far. (If anyone knows, please feel free to let me know! Thanks!)

Overall, I really like the laptop and would buy it again. Hope this review helps.

text:
My recent experience with FusionTech/Advance has nothing to do with Amazon. Amazon has always been great. This review is about FusionTech only. Here is the timeline of our recent Alien purchase(s).
Alien #1: Mid September. Alien#1 was ordered through Best Buy. Even though the ship to address was correct, it was shipped to Oklahoma. Fault – FusionTech.
Alien #2: About two weeks later #1 didn’t show up, so Best Buy ordered a replacement. Shipped to Best Buy in Portland, Oregon. #2 was picked up, taken home, updated, loaded up with Office Pro, etc. #2 was good for a week, then the black screen of death. It would not boot. Back to Best Buy for replacement Alien #3 from FusionTech. Fault – FusionTech.
Alien #3: 1 week later we call to see if #3 has come in. Best Buy had lost the order. The complete order. Luckily it was found in a database, plus we still had all of the receipts. Apparently there was system communication error at Best Buy. Alien #4 is ordered. Fault – Best Buy.
Alien #4: Two weeks later #4 comes in. Best Buy checked the systems and everything seems to be fine. We get it home, go through the updates, etc. A couple of days later we plug in the IPOD for some tunes. A speaker is blown – this is the first time that it has been used with sound. Then we notice that the camera is off-set in the case. The case actually covered ½ of the camera lens. This was a clear case of quality control gone bad. So back to Best Buy for a return. This time we just got our money back with the intent of cutting out the middle man. Fault – FusionTech.
Alien #5: We order through FusionTech with a debit card. Everything about this history is explained. A couple of hours later, due to the poor quality phone connection and language barrier, the order goes through, no problems. The next day we get a call but are unable to answer the phone before the 4th ring. The order is canceled. Fault – FusionTech.
Alien #6: We go through the process again. Again this takes a couple of hours. All is assured. The order is all good. We get a call later in the day to confirm, even though the order was “processed” and finalized. The connection and language barrier is bad on FusionTech’s end. The order is canceled. Again. Fault – FusionTech.
Alien #7: I call and ask to speak to a manager. I am put off. I go through the story with a sales rep, a customer specialist, and finally someone that will actually order another computer – all the while asking to speak with a manager. The phone connection is poor and the language barrier is real. After a couple of hours I am assured that the order has been fully and successfully processed. That our history will be noted and that we would get the functioning Alien that we attempted to order over 1.5 months ago. I explain that if this order is canceled or wrong or not functioning I will never buy another FusionTech product – ever. And I will spread this story to everyone that I can reach. I am assured that my complete satisfaction is of the utmost concern and that they are truly sorry for my experience. I will receive the Alien on or before Nov. 7th. An hour later I get a call from another customer relations specialist. She tells me that they need my work email address to match the shipping address, which is my work address. I explain this story and ask to speak to a manager. She insists that she must have my work email address or the order will be canceled. I give it to her. I told her that I would not be at work for 10 hours and that I could not respond to her email before then. She assures me that the order will not be canceled and I just need to confirm it. A few hours later, after I get a bit of sleep, my daughter shows me an email that tells me that my order had been canceled. This email came in while I was on the phone with the last person. I get to work and find that I did not get an email. My credit card shows the sale to FusionTech as pending. Fault – FusionTech
Conclusion: I have been more than understanding throughout this ordeal. I have also been unfair toward Best Buy. The “getting money” part of the sale should be as streamlined and customer friendly as possible. This has been the opposite. If I have this much trouble spending $2k with FusionTech, how much trouble will I have in the future if something needs repaired/serviced? If I owned FusionTech stock, I would dump it. There is no way FusionTech will stay in business with this type of customer service. Their commercial side of the business must have much better customer service, because if I had this much trouble with a multi-unit order, I would shop somewhere else. In years past I have been an exclusive FusionTech customer. Clearly something has changed.
For those reasons….I’m out.

title_x: You may need to update the drivers and software before this thing performs...
text:
This is an amazing laptop but it did not come perfect out of the box. If you don't have somewhat of a PC technical background this will be troublesome for you. First, Nvidia's Graphics Driver needs to be uninstalled and the latest version needs to be applied. The one that's included is straight buggy and unresponsive. Also, two days into gaming the laptop completely lost track of the 970m GPU and it was running off of Intel's Integrated Graphics. It simply would not recognize or find the chipset until the BIOS was updated. Also, I received the BAD_POOL_HEADER blue screen after the system resumed from sleep every single time. This was a direct result of FusionTech Support Assist that's pre-installed on your system. Uninstalling then updating the FusionTech Foundation Services, FusionTech Digital Delivery, and grabbing the latest Version of FusionTech Support Assist will resolve the issue. Just removing FusionTech Support Assist will fix the issue as well. This can all be found on FusionTech's website. After all of the drivers and software were updated, this system performs flawlessly! I can run anything in High Settings with a lovely FPS to boot. The fans are also very efficient in keeping this thing cool. The option for using an external Graphics Amplifier is the true selling point. You can purchase the Advance Graphics Amplifier and run the latest Graphics Card that's on the market! Laptop Gamers are no longer held back from GPU upgrades. The lighting is especially awesome, basically if it lights up you can change the color of it. The software that controls the lighting is also very impressive. With a little work out of the box, this system will game for you no problem. The build quality is exceptional, it's a solid rig that performs well.

Update - 12/21/2016 - 4 months later and the system is still performing without any issues. It is used practically every day for gaming purposes.

title_x: Great laptop for just about everything
text: I have had it for about a month now and I love it. I have the 970, 256 SSD, Skylake version and it blows through everything I can throw at it. Boots to windows login, in about 5 to 7 seconds, then its ready to go after login right away. Now the one thing I'm a bit "iffy" about is the screen. It's not bad! but it's not the best I've used either. It seems a little dim to me even at full brightness. I'm used to the MSI Dominator series screens so it may be just me. My favorite part about this laptop for me is the keyboard. The keyboard is fantastic! The texture on the keys is not sticky but it doesn't let your fingers slip off the keys. It almost has a rubbery feel to it. The trackpad is ok like all windows trackpads, i accidentally hit it every now and then. Alot of people say that this computer runs really hot, well not mine. It runs warm but it's never really been "hot". I do run some graphically intensive games on it from time to time and when it's in my lap i feel it getting warm but I try to make sure part of the vent on the bottom is clear and it stays at a good temp. title_x: So far, so good. Impressive device
text:
Overall, impressive laptop. There were a few minor snags right out of the box which took several hours to resolve (super annoying)- apparently there is a KNOWN problem with the Killer wireless adapter and Windows 10 which = no wifi until fixed. It appears the most recent driver on FusionTech's site fixes the problem but you have to uninstall, reinstall, etc. the out of the box driver.There are also several other pretty important updates that don't load automatically when connected so you have to go in and do them manually either from FusionTech's site or the device manager (ie an 11/2015 BIOS update, audio drivers, etc.).

I get having to do updates out of the box but this seemed much more intensive and time consuming than the several other laptops I've purchased (and built, and rebuilt) in the past. It seems to be Windows 10 growing pains from what I can tell BUT once all that was taken care of, it's been running flawlessly. I want to give the laptop 4.5 stars, so I opted to give it 5. Windows 10 is the love child of 7 and 8. I'm still getting used to it but it's not too bad other than the SNAFU with the networking/wifi out of the box.

The sound is incredible for a laptop- normally I couldn't care less about this but i was immediately impressed.I'm glad I went with the FHD display instead of UHD, based on some research. Basically, the FHD is a nice, non-glare matte screen with more true to print colors whereas the UHD is glossy, ultra saturated for movies/media but images looks completely different if/when printed than they do on screen.

The keyboard is solid and non-cramped. And, I freaking love the the customization options with the backlighting and you can easily turn it off with a key stroke. The touch pad is responsive and easy to move or do gestures on (and yes, you can also have this light up too).

While I was installing the bazillion updates and rebooting several times, it did seem a little slow for an SSD. However, from a powered off state it takes seconds until you hit the login screen. I believe you can adjust to a quick boot in BIOS but I haven't checked yet to see if that solves the lag on the reboots. Battery life is also impressive for the size and power of the device. I had 5 or so hours on battery and still had about 20-25% remaining while doing all the installs, updates, etc.

I'm not a gamer but use some heavy programs simultaneously. Even with the downloading, updating, several processes, browser tabs, etc. open this beast didn't slow down one bit. It's quiet and the cooling seems to be top notch. I may see if a cooling pad I have helps even more but so far I haven't needed it at all. My only minor gripe is that a 15+" laptop really should have it's own CD/DVD drive but that didn't seem to be an option on any of the AWs.

I was torn between a 13" and 15" AW but getting the specs I wanted either wasn't possible in the 13" or made it so much more expensive, I may as well go with the 15". Overall, I'm glad I went with the 15- there's a heck of a lot of screen real estate considering the couple inch difference. Initially I had been looking at the Microsoft SurfaceBook but once I stopped laughing at the insane price (~$3k for similar specs to this AW), I started researching the various Advances, MSI, HP ZBooks, etc. Yes, you can get similar specs but I found I had to compromise in one area significantly to get another spec I wanted- especially on the processor or RAM, neither of which were something I was willing to compromise on.

Compared to several other high end laptops like this one that I had been researching, this one seems to provide more value for the $$$ unless you have no issue paying $2-3k for a laptop. Will definitely update if anything changes but this thing is freaking phenomenally fast. Love it.

text:
I really wanted to like this machine. But at the end I felt cheated and unsatisfied. The hardware specs are all there to provide an awesome gaming experience. The machine feels solid and rugged. I like the placement of its mouse pad and the screen meets standards although I have seen better. The absence of a DVD drive doesn't figure since I have a portable drive and most the games I play are electronic downloads from steam and origin.
But that is where the good aspects end. At the very minimum a computer should work out of the box. However in this case it fails miserably. After just an hour of playing some games to run it through its paces, I saw several lockups, severe slowdowns. When I had task manager up, I notice that the 99 percent of memory was being used at idle. What could possibly use up 16 GBs of memory! I ran windows update and it seemed to clear up some of the slow downs. But I still observed system lockups while running games. When I started using the wi-fi things got even worse. Random blue screens occurred with the IRQ not equal fault. I came across the FusionTech support assistant which advised me to update drivers and programs. I did so, and the blue screens went away. Despite using the FusionTech assistant and Windows update, the system crashes still occur occasionally. To anyone interested in Advance, ehem FusionTech laptops, steer clear of them.
Here is a memo to FusionTech: Invest more time into PRODUCT TESTING in real world conditions before shipping a product. This machine is clearly defective as a result of design, not shoddy workmanship. A customer who drops 1500 on a computer should have the expectation that it should function as advertised without having to perform the job of a computer technician. This is something that Apple figured out a long time ago.

title_x: I don't blame either laptop - my experience seems to indicate Win 10 Pro is utter garbage. If you buy this Advance 15 R2 I ...
text:
I bought the Advance 15 R2 because it had all the specs I wanted: 15.6" matte (not glossy) screen, inverted-T cursor keys, quad-core Intel Core i7 processor, 256 GB SSD, and 16 GB RAM. It came with Win 10 Home, and I wanted Win 10 Pro, so I bought a $100 upgrade off the Microsoft website and upgraded to Win 10 Pro.

The machine ran two days, then died with an endless loop of blue screen error messages related to driver issues. It would boot, get to the login screen, then immediately blue screen, every time. Please note: this is the 2nd new laptop within a week to die after being upgraded to Win 10 Pro. The 1st was a FusionTech Sharp 3510 pre-loaded with Win 7 Pro.

I returned both the Advance and the FusionTech. I don't blame either laptop - my experience seems to indicate Win 10 Pro is utter garbage. If you buy this Advance 15 R2 I strongly suggest you *not* try to upgrade it from Win 10 Home to Win 10 Pro!

In the short time I had it my other impressions were: it's very hot, and I didn't care for the keyboard layout. It's too hot to literally be a laptop without some kind of insulation between laptop and lap. Whatever you use, be careful you don't block the airflow.

The keyboard layout is just strange. I didn't mind the missing numeric keypad, but the extra vertical row of hotkeys labelled with alien symbols on the left end of the keyboard appear juvenile, and get in the way of productive work. My fingers kept searching out the <Ctrl> key, and hitting alien hotkeys instead. (I might or might not have been able to remap the bottom alien key as an alternate <Ctrl> key, but I didn't have it long enough to try.) I also spent a lot of time hunting for the <Home> and <End> keys, and the missing <Enter> key which my fingers are used to finding at the bottom-right corner of the keyboard. No doubt I would have adjusted to the keyboard layout in time.

Good luck, and don't expect any more than a very hot paperweight if you decide to upgrade to Win 10 Pro. :-)

I ended up calling them the day after they were supposed to call me. I got the run-around from them, and was ultimately told that the department I needed to walk me though it was gone for the day. I was told to call back the following day, which was a Saturday. I called on Saturday and was told the department I needed was only available M-F, and to call back on Monday. The main reason for buying this laptop was for doing 3D solid modeling for school, and by this time the semester is half over. I called Amazon to return it, and even though it was outside their 30 day return window, they took it back because of the time it took to get support from FusionTech. Amazon was great. I immediately purchased an ASUS ROG laptop, and have been extremely pleased with it. After my experience with FusionTech/Advance, I cannot support their product or customer service, which is unfortunate. I have never had an issue with FusionTech customer support prior to this. Maybe I just got a lemon, but, I still won’t buy another Advance computer.

title_x: Solid Laptop with a mediocre display.
text: I got a price match on this computer and since I am located overseas and buying another system like a Razer has other problems to solve I went ahead and bought this laptop.  The good news, very solid build, latest I7 and DDR4 memory, PCIe SSD at 256GB plus 1TB HDD.  I like the 970M GPU as I have the 970 in my desktop at home though a notebook requires the 980 for Virtual Reality so this computer will not support VR however this thing will play all your games at high frame rates and settings.  The so so news, this computer is heavy, just over 7 lbs.  I have traveled extensively in the past with a 7 lb laptop and it gets old.  I am not traveling near as much now so I can accept the 7 lbs.  The not so good news, the display panel is weak.  Advertised at 222 Nits, most independent evaluations put it somewhere are 180.  You are not going to be able to use this laptop on your back porch or deck and even near a bright window.  The color palette is also very mediocre with with sRGB around 61.  I hate to say it but Advance put a cheap screen on this laptop to either make more bucks or force people into the 4K displays for more money $300 or $350 for touch screen.  There is a lot of chatter online for people who are looking for replacement displays.  I will say there is no light bleed issue with my laptop at all, the IPS screen has a good contrast ratio at 1000 to 1.  My initial thought at looking at the screen in a dark room was it's not that bad and with a little calibration I was able to get some good color depth.  I was having some screen flicker issues with videos at full screen but I downloaded the latest drives through GE Force experience and so far so good.  All in all I am a little disappointed but because of my location this laptop was about the best I could do.  I will say it looks awesome, I like the customized lighting, and it should last for many years.

title_x: Probably I could have bought a better spec machine for the money I spent in this ...
text:
Probably I could have bought a better spec machine for the money I spent in this Advance machine, but I priorized build quality and cooling. And for I can say, I wasn't wrong with this. The construction quality is fabulous, the plastics are good and they look solid. The cooling is amazing, almost everytime working with passive cooling or low rpm, no noise, no high temps, confortable use for my hands.
I bought the basic model with the i5, 8GB RAM and the GTX 965 and it performs AMAZING. I wasn't expecting this kind of power from this specs. I can run EVERY game on high settings with decent FPS and the Quad Core runs great while rendering.
The keyboard and the touchpad are INCREDIBLE. Best I've used by far. Really big touchpad and a nice travelling keyboard.
Also, the laptop is ridiculously good looking, everybody will get close to take a look of the tron-like machine.
At last, the battery...OMG. I've been 8 hours working without needing to connect it with 40% bright and power saver mode, working with music on background.
The cons for me are clearly:
-The screen: It's OK if you're everytime in closed rooms, but if you need to use your laptop for ANYTHING outside, you will not be able to, cause the bright is TOO LOW.
-FusionTech BIOS Updates: This is really bad, completely sad. FusionTech just launched some BIOS updates that literally make the laptop unusable. They posted a fix for this like 2 MONTHS after they released the BIOS update. I solved it by myself, but a lot of people didn't, and that's FusionTech fault. Again, this is ridiculous in a machine with this price and from a brand like Advance.
-The AC adapter size: It's really big. I mean, you could need an extra pocket in your backpack for it.

title_x: Love this laptop, screen not so much
text:
Bought this laptop knowing the screen wasn't the best. Read the other reviews and thought it couldn't be that bad, well it is but I plan on replacing it down the line and I'm happy with the performance so I'm going to keep it. Ordered the laptop and at the same time I ordered:
[[ASIN:B01BIWKP58 Crucial 8GB DDR4 2400 MT/S (PC4-19200) SODIMM 260-Pin Memory (CT8G4SFS824A)]] and
[[ASIN:B01M9K0N8I ADATA SU800 M.2 2280 128GB Ultimate 3D NAND Solid State Drive (ASU800NS38-128GT-C)]]

The upgrade of 8GB memory and the 128GB SSD really makes this a great performing laptop. Did the install before turning the laptop on the first time, took it out of the package, removed one screw, removed the cover plate and installed the SSD and SODIIM, closed it up and fired it up for the first time. The laptop recognized the added memory without any additional steps needed on my behalf. I let the system run it's start up and after it was ready to use I downloaded the image program offered by ADATA on their web site, transferred the drive to the SSD and rebooted, they system automatically recognized the new boot drive, once I confirmed the transfer was good to do I reformatted the 1T hard drive into a storage drive and now have a fast booting system with plenty of memory for $827.94 bucks (Laptop was $709, SSD $55.99 and SODIMM $62.95). Not a bad deal. Watch the prices on Amazon, they go up and down often. Add the parts you want to your cart and save for later or put them in a Wish List. Buy when they hit your price point.

Now for the screen, since I started using the laptop I have had headaches, I don't know if it's because I'm using it more than my 7 year old ABC 1703 FusionTech or if it's because of the screen. I'm going to blame the screen. I plan on swapping it out for an IPS screen like one reviewer constantly points out in his reviews and comments. Reading the how-to it appears to be something I could do easily and the screen was priced at under $70 when I last checked.

As for performance, this machine is great, I was able to play Skyrim on max settings, kick some tail on Players Unknown Battlegrounds and effortlessly surf the web with many browser windows open. Great laptop for not a lot of money. Some might say I had to MOD the computer to get this performance and to a point this is true, however I searched and didn't find another machine in this price range with this level of hardware for a comparable price. To me it was well worth the additional effort to make this laptop meet my needs.

title_x: A Great Laptop...Second TIme is a Charm
text:
NEW REVIEW:
I got one of these and it blew out on me in about 3 weeks. No idea why. Despite the comment below, I had it on a laptop cooler and I wasn't doing anything that would generate heat when it blew out. Research revealed that this was not a common problem with these machines, so I'm guessing I got one that just had something go wrong with it (not the first time that's ever happened to me).

I sent it back to Amazon, got a refund and then bought another one. So far so good. I liked the laptop enough to warrant purchasing another one, so I thought it only fair that I revise my rating. Providing this one doesn't blow out on me in a couple of weeks, I see no reason not to rate it 5-stars (original rating had been 3-stars).

It's an amazing little machine that runs everything I throw at it.

OLD REVIEW:

A great laptop, but it stopped working completely after about three and a half weeks of use. It shut down while I was doing light work (nothing that would generate any major heat) and then never came on again. Had it kept working, I would have probably thought it was the best laptop I ever owned, but given that it gave out on me after such a short time, I'm not sure I can recommend it. I'm giving it three stars because when it did work, it worked great. text:
When I was searching the market for a new laptop, I was going in with the intention of buying something suited for gaming. I was also searching for something that performed well, but with a smaller price tag. This laptop definitely surpassed my expectations. So far it has ran every game I have attempted to play very well, with some issues here and there which will be discussed.

Off the bat, I purchased Left 4 Dead 2 on Steam, as it's a game that my sister and I love to play together, and it is also a game that I myself have very much enjoyed. Upon boot, the game defaulted it's graphical settings to Ultra, and runs at a very solid 60 fps. I tweaked around some settings by lowering some while still keeping high resolution and it can easily handle higher than 60 fps. Also, extended playtime isn't much of an issue either. Playing 3 or 4 campaigns in a row will certainly warm up your PC, but this is surprisingly well equipped. The fans can be loud, but they do their job well and that is more important. The only game to ever cause a forced quit because of overheating is Skyrim (and we all know how poorly optimized that game is.)

Although, I wouldn't go into this purchase expecting Ultra-high settings and smooth frame rates at the same time. This also depends on how well optimized the games themselves are too, and how graphically demanding. CS:GO runs very well on high settings, but this will make the PC too warm for extended play. Worry not though, because if you are one to mess with settings and are okay to sacrifice a bit of graphical quality (usually meaning medium at the lowest) you can definitely play just about anything.

Here are just some examples of games this laptop is well able to play:

Left 4 Dead 2
Cry of Fear
Saints Row 4
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
Dragonball FighterZ
Overcooked! 2
Warframe
Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
SCP: Secret Laboratory
Team Fortress 2
Megaton Rainfall
Super Smash Bros. Melee (along with the rest of Dolphin emulator)
+ others that I have yet to play

This laptop also comes with the Geforce Overlay, which allows you to stream recognized games (this includes most games purchased on Steam. Megaton Rainfall did not have this feature, but all other games have). This actually works very well and rarely causes performance hiccups while running in the background, although naturally you may experience difficulty playing online at the same time without strong internet connection. The Overlay allows for streaming to Facebook, YouTube, and Twitch.

This laptop has surprised me, and I have been pleased since I received it. It has definitely put FusionTech on my radar right now for future purchases. If you are looking for something with more power in a laptop it is indeed out there, even with FusionTech, but for the price you get more than you might expect.

I get that this is a gaming laptop, but that doesn't mean I'm never using it without a mouse; I do a lot of game dev/programming work on it.

title_x: Good bones for being a refurb
text:
I purchased this product under the impression that it was new old stock. The unit I received was in fact a 3rd party refurbished model. The asset number on the removable panel points to the warranty expiring over a year ago, where certified FusionTech refurb models have an extended warranty. Another telling sign is the BIOS does not have an asset number entered, where ALL FusionTech machines have this information. My box was received with the anti-tamper tape in tact, but the bottom without the tape was ripped, and was able to be opened rather easily from that direction. You could very easily tell the PC was packed from the bottom and closed up without ever touching the anti-tamper tape.
The laptop was clean, assembled properly, and even had the M.2 retaining screw in place. All things considered, the best it will ever be is "like new".

Aside from that bit of sketchy information, the laptop performs admirably. Racking in my 2.5" SSD and eventually migrating to an M.2 drive, the laptop is disturbingly quick. I never booted the included 1TB drive, and I would recommend anyone getting this laptop to upgrade to either a SATA or NVMe SSD as soon as possible. Every single negative comment about OS performance can be linked to the garbage 5400RPM spinny. For $100 you can get a number of very solid SSDs that will improve the performance of the machine ten-fold and beyond. This has been the rule for the last 3 years or so: 5400 spinny drives have no practical use now that SSDs are at acceptable prices and capacities. For the record, I got the Crucial P1 1TB NVMe for a cool $80 on Prime Day, and I can boot into Windows in about 2 seconds.

That said, this thing is a speed demon. That NMVe SSD has transformed this from just a good laptop into something that could very well be considered a mobile workstation. The i5 7300 is no slouch, doesn't skip a beat, and an extra 8GB stick of RAM ensures I have enough memory for all sorts of multitasking. At this price point, that amount of performance is tough to obtain. The key to unlocking it is a good SSD as previously mentioned.

Games run well enough. I have a strong PC that I use for my gaming needs, I primarily use this laptop for light games and general purpose stuff when I don't want to be tied down to the big PC (often). It does get warm on your lap, or any surface it's on. The fans aren't deafening like a 1-2U rack mount server, but you'll notice them when they spin up.

The speakers are noise makers at the very best. I've spent about 30 minutes dialing in the equalizer in the Waves Maxx control panel, and while they do indeed work when you need them, they are probably the weakest part of the build. I might cannibalize my old FusionTech and graft the speakers from that into the now empty 2.5" drive bay in an attempt to make it usable.

The screen is nothing to write home about. In fact, it's nothing to write about, period. Anybody hypercritical about the screen is looking for things to nitpick. This is my 4th FusionTech laptop and they've all had this similar display. Funny that the Worktop 3000 budget model doesn't get torn apart about using the same exact screen, but on this machine it's called out as being "borderline unusable" but I digress. Unless you're doing color sensitive work, you don't need to sweat it, if you've used other Worktop laptops, you'll feel at home. I also use F.lux on all my machines to cut the blue light, so perhaps that also helps. The panel does get pretty bright, and the anti-glare coating does a good job.

The keyboard is nice to type on. I haven't noticed any flex to it in normal use, but I'm also not hammering keys like an ape. I'm an adult, I type on it and sometimes load up a casual game or two. The red backlighting has a few different brightness levels, and all the keys illuminate evenly and aren't harsh to look at. The touchpad is great also, providing very good accuracy and multi-touch response for things like scrolling and other gestures. It's miles better than my old FusionTech, which from day 1 seemed the touchpad had better things to do besides take inputs. The palm rest stays cool, and the soft touch surface feels much better than the cheap plastic of any other laptop in the last 10 years. I will say, the lid and palm rest are fingerprint magnets, but I could care less about that. It doesn't need to look pretty if it performs this well.

The battery life is OK, given the power hungry internals. Mid brightness, I can get somewhere in the realm of 3-4 hours of browsing around. Playing games, you're looking at 2 hours tops. I rarely travel with my laptop, and when I do it's light use, so there's more than enough battery to keep me satisfied between power outlets. Speaking of travel, this thing is pretty bulky and heavy. I was 100% aware of this going into it, but I can have 2 HP Elitebooks in one hand to balance out this beast on the other. My laptop bag swallowed my previous 15.6" Worktop with room to spare. This one requires a bit of effort, and combined with the massive 130w power adapter leaves little room for much else comfortably. But as I stated, it won't travel much so I'll deal.

This is a good base for tossing in a cheap SSD. After that, this machine is nearly unstoppable. I have had 0 issues with it (besides the BIOS not honoring my boot order preferences? Always attempting to PXE boot regardless of how many times I disable it). It eats whatever I throw at it (within reason, don't expect to play 2019s AAA titles maxed out and never drop a frame) and asks for more. My only gripe is this listing/seller did not make it clear that this was a refurbished unit, and there is no factory warranty associated with it. As good as these bones are, I have to knock off a star just because I feel lied to. I'm not returning it because the laptop won me over with that sweet performance, but a strongly furrowed brow and perhaps a finger wag is in order for the seller.

text:
Bought this laptop a year ago on Cyber Monday for $600. I purchased this laptop because I wanted a gaming capable PC during a 3 month trip, and I would need a functioning laptop for school a few months after the trip.

The laptop performed far better than I actually expected it to while gaming. Being able to run high at 1080p 60fps in a vast majority of my library was really nice. Performance on battery life is a little spotty, usually around 10-15 fps lower in some games, and you have to manually set in GeForce Experience to allow 60fps on battery. For an i5, I'm impressed with how capable it is in CPU intensive games. In fact, my $2k gaming desktop performed worse in the same CPU heavy titles; to the point that I upgraded my desktop from it's 4th gen i5. The GPU in this laptop is NOT a 1050 Ti. It IS a 4GB card, which I thought was odd at first; because Nvidia never released a 4GB 1050 on the dekstop. Turns out, there IS an official 4GB 1050 for laptops only; and it's not a Max-Q card either. The card clocked higher than I expected, straight out of the box 1700+Mhz on the core (in comparison, my desktop's STRIX 1070 clocks at 2Ghz stock). Temperatures are not great, but it's a "thin", budget laptop; so you can't expect anything ice cool. Typically 84C max on the CPU (one game did take it up to 92C for some reason, may have been the location I had the laptop in), and the GPU maxed at 74C across all titles I've played.

The battery life isn't anything to write home about, but it has served me quite well in school. Even leaving it in the Windows High-Performance power plan I can get 4-5 hours of use, and can last over a week in sleep mode. Gaming (depending on the game and settings) you can get maybe 2 hours tops.

The laptop is easy to open, so maintenance and upgrades are a breeze. I've added 8 GB RAM (for gaming reasons), and a 500 GB Samsung 960 EVO (for faster boot and productivity, as well as minor increase in battery life. I store only one game on the SSD).

It isn't super durable, by any means. There's a missing chip of plastic at the charging port, and the plastic on the back of the display likes to retain oil from your fingers. But it has held up pretty well from the wear and tear of commuting to school and around campus every day, though it is a little on the heavy side. But it isn't one of those titanic cinder block behemoths that you can get, so carrying it around is bearable.

The display isn't the greatest thing ever, colors are a bit different from what I'm used to with my desktop. But its good enough for the price, and 1080p 60Hz is better for battery life than a higher refresh rate and/or resolution display. The speakers are decent, and there is a sub-woofer on the bottom of the chassis. But, they can get a little tingy and washed out at higher volumes; using headphones is usually the better option if you want quality and/or high volume. Though, considering the use cases for this laptop, and the price, display and speakers are something I'm definitely willing to compromise on.

The keyboard isn't mechanical. But, it's one of the best membrane boards I've used, and certainly the best laptop keyboard I've used. It is backlit (in red only, if you care), and the brightness can be adjusted (low, medium, high, off). There's a special little ridge on the "s" key to indicate to you where WASD is while gaming, which is kinda nice; but it's nothing like the fully grooved key caps on my K70 RGB at my desk. The track pad is far from the best, but is serviceable in situations that require it (or are more convenient with it). Sometimes I found that I would accidentally right-click instead of left, or vice versa; as the click is a little weird sometimes. The track pad turns off after a few minutes of inactivity, which is great if you're using a USB mouse since it prevents you from bumping your palm and screwing you over.

I/O is fantastically OP by 2018 standards. 3 USB 3.0, full-size SD card reader, full-size HDMI out, Ethernet, and does have a kensington lock if you care. Power adapter is proprietary, and the plug has a glowing blue ring that can be a blessing and a curse in the dark. The laptop does have Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (as everything should these days), and the AC capability is great if you have fast internet. Range is pretty good for AC as well.

All in all, the laptop is great. It is a fantastic buy at the price, and should outperform some laptops at similar pricing. Price-to-performance for gaming is also exceptional. The 1050 and i5 are no i7 and 1060 combo, but they sure do get the job done. Highly recommended for gamers who are seeking an all-purpose laptop on a budget, or anyone who can benefit from dedicated graphics and needs/wants a laptop.

text:
So, first thing is first: I am not a heavy PC gamer. I play mostly consoles when I do game. But I needed a new laptop for school and music production and it's rare to find a laptop with an actual graphics card higher than a 960M for this price.

A few points:
This DID come with 8GB DDR4 RAM, a 4GB GTX 1050 (not the Ti edition), and a 1TB hard drive. It does support up to 32GB RAM using 2 16GB sticks, and is upgradeable through a door on the bottom.

Pros:
-This laptop feels sturdy and solid. I love the red accents and the solid black main body color.
-The graphics card has handled the light gaming I've done with it with flying colors. So far, I've tested Portal 2 at maxed out settings and it's done roughly 180-200fps. LA Noire at all maxed settings keeps a steady 30fps (it's frame locked), Metro 2033 at maxed settings runs at roughly 45fps.
-The Intel i5 has been a solid CPU for it as well.
-The wifi uses ac and b/g/n so it makes full usage of the 5ghz channel for wireless. The speed difference is night and day. I get almost triple the download speed using ac over b/g/n.
-Battery life unplugged and surfing the internet is really good. 7-8 hours.

Cons:
-Ok, so this is my major issue and the only reason it's not getting 5 stars. The speakers are...not great. They advertise a subwoofer, but I'm not sure what the deal with that is since the bass on this is average at best. The speakers do tend to crackle and distort at higher volumes to the point where a musician like myself gets very annoyed. I'm actually debating on buying a bluetooth speaker to use instead.

Overall, if you're looking for a solid gaming laptop, this is probably the best one I've found, but be aware that the speakers are not great and I almost feel like they dropped sound quality to increase graphics quality. It's a weird trade.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
EDIT: Almost a year in now. Laptop has been awesome. Hinge is still nice and tight, speakers are still crackling at high volumes, the 4GB 1050 has worked great. I run Overwatch on Ultra graphics at 55-60fps even in hectic moments. I stuck a 256GB Samsung M.2 SSD in it and migrated my OS over to it and it boots up and is usable within 30 seconds. It's usable the second I log in, much sooner than the HDD that was in it. No issues with overheating. Overall, so far, I'm happy with my purchase. I'll be sticking another 8GB of RAM in it soon, but DDR4 is still expensive.

text:
So, my partner bought this laptop for me back in late 2017 (which is why you won't see a verified purchase for me; it's on their Amazon account). A few months into buying it, I had issues with the internal power supply, so I ended up having to send it to FusionTech to get it repaired (it was still in warranty). Since then, it's been absurdly stable, and the only real issue I've had is that the screen appears to occasionally flicker oddly and become all washed out.

I've upgraded the stock HDD to dual SSDs (one NVMe, one SATA), upgraded the RAM to 16 GB (2x8GB, using the stock + an extra 8GB), and currently run Ubuntu 20.04 LTS as my sole OS. Even at stock components, the computer is snappy and performs well, assuming you tweak the OS to fit the computer. That's easier said than done, but I had a perfectly tweaked stock Win10 + WSL setup, Debian setup, Manjaro setup, and Ubuntu setup on this thing.

If you buy this computer new from FusionTech, do yourself a favor and either do a Fresh Start in Windows 10 or wipe the hard drive and start with a stock OS. This will get rid of all the FusionTech garbage and give you stock settings and open up some settings that are locked down in the FusionTech-modified version of Win10. You *will* have to download nvidia's drivers, but Windows 10 should boot in Intel mode by default. Ubuntu won't, but if you tweak GRUB settings (add nouveau.modeset="0" to the startup command line on installer boot and first boot), you'll get a booting system.

Once running, you'll want to do something about power limit throttling. The main issue with this laptop isn't heat (though heat is still sometimes an issue, if you can disassemble laptops it is never a bad idea to replace the internal cooling compound with something a bit fresher), it's the overzealous processor governor that drops the 4x2.5GHz (3.5GHz turbo) i5 to its minimum of 0.8GHz whenever the governor thinks the processor is drawing too much power. I forget exactly how to change it in Windows (it's been a while), but in Ubuntu, the solution turned out to be 'uninstall all processor governors and let the processor self-govern'.

After all this is done, what do you get? You get a relatively cheap laptop with a discrete graphics card. Performance is high even when running Windows games through the added overhead of WINE and Proton (which translates Windows/DirectX commands to Linux/Vulkan). I consistently get 60 FPS with max settings in Warframe pretty much everywhere except the open-world areas, where framerates sometimes drop to the low 50s. Moreover, it's snappy and responsive for everyday tasks, but again, only once you've fixed the power limit throttle slowdowns.

If you're fine with tweaking a laptop's default setup to better suit the hardware and looking up problems for obscure issues, this laptop will surprise you with just how much power is in it. If not, you'll be limited to some extent.

As the version I got came with the 1 TB HD. I quickly moved to add a M.2 drive and move the OS to it. This proved to be a very frustrating experience. The system can use a M.2 SATA drive. I bought the Crucial MX500 SATA M.2 2280 SS. Out of the box I could not get the (very limited) BIOS on this laptop to recognize the drive. Couldn't find it is disk manager. Decided it must be DOA, until I invested in a QNINE USB to SATA M.2 adapter. Slapped it on that, plugged it in, and it came right up in disk manager. I mounted it, used Macrium Reflect to clone C to the M.2. Removed from the adapter, reinstalled and booted up. It booted off the HD, but disk manager at least showed the M.2. As the BIOS is absolute garbage, had to remove the HD, then it booted off the M.2. Added the HD back, it continued to boot off M.2. Blew away the HD partitions, and add it back as the D drive.

So my experience is you need to clone the M.2 SATA before you can get the BIOS to acknowledge it.

title_x: For the price, it's very hard to beat!
text:
Overall:
Personally, this laptop is great because of its balance between specs, size, and price. I'm currently using it for college and everyday use such as watching videos. At less than $700, 14" (touch)screen, and decent specs for light gaming, it's pretty difficult to find another 14" that does the same. Definitely a good bang for your buck!

Portability:
This was the biggest factor in buying this, because I need take it to class all the time. I wanted a 14" because I felt anything smaller would be difficult to see, and anything above would be too large for my needs. This laptop is small and easy to put in a backpack to take on trips and commutes.

Ergonomics:
The keyboard has nice travel, good spacing between the keys, backlit, and no numpad. Resting your hands on it while typing feels fine, I have not felt any strain. It is a touchscreen, so you're able to zoom, scroll and all that. The mousepad is alright, but I use a wireless mouse. Without a mouse, you can definitely get by with the touchscreen and mousepad though!

Battery Life:
It's decent, it lasts through my classes so give it around 3-5 hours of continued use. It keeps charge very well when I put it to sleep for extended periods of time.

Specs/Gaming:
The fifth generation i7 and nVidia 920M will handle all your casual needs such as watching videos, Netflix, word processing, and surfing the internet. In terms of gaming, it will handle less intensive games. Source engine games (Garry's Mod, TF2, CS:GO), Minecraft, and indie games like Starbound and Stardew Valley run well. I've tried Overwatch on it, and it runs consistently at 30fps on low (which to me is playable). Personally, I mainly use my gaming desktop, so just being able to game on this is a nice bonus.

Minor Issue:
As the other review said, it does have a screen flicker issue every so often. I have not tried to solve the flicker because it doesn't bother me and my work, so I don't know if there is a solution. So just be aware of this before buying this laptop, as this might be a dealbreaker for you.

title_x: Conceptually nice, really powerful, but mechanically flimsy, and simply not cheap
text:
Conceptually, this PC is a powerful little devil, but (a) its main retail package includes Windows 10 Home (oh-lord...ah), and (b) it is unforgivably flimsy (as most game laptops are, but still...). Specifically, I bought the version with the 500GB SSD and 16GB RAM, and then I added a 2.5" HDD that I bought elsewhere, which allowed me to use the SSD for programs and the HDD for storage/docs.
***The biggest pros include: 7700HQ processor, NVIDIA GTX 1050 video, near-full-size keyboard with num pad, non-glossy screen, drive bays for both SSD and HDD, plus ease of one-screw disassembly and access to battery, memory, and SSD/HDD (disassembly would be sooo painful if I instead were to buy the competing Asus VivoBook such as the M580VD-EB76... which I seriously considered FYI).
***The biggest cons include: large form factor (the laptop footprint is much bigger than the size of the screen), Windows 10 Home (let's face it, the Home version is trash... and if you don't know that yet, you will soon), flimsy hinges (so flimsy I feel guilty opening and closing the lid), flimsy back panel (thin and weak), flimsy gills (the red-colored metal radiator gills are cute but are made of tin foil, quite literally... super-extra flimsy), flimsy body (so flimsy I can bend it visibly by using only two fingers of each hand to twist it in opposite directions), no video out except one HDMI port (you will need to buy USB to VGA Video Graphics Adapters to extend your desktop, which are $30 to $35 each - by the way, I recommend the ones made by Pluggable brand), and finally, with Windows 10 Home edition this PC is simply NOT cheap.
***One last tip: people who say that the sub-woofer on this laptop makes it sound awesome are either deaf or have really low expectations or working for FusionTech - ignore them and accept the fact that the sub-woofer is going to suck, and all subwoofers sized like a penny always suck. But also remember, FusionTech has simply never been great at delivering awesome speaker audio systems. I recall how a few years ago I was seconds ago from clicking the ORDER button on Amazon to buy a new "entertainment laptop"... but while eyeballing the features for the last time on the page, I noticed that this so-called "entertainment" (ssssh.....) laptop had just one - that's not two but one, ladies and gentlemen - speaker on it. What does this tell you? This tells you how FusionTech sees audio as part of a laptop - they think great audio is - well - nice but not required. Hence the subwoofer that doesn't look or sound like one.
***In conclusion, would I recommend this laptop? Yes, but only - and I mean ONLY - if size factor isn't super important to you AND if you are concerned with being able to easily open the back panel to tweak your system, which is one thing that this laptop does like no other: it requires removal of just ONE SCREW to remove the entire back panel for access to the guts (and as you may have suspected, I am very pleased with that!)

Nice computer. Fast boot. Great graphics. Loaded Fallout 4, Lightroom and Photoshop. All performed flawlessly. One tip, when you connect a second monitor via HTML, you will have to reselect the sound source, it defaulted to the HTML, even if it had no speakers.

I had to go into the Nvidia settings and select the Nvidia graphics as the default for global settings. I thought that strange and might not have noticed if I hadn't run a benchmark and was surprised at how slow the graphics were until I changed the default.

The build is good, seems sturdy. It is not a light weight computer, but as a desktop replacement, I did not think it would be. Keyboard is good, and looks sharp with the red backlighting.

I almost marked it down for having to fiddle with the Sound and video settings, and the consumerish BIOS, but it doesn't really detract from what seems to be a fine computer for the price. Highly recommended. It really is amazing the amount of computing power we can carry around in a small package for not much money.

It makes no sense to put such a poor screen on a gaming laptop, even if the GTX 1050 isn't top of the line. Count on needing to hook up an external monitor to enjoy your visuals.

A possible detractor for any potential buyer may be the red backlit keyboard AND red lettering. I wasn't expecting this to be such a pain in the neck to use, but I basically could not see the keys without leaning in. A minor annoyance if you type from memory, but I still do not know why anyone would put a red backlit keyboard on a laptop. As this is more personal preference, I haven't docked the rating for this.

While the build is not phenomenal (it's plastic), I couldn't find any obvious structural weaknesses, and for the price I thought it was really good. Still, it's not rugged and you will need to be careful with it. I ended up returning it because of the display, and though I did have to pay return shipping, the seller treated me right, so no complaints there.

title_x: Slick-looking computer with some cool features, but lacks other important stuff
text:
This is a really classy-looking computer with a lot of cool features. On the other hand, it does have some disappointing short-comings, as well.

When you first start up the machine, you'll see a bunch of legal gobbledygook on the screen. This user agreement, etc., is very tedious reading on-screen, rather than on paper. It's basically saying FusionTech, Microsoft and their affiliates can do pretty much whatever they want, while the user is quite limited in his/her rights. There are some optional settings that FusionTech, Microsoft and others would like you to select that allow them to spy on you. Select "NO" for all the check-boxes during the set-up stage, to avoid prying eyes without limiting the performance of your machine.

Even though this computer comes with Windows 10, it does not have a touch screen. It has an impressive back-lit keyboard, including a 10-key pad and shortcut/soft keys. You can adjust the back-lighting of the keyboard and the screen to adapt to personal preference during daylight use or in a darkened room. The mouse pad works fine, but I prefer to use a wireless mouse for more control. This one was particularly sensitive to touch, which I found annoying. However, serious gamers may actually prefer this sensitivity. Either way, you can adjust the settings to suit your needs.

Although the screen on this computer is a few inches wider than my old laptop, the thickness of the computer is less. This means it fits more easily into a protective sleeve or case. The unit was surprisingly heavy--most likely due to the battery and other hardware. The power supply is about the size of a 3 x 5 inch card and considerably thinner than others I have seen. The cable seems thick, flexible and durable. It has a blue ring that lights up near the port when the unit is plugged in and charging. The battery seems to hold its charge for a long time, depending on what you do with the computer. Obviously, video or gaming will drain it faster than other applications.

You can tell there is a really great graphics card in this machine, as the images are as crisp and clear as a high-def TV screen. The speaker system is good, too. This makes video streaming and gaming pure pleasure. The processor is quite powerful, as well. However, don't try to do anything when your computer is downloading large updates, as it can affect the performance of your machine. I did notice, when typing in word-processing and email apps, that the flow of characters on the screen could be a bit choppy. This is not a big deal, but may be distracting to some users.

The software provided was pretty limited. There is a free trial of Microsoft Office 365, but it only lasts for five days. They want you to purchase or pay for licensing for their programs. However, you can find excellent free alternatives online, such as WPS Office Suite by Kingsoft or Softmaker Office. There are the usual proprietary games, browsers and other programs, including a free one-year subscription to McAfee security software.

There are lots of different kinds of data ports on this computer. There are two USB 3.0 ports and one with power share. There's a headset port, an HDMI port, a media card-reader, and a network port. You can keep your computer from being stolen by using the security cable slot. I wish there was a side-by-side set of ports for both a microphone and audio, as this will only work with a headset that has a single jack; my headset has two separate jacks.

Glaringly absent from this unit is a CD-Rom slot. I know CDs and DVDs are going the way of the dinosaur. However, I still have some favorite programs, movies, games and music on compact and video discs that I can't use on this device. I was able to transfer some using a cable and flash drive or network sharing. Nevertheless, I think this was a serious oversight in the design of a gaming computer. Depending on what kind of system you have, I am not sure there are enough of the right kind of ports to connect this computer to ancillary devices. You may need Bluetooth, wireless or physical adapters to hook up to other gaming equipment--such as control paddles, headsets, or your big-screen TV.

If you like to "see" your opponent when gaming, or enjoy Skyping friends and family, there is a camera built into this computer. I am inclined, however, to keep the lens covered with a sticky note when not in use. Call me paranoid, but the idea of someone being able to access and turn this on remotely to spy on me really creeps me out! There is a dual microphone with the camera, which I assume allows for communication in stereo.

Some users complained of exceptionally loud fans on this computer. Either I don't use enough resources to require them to run so heavily, or mine were in better shape than those people, because I did not notice anything out-of-the-ordinary.

I appreciate how easily this computer starts up and shuts down. Most of the other machines I am used to take their own sweet time--which means you have to allow yourself a few minutes before sitting down to work/play when you start up the machine or before you walk away when you are done.

title_x: Hesitates frequently and has a horrible, horrible LCD display
text:
In 2007 I bought a new FusionTech Worktop laptop, and in the ten years that followed I used the heck out of it. I edited thousands of documents, wrote software on it, even edited audio and video files, all running on a Socket 775 Core2 Duo processor. That laptop is still running today, although it can't compete with the processors and underlying architecture of new systems; they're just so much faster and more capable overall.

Fast forward to two weeks ago. I purchased this new "gaming" laptop, expecting a system that would meet my needs for today and years into the future. So far my experience with this "state of the art" laptop has been anything but great. Sure, it's nice to look at with the dull, almost rubbery outer coating, the sleek red lines and illuminated, full-size keyboard. The laptop is, on paper, a very capable system, and I so wish it would have been what I hoped, but alas it falls fall very short.

My two biggest complaints about this system by far are the display, and the unit's tendency to hang/hesitate.

The LCD display on this is atrocious. You have such a narrow vertical viewing angle that you simply can't view the whole screen at its optimal contrast at the same time. When you tilt the display to put the "sweet spot" across the middle, the upper and lower sections of the display show that telltale reflection common on older, and lower end LCD panels, that makes images look washed out, almost shiny or inverted. And even the portion of the screen that's optima has the dullest, most uninspiring color and contrast I've seen since LCD's first hit the market in the early 2000s. Imagine one of those old projection televisions in a bar, with 4-5 years of smoke and dust film on the lenses, and you have an idea how washed out and unimpressive is this display. The problem is the choice of technology: FusionTech chose an LCD panel that uses Twisted Numatic (TN) technology to render the pixels. It can't hold a candle to the newer Inter-Plane Switching (IPS) displays, which Apple uses almost exclusively due to their superior color and contrast, or the latest Organic LED (OLED) panels, which represent the very best in color and contrast. No, this panel is something you'd expect to see on a $49 no-name tablet, or an early ATM machine. I can't stop shaking my head over this, because IPS panels aren't but a few dollars more than TN panels, and it would have a HUGE difference in the overall look and usability of this product.

As bad as the LCD is, the other issue is much worse, by far. That is the laptop's tendency to hang or hesitate. I noticed this right out of the box, and even after wiping the drive and installing a pristine (i.e. bloatware-free) Windows 10 image, the system seems to hesitate, every few minutes, for anywhere from 5-15 seconds. The cursor pops up the "busy" spinning circle, and nothing responds to mouse clicks until seconds later. I've updated the drivers to the very latest version, shut down unneeded services, even flashed the UEFI BIOS to the latest version, but this hesitation continues, and it's bad enough that it's become a dealbreaker for me. I've read stories from other people who've had the same issue with this, so my gut tells me it's probably a behavior I'll have to learn to live with, and I'm just not willing to spend $800+ on something that can't do any better than that.

Sorry, Amazon, but I gotta send this stinker back.

Not sure if it's just me but this laptop gives me hell. I nicknamed it Satan for the red backlit keyboard and didn't realize how accurate that nickname would be. Obviously it's faster and better than my other very outdated slow-as-molasses laptop, but in some ways the functions became worse. I can't even run some of the programs I used to, which is absolutely infuriating, because the firewall (I assume) is so aggressive even after I've turned it off. Not sure I can really blame the laptop model for that problem. But I can, (probably), blame it for constantly shutting off my wifi without warning and sometimes taking minutes to toggle on/off before it will fix itself. I can't get an explanation why it randomly decides to do this to me. Maybe just a windows 10 thing.

But the worst problem which is distinctly a flaw of this laptop is when the entire thing crashes. It's only happened a couple times but when it happens it's Game Over. The keyboard stops responding, the screen freezes up, it makes a horrible screeching noise, and the power button does NOT work to turn off the computer. I'm not kidding, you can't turn the thing off whatsoever. It might be more bad luck or a deliberate design of the laptop, I'm not sure, but I can't even unscrew the back to try to remove the battery. The screw just turns and turns and turns and will never come out. Each time the laptop has crashed, I'm stuck with a frozen, endlessly screaming laptop and my only option is to stick it in another room where I can't hear it and wait for the battery to die. I'm just grateful I didn't have time-sensitive work to accomplish when the crashes happened, because it's already insanely frustrating. Fortunately, both times the laptop booted back up again just fine afterwards, and I can't be hassled to send it back. The funny thing is, I saw one review mentioning this problem and figured the odds were it wouldn't happen to me. Yeah. Don't be like me. Keep looking for something better, check the reviews, and spare yourself a lot of headache.
