title_x: Laptop is too expensive for screen quality this poor. Get the FusionTech Worktop 7567 instead.
text:
The display in this laptop is a low-quality-TN type panel with poor contrast and viewing angles, which is considerably worse than the typical TN desktop monitors often covered in comparison videos, and I would say frankly doesn't make sense for a laptop costing this much. Companies are too-often keen on offering upgrades over already-good CPU/RAM specs, while dropping the ball on very noticeable components the buyers don't always know to check or know what standards to have for, such as the display. This is one of such laptops.

This is the 5577 model, and the same used to be the case for the 7567 model, but FusionTech realized their mistake and partially addressed the problem by switching to an IPS panel on most sub-models in the USA and a few other regions. It is not a high-end IPS panel with 72% NTSC color gamut, but is a 45% NTSC IPS panel which I would say is to expect at the bracket this laptop is in.

The 7567 also offers a NVIDIA GTX 1050 Ti which is a bigger improvement over the GTX 1050 than the "i7" 7700HQ is over the "i5" 7300HQ, for most gaming. Intel's branding scheme I think is a bit misleading since basically any HQ-series outperforms any U-series regardless of the Core i-number, despite the i-number being the focus of most promotional materials, but that's an issue for another post. The main point I want to make here is that the Worktop 7567 is a more recommendable option to me because of its better GPU and much less poor quality display.

To get this, you need to choose the 7567 model and not the 5577 model you see in this listing, and you need to choose one that lists "IPS" for the display spec, since not all of them do. I recommend model FNCWF514S which has the IPS display, GTX 1050 Ti, and 256GB SSD. The RAM is upgradable, and the 2.5" HDD bay is left open for storage expandability.

You can choose to replace the display yourself, and if so I would probably recommend an AUO B156HAN01.2 or LG LP156WF6-SPB1 for 72% NTSC color gamut. That is the only case I think I could truly recommend the Worktop 5577, and it's still a tradeoff because you won't get the better GPU that the 7567 offers. So, if you buy one of these, invest in a separate mouse and disable that touch pad.

title_x: Its like a tuned up car where the doors get stuck and keep you from driving it
text:
Bought from a different distributer because of a sale. First laptop had weird hardware glitches such as one half of the screen being darker than the other and flickering. Mouse pad would randomly stop working. Also CPU intensive programs might blue screen the laptop when you leave them on idle for too long but you probably shouldn't do that anyway. I returned the first laptop and got my current one and the problems persisted. Despite this I've held onto the laptop because of its power, speed, and storage space. Tech support wasn't much help but at least the warranty would let me return it if I needed too. I let my warranty expire which is probably a bad move on my part but the hardware problems have pretty much gone away and never hindered the functionality of the machine itself.

The battery life isn't that bad as long as you keep in mind when you can get to outlets. It charges pretty fast and it's good for about 4 or so hours of consistent use on one charge. More if you're just doing basic tasks but if you're buying this you're probably going to either use it for games, music production, or 3-D modeling. Which is what I use it for. And I've never had any problems on that front.

It's nice and durable. The rubberized finish on top won't get scuffed any worse than any other laptop. Takes stickers well.

It has two hard-drives. Use them. The SSD isn't that big and things auto download to there. Do yourself a favor and take the extra five seconds to actually save things to the 1TB hard disc. Keeping the SSD clean makes sure the programs you actually want to launch from there are fast and all the things you don't use are organized.

Also for some reason when I use the HDMI to connect it to a TV and try to use a streaming service it doesn't work. I just use Chromecast now. It's faster anyway.

Its like a car where all the money was put into the engine and they kind of didn't care about the rest. So if you need something rugged and powerful this is it. It can take a beating and it'll be really strong. But it'll hit small snags inside itself every now and then that will make you hit the side of it trying to shake it loose. So far it fixes itself with a restart or with a bit of time. If you buy it you should just keep re-upping the warranty if you're planning on buying it and concerned.

title_x: Worst Computer I've Ever Had in 30+ Years of Computing
text:
I'm not a gamer, I'm a professional adult who mainly uses lightweight programs like Chrome, MS Word, and MS Excel, but I also occasionally shoot and edit marketing videos. Like anyone else, I also watch my fair share of YouTube and Netflix on my computer.

I spent *days* researching different computers and even looking at various builds in mini towers. I finally settled on this FusionTech, and I was initially happy with it. It was snappy.

But after I used it for a few months-- and now it's been about a year-- I started to have tons of problems.

First off, a direct problem with the hardware itself-- the computer runs hotter than a hibachi. I had to buy a four-fan base and prop the computer up at an angle just to get airflow to keep it cool. The actual fans on the FusionTech are loud as a wind tunnel, but thankfully the aftermarket fans are much quieter and keep the laptop cool.

The second problem is with the stupid design. The sharp angles look cool to some people I guess, but all they do is make the laptop more uncomfortable and likely to stag, chip, dent. The red keyboard keys are also really stupid. Yes, I guess they look cool when illuminated, but they never get really bright, and red is a very hard color to see at night or in the dark.

The third problem is memory management. I don't know if I got a lemon, or there's a fundamental problem with the design, but my laptop either seizes or crashes *daily* and I am not doing anything exotic with it like running bleeding-edge games. Hardly. But I get the blue screen of death daily, or the computer simply becomes irresponsible.

I'm out side the warranty period, so I'm out of luck. But I will never buy another FusionTech. I was alive when both Apple and IBM got started. I've been computing a long time, and I've owned 20+ machines in my life from various brands. This FusionTech laptop is absolutely, positively, and without any exaggeration or embellishment, the least reliable piece of crap I've ever owned.

title_x: Great Laptop After Much Research! Be careful though!
text:
In short: Good computer, BUT could have been a very bad purchase if I didn't create a 'restore point' right away.

In long:
I bought this computer after reading several others were having issues with the graphics card/windows. I received this laptop on 12/10/2018. I am writing this on 12/16/2018.

The first updates I did, the computer seemed fine. I then immediately went and saved off several restore points. For BOTH drives. I had read that others with the GTX 1050 Ti 4GB /Windows OS would sometimes shutdown when during game play, or regular use.

After saving off these restore points, I did the usual downloaded chrome, and started getting everything set up the way that I like it. After this was done, I again saved a restore point on both the SSD and the HDD. - VERY smart move. At this time only one of my monitors was working with the laptop. I usually have my laptop closed and have 2 x 22" monitors.

Next day there were several other Window's 10 updates. I figured I could download them and then try to figure out why both monitors wouldn't turn on. The update finished.

I plugged in both my external monitors, and attempted to connect them. Once i tried this the graphics card's shut down. Both the discrete GTX 1050 Ti and the built in Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 ( this one is built in on the processor) were disabled, and when i attempted to enable them - without the monitors plugged - they would run well. As soon as I plugged one of the monitors in both graphics cards would crash. Windows would then inform me "Display driver failed to start; using Microsoft Basic Display Driver instead. Check Windows Update for newer display driver".

I went online and read a bunch of other people talking about this very issue. More or less - as far as I could find there was no great fix for it. There were chats on reddit and elsewhere for almost one year... without a great answer.

I then went back to the restore point, and tried it all again. This time I did all of the driver updates, saved the restore point again, and then I plugged in the monitors. - and guess what - they both work well. I have then gone and updated Windows as it wanted me to do to. Now everything works.

SO I now have like 6 different restore points, because I would rather not have this happen again.

FYI:
I literally spent over 60 hours comparing different laptops to get the most bang for my buck. I also really wanted the Thunderbolt 3.

Here are my needs, I work in excel, working to learn more of SQL and other data base systems, like to watch youtube, movies, recreationally look stuff up online, look at things online for future business purposes, and I have 500GB of music, I am a total audiophile. Honestly this computer is/was totally overkill. But thats what I wanted. Something that would work well for at least the next 4-5 years, and be able to keep my two 22" monitors running well.

Main reason why I chose this laptop is because it has the Thunderbolt 3 attachment. In all honesty, I do not use it, but I know in the future it will become far more relevant.
Here are the specs:
-Core™ i7-8750H
-NVIDIA® GeForce® GTX 1050 Ti 4GB
-1TB HDD + 256GB SSD Storage
-16GB RAM
G5587-7835BLK

Miscellaneous info - On the laptop monitor - I was worried about the monitor not being connected all the way across. I was thinking I might accidentally bend or break it. I feel pretty confident about it now, that i have one.

Also the charger chord for it is quite large. Just an FYI.
I hope this info helps future buyers.

title_x: Very, very good, but not great. Get the larger SSD
text:
Overall this is a very, very good product. Graphics are great, computer is fast, very stylish. However the 128 GB SSD C: drive is way too small. Virtually every additional program you install defaults to the C: drive for program files and data storage. I crashed my C: drive when my Microsoft "one drive" attempted to download my pre-existing data files from the old computer to the new computer's C: drive. My Microsoft Office 365 re-installation puts my huge existing data files (mostly huge Outlook .PST files) on the C: drive. If you are fairly computer literate you can overcome these issues, but novices will have difficulties.

The problem is not with the computer. Software products, including Microsoft, simply have not adapted to the dual SSD/HD configuration options to allow minimal installations on the SSD drives and huge data files on another drive.

Also the FusionTech installation includes the dreaded SmartByte program which throttles my 1 GB/sec Ethernet connection down to a snail's pace. Deleting Smartbyte solves that issue, but each FusionTech "update' re-installs Smartbyte.

I would definitely but this again, but only with at least a 256 GB

title_x: Run it hard, run it long
text: So I just bought what was a mid-priced notebook at your neighborhood “value” store less than a year ago. And as an ex I.T. geek you’d think I’d know better. But at the time anything was better than what I was running!  Anyhow, it wasn’t long before waiting 5 minutes to boot and another 10 minutes for enough processes to calm down so the mouse would respond it really started to irritate the ____ out of me. After a little homework I couldn’t be happier with my choice of the FusionTech G5587.  Just remember to load as many of your programs that you can to your D: drive (that good ole SATA HD with lots of room) and check the setup and/or options within the programs you run, change those default locations to D:/whatever/you/name/it. I am very impressed with the response times of this notebook and even more impressed with the lack of any “nope I’m not going to respond for awhile” experiences. I was running this system with two monitors, extending to 21.4” HDMI monitor. Then I remembered my old USB mini-monitor was still around and hooked it up too. And now everything except the power cord and one USB C (Thunderbolt) cable has been yanked from my notebook.  That lone USB C cable plugs into a WavLink 5k dual display hub and all those phone /tablet /watch /Pencil /vaporizer / flashlight and every other product that wants a USB charger these days had their plugs removed from my notebook. Only one issue, that does say “dual display hub” doesn’t it?  Yeah, I added another 21.4” HDMI monitor. So that’s a total of four monitors now. I run the full Office Suite, as well as some intense flight sims, and this machine hasn’t missed a beat yet. PS:  As I’m a small cog in Microsoft’s world this machine has to deal with versions of Windows the public will never see. It’s always a very tense moment when your machine reboots after installing (hopefully) the latest weekly update. However, between the built in support apps from FusionTech, intel, and others she’s always come back to me (so far).  Would I recommend this notebook?  Duh, wadda u thunk

text:
I waited a while before writing this review in case anything came up. Which it did, but it didn't have anything to do with the PC hardware..
This is a really good laptop. It's lightweight and running windows on a SSD definitely makes a difference! I've been wanting a computer that had the OS on a SSD for years now and I finally have it in this affordable little gem. The laptop itself isn't much to look at. It does have nifty red back-lighting to the keyboard, which is nice as I'm frequently in a dark room. I do wish it offered more color options for the back-light, but I'm satisfied with what I have. I do wish it was a little easier to navigate the partitions though. Since the OS is on the first partition the system defaults to trying to put literally everything on the C:/ drive. It would be more convenient if I could figure out how to get photos and docs to autosave to the D:/ drive and if my quick links linked to the second partition (D:/ drive).. There probably is a way to do it, I just haven't done it yet.
The only issue I have had with the laptop didn't have anything to do with the laptop hardware, it was an OS issue. The PC I purchased is a refurb, which is fine for me, but someone forgot to take the retail OS off the PC and put the OEM OS on so it ended up throwing notifications that my windows license was about to expire, which Amazon took care of. They ended up crediting my account so I could purchase another version of windows and install myself. While it was annoying to have to go out of my way to do work on, what is to me, a new laptop but it worked out fine. Overall I give this laptop a 9 out of 10. You get what you pay for, luckily this PC is a really good mid-range gaming laptop. I'm satisfied with my purchase.

text:
The FusionTech G5 15 is a step up from my previous laptop, and it works well for both business and personal use. It runs games as recent as Resident Evil: Village with only a few decreases in video quality needed. Its memory is divided up into 100 GB SD and 900 GB HD - programs and files on the SD will load quicker, so it is best to store most of your data on the HD if you don't mind it taking longer to load. Its battery life is strong as well.

My only complaint is that its fans are noisy, especially when you are playing a demanding game. It can also heat up fairly quickly, so I would recommend getting a cooling pad to go with it.

Overall, the pros of the laptop outweigh its cons. I wanted a higher-end gaming laptop without going over budget, and this model delivered on what I had hoped for. I purchased my model in December 2018, and it is still going strong as of writing. I would recommend it to people who want a compact, portable, and powerful gaming machine that can still work well with everyday applications.

text:
I bought a FusionTech G5 15 with an extremely similar configuration to this from FusionTech through my university's bookstore and I would say that this is a good entry level gaming laptop. It should run pretty much everything except for the most demanding titles (e.g. Ark: Survival Evolved) without too many problems, with the only issue being that it runs hot so it may be worth it to buy a cooling pad or something like that. Also, the fans sound like a jet engine under load but that's probably due to this being a laptop and not a desktop so take that into consideration as well. Also, the keyboard is really nice which is a plus.

The only major cons of this machine in my opinion are that:

a) The speakers are weak, so if you're used to better speakers or are hard of hearing that might be a problem

b) I wish the laptop had a second USB port on the left side (it has 3 total USB ports, 2 on the right one on the left) otherwise the port selection is pretty good (3 USB ports, SD Card reader, HDMI port, ethernet port, etc.) but if you're not using too many peripherals this won't be that big of an issue.

All in all, after a little over a week of use, I can say that this is a good entry level gaming laptop and would give it a 9/10 and would recommend if you're looking for a laptop like this.

text:
I've had this laptop for a couple months. I don't like when people write reviews after a couple days or one day of use - they're useless reviews written out of excitement for a new product.

Anywho - after using this laptop now for a couple months, it is pretty solid! It runs games very well. The only game I encountered that needed some adjustments to a lower graphic setting was ARK: Survival. Yet, it can still run the game and pretty well at that. Most games will run at MAX settings.

-Battery life is poor if unplugged and gaming. That's not exclusive to this laptop, just about any laptop will blow through the battery when running games unplugged. How can you write a poor review about this subject when you should know good and well you're not going to get 5-6 hours on unplugged gaming? Anyway.

-Battery life is pleasant if not gaming. I don't have exact data in regards to how long it last unplugged with light work vs gaming. I haven't taken the time to do that. However, I can say the battery goes noticeably quick while gaming, and doesn't while doing normal browsing/work. With that being said...

-This is a solid laptop for business purposes. Although I have tested several different games (ARK: Survival, World of Warcraft, Fifa 18, Star Wars Battlefront 2, etc..), I don't use this for gaming, at all. Again, I have tried several different games and ran them for hours on in. But I've since deleted them as I needed this laptop for business reasons. The reason I've mentioned gaming primarily so far is because I understand that this is what this laptop is geared for and marketed towards.
- *Note: The laptop runs hot while gaming. If this is an issue, don't game on laptops. This issue isn't exclusive to this laptop, rather it's an issue with laptops in general - until technology advances in this area, there isn't enough room to ventilate the air (like in a desktop computer) so the laptops will run hot in high-intensity usage like gaming.

-Again, I bought mine for business reasons. I wanted something that could execute anything I needed, swiftly. No matter how intense. This laptop will do everything you need it to do from a business perspective (for the vast majority of people) regardless of intensity. It's an A+ for me.

title_x: Great Value and Good Casual Gaming System...maybe a bit more!
text: I purchased this machine Nov 2018 and took advantage of Black Friday/Cyber Monday deal and paid well under $1000 for the system.  At $879 -- it is a deal!  If you are paying over $950...you might as well upgrade to the 17" screen.  Me I need a compact gaming only system and this is it.  It runs Fallout 4 flawlessly (which is definitely saying something if anyone knows Bethesda) The set up is fast and is not troublesome in anyway (the noise mentioned in other reviews is negated by even a cheap set of earbuds.  My main critique is the pointing device.  It is HUGE and gets in the way when you are gaming using your keyboard.  It took quite a while to master the ergonomics of not tapping it while playing.  I you do purchase this system I recommend one of the inexpensive optical drives, an inexpensive set of ear phones, and a cheap mouse.  My total for those accessories cost way less than $20.  I highly recommend this system -- it is for the casual gamer not the hardcore living life in the virtual world crowd.  It feels fairly rugged but I worry about the stiffness of the earphone jack, anything with those tight tolerances will surely be trouble and I will update my review should it ever become a real problem.  256 SSD is the right size and the 1TB HD is more than sufficient.  I find the screen just right for me.  Overall a good buy if the price is under $1000 however, there are other systems you should look for if you want to spend more than that.

title_x: Was a great laptop until today.
text:
I've had this laptop just about a year. The performance has been great up until now, and then it just died today. Was working fine up until this morning, I closed the lid, and a few hours later, it won't turn on. Completely dead. Fortunately I had about 30 more days on my warranty, but I still have to mail it in, and wait about 2 weeks for them to work on it.

It's been very good for games, and performance has been fine. The outside, as people have said, is very plain and has a cheap plastic feel. I like the backlit keyboard, the screen has a nice sharp picture, and I've been happy with it.

Major cons for me, not including it's death today... The laptop has two hard drives. Unfortunately, everything default installs on the smaller hard drive, and you have to manually move things, change settings, etc in order to get it onto the second (and larger hard drive). I am not enamored with Windows 10, but that is not FusionTech's fault and so far it is running all my legacy programs including Adobe CS4 applications like Photoshop, Dreamweaver, InDesign, Illustrator and Acrobat Pro. So no real complaints about Windows 10.

Some of the reviews suggest the fans are loud on this machine. I have no issues with noise at all. I can't hear the fans, but do feel the slight air flow from the vents. While I do like the red backlit keyboard, I do wish it would stay on at all times. When I look down after a short period of inactivity, I have to tap a key to light the keyboard. A small annoyance.

I have not put it through its gaming paces as most of my games are too old to run on Windows 10, but that is not why I bought this machine. I do have some concerns over the durability of the laptop as evidenced by a couple of reviews here, but so far it seems as sturdy as my previous machines. I am treating it with kid gloves, however. No reason to tempt fate and it should be treated carefully for what it cost and what it does.

On balance, you will not find a laptop with a trusted brand name with these specs at a better price.

About a week later, I'm a bit disappointed, because the back of the computer scratches very easily. Because of that, it lost its wow factor fairly quickly. The touch pad is also a magnet for finger smudges.

I read some complaints about the keyboard, but I don't have a huge problem with it. As a writer, a keyboard is one of the few things that can make or break a computer for me. title_x: Best laptop I've owned in years despite thermal issues - UPDATE 05/20/2019
text:
UPDATES 05/20/2019 - original review below.

After a few weeks with the laptop, I have noticed some issues with the laptop. Namely, thermal and WiFi. I've dropped by review from 5 to 4 stars.
None of these issues are deal breakers and I still love this laptop, but let me explain so you are aware going in.

Thermal: the intel i7 processor on this machine is a beast and it produces a lot of heat. Unfortunately, the design of the laptop is so thin that it has no great way to dissipate heat. When the i7 goes up to nearly 4GHz (the turbo boost on it) it usually throttles (clocks down) because the temps of the processor will go up to 90 or so Celcius at least on my machine, (max temp being 100 C). Additionally this will make the fans go kind of whacky. There are a few fixes (and you can implement multiple), one of which I chose to do and it resolved my issue. The first fix is you can undervolt your processor. This requires software called intel xtu. I didn't mess around with this option. The second option is re-pasting your processor, and installing thermal pads on your heat sinks to draw the heat from the processor and GPU to the bottom case to dissipate the heat correctly. This, in addition to the intel XTU are your options if you NEED 4 GHz. The last option, which worked perfect for me was to turn off TurboBoost in the BIOS (very easy). This permanently clocks your processor down to 2.2 Ghz - which for me, was way more than enough performance. I'm able to game at the exact same FPS as with turbo boost, as well as photo editing without any noticeable slowdown. All I've seen from doing this is better temps and no more crazy fans. Again, this isn't a dealbreaker for me and I don't think it should be for you. If it is, and you NEED 4GHz either be prepared to do some work to fix it, or you should consider a gaming machine that dissipates heat better.

The second issue is the WiFi card. The Killer 1535 card included in this machine has some issues. I am replacing it with an Intel 9260 (very inexpensive Wifi Card and easy to do) to deal with these issues. The issues with the card are random disconnects somewhat infrequently, but the 9260 is a cheap easy fix. Driver updates didn't seem to help.

I still love this laptop despite these issues.

ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW

After owning a FusionTech Latitude E5450 for the last few years, I decided it was time for an upgrade. I set out on a research hunt for a laptop that had high build quality, great performance (preferably with a dGPU), good battery, as compact as possible and not overly expensive. I also wanted a strong 4k panel. Those are some tough requirements to meet, but the FusionTech ABC 15 9570 exceeded my expectations in these areas.

I've owned a lot of laptops in my lifetime, everything from an Apple Powerbook 150 to a GPD Win, to fat gaming laptops. Out of all of the laptops I've ever owned, this is easily my favorite. Over the last few years I've been fairly disappointed in the direction of Apple and have found myself leaning more and more towards FusionTech, and as far as I can tell their quality has only gotten better.

BUILD QUALITY
The build quality of this machine is unbelievable for the price. Although styled differently, I feel like I am holding a machine on par with the quality of a MacBook Pro.

PERFORMANCE
The performance of this machine is great, especially for how thin and light it is. The i7 CPU has 6 cores. It's faster than many desktop processors even on the market right now. 16 GB of RAM should be enough for anything you'll run aside from some video processing type tasks. The GTX 1050Ti Max-Q is a fantastic card as well. It's about on par with a 960M in terms of performance (not quite as good as a true 1050ti). Although I don't use this for heavy gaming, I'm able to play Playerunknown's battlegrounds on 1080P with about 50-60 FPS on average. The NVME SSD is snappy. When doing photo editing tasks, the machine doesn't have a single issue.

THERMAL
The laptop stays pretty cool, even under fairly heavy loads. I haven't done any empirical tests, but during heavy gaming the keyboard gets a little warm as does the underbody. Nothing that doesn't happen on any other laptop with this kind of hardware. I did not notice any throttling of the i7 CPU (monitored with task manager) during gaming either. The fans will go on in these situations but this doesn't bother me at all; I'd rather have a cool laptop with fan noise than a hot one with none.

DISPLAY
The display on this is the best part of this whole package. I have the 4K screen and I highly recommend it. The colors are perfect on it, it pops and looks perfect, especially for creative tasks where color is important. I wouldn't recommend the 4k if you have extremely high battery demands or perhaps if you're a hardcore gamer; the 1080p screen would probably be better for you. The 4K screen will probably set you back an hour or two of battery time, and for gaming in FHD on it, it will look a bit weird downscaling to 1080P on a 4K monitor...but to me, the 4K is worth it for the colors and pure beauty.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is flawless in my opinion. About as good as you can get for a laptop keyboard. The tactile response is perfect, the sound is clicky enough to be engaging but not loud enough to be annoying. Backlit keyboard is a nice touch too.

BATTERY LIFE
Battery life is fairly good for the specs that are in this, with a 97+Whr battery. With keyboard lights off, battery set to high battery life mode in Windows 10, and FusionTech Power Command set to Optimal, I get about 6 hours with moderate use (web browsing, Photoshop Lightroom CC). This is totally acceptable to me. With the 1080P screen you'd probably get 6-8 hours. With heavy use (such as gaming) don't expect more than 1 - 1.5 hours.

SERVICEABILITY
From what I can tell, this machine is fairly serviceable, especially by today's standards. The RAM and SSD are easily user replaceable, and I'd argue that the battery is as well.

Honestly, I can't think of anything bad to say about this laptop. Maybe that I wish the battery life was a little bit better, but this isn't FusionTech's fault and I can't knock the machine for it. The hardware in it is some high end power hungry stuff. They somehow stuffed nearly a 100 Whr battery in here which helps a lot but I'm not sure there was much else they could do.

Any other questions and I will try to answer them in comments. This here is a keeper.

The FusionTech ABC 15 9570-8th Generation Intel Core i7-8750H Processor, 4k Touchscreen display, 16GB DDR4 2666MHz RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050Ti, Windows 10 Home, Gaming Capable is a very good computer. I have had it for a few months, and I have had no problems with it. It functions exactly as a computer should, and works like all the other FusionTechs I have owned over the years (my wife uses FusionTechs for her job). The laptop market is crowded, and it is hard to find the perfect product. Here are some things to know:
1. Is it fast?
For everyday usage, it is plenty fast enough. If you plan to use the internet, type in Word, or do a school project, this computer will meet your needs.
2. Is it fast enough to play games?
The description says that is it gaming capable, which only means that it can play games, but does not mean it can play the most graphic demanding games at its highest setting. Yes, every game I played (all from Steam) worked fine. I let each game determine the settings, and they all worked. When I checked the settings, there were still even high setting available, and changing to those setting did slow down the game. If you are a hardcore gamer, I am guessing you will want a computer designed for high end games. If you are casual gamer, this will do the job.
3. How is the keyboard and track pad layout?
I had no problem with the keyboard, but the track pad uses the modern setup I find on most computers. It is big and can get in the way while typing. The pad is one big button, but there is a left and right side. I often have to look down to click. This is why I use a mouse, but sometimes, that is not an option. The track pad will suffice, but it is far from perfect.
4. How is the software?
It uses Windows 10. I had to do a huge update when I turned it on. So far, I have no problems with Windows 10.
5. Is it quiet?
Under normal conditions, the computer is quiet. Playing a game, of course, required more power, and therefore, the fans speed up. I did not find it any louder than any other laptop.

Overall, this is a good computer from FusionTech. I see this computer as a great entry way to laptop gaming, or a student going off to college. It has the power to do most things, but hardcore gamers would probably buy a better laptop anyway. So far the computer has been reliable and completed every task I asked it to do. I recommend this laptop.

title_x: Beautiful Computer, #1 Macbook Pro Competitor, Poor Thermals
text:
Pros:
I've had this computer for almost two years now, and it is quite a beast. I mainly got it to edit photos and videos with. The 4k screen BEAUTIFUL, has amazing color accuracy, and my color grading on edits is true to what I see on the screen, which is amazing. The brightness is quite good. When browsing the net, I usually turn down the brightness as it hurts my eyes it gets so bright.

Very professional looking machine. I'm not ashamed to take it to meetings with me. The chassis is extremely solid and high end feeling. I added a D-Brand skin to the lid to give it a different look. The aluminum case construction is very rigid and does not flex. The feet hold the computer solidly in place on the table and on your lap (would not recommend as the case gets quite hot under load). The rubber on the palm rests is comfortable and expensive feeling, and the touchpad is frosted glass, like a Macbook. It would be nice if it was bigger, but it is great how it is.

I/O is great, for 2020, with two USB-A ports, 1 USB-C, 1 HDMI, an elusive headphone jack, and a SD card reader, which was essential for me.

The upgradeability is good for a newer laptop as well, with upgradable ram and an upgradeable SSD. I use a 4tb external drive to store most of my work on, but it is nice to have the option to upgrade the internal drive as well.

The power button is a fingerprint reader and works very nicely with Windows Hello.

Cons:

Closing the lid
This is not a FusionTech issue, as much as it is an Intel issue, but closing the lid on this machine WILL NOT put the machine asleep. It stays on to receive notifications while it is "sleeping." INTEL. I DO NOT need the computer to stay on when I am driving home to get emails. It will come to my phone. If you shut the lid, and stick it in your bag, when you take the computer out it will either be extremely hot, or dead, depending on how long it is in there. Why can my 2013 MacBook Pro sleep for months at a time and this computer cannot sleep overnight without dying? Every time I put this computer in my backpack (which is every day because I take it to work with me) I have to shut it down so it doesn't die or melt.

The thermals.
Don't let the 1050 Ti fool you, this computer is NOT a gaming machine. Even running a light game, like CS:GO, it thermal throttles. I have re-pasted the CPU and GPU with Thermal Grizzly, added small heatsinks to the VRMS on the motherboard, and undervolted the CPU and GPU, all to try and stop this computer from throttling. Nothing will stop it. Even disabling the Turbo function on the CPU only buys you a few more minutes until it thermal throttles. While gaming, the CPU clocks down to 800 mhz, causing huge in game lag, until it can get the thermals back under control with its jet engine fans, usually taking around 15-30 seconds. The i7 8750H is bad, I can't imagine how awful the i9 would be in this machine. It would probably perform on an i5 level or worse.

The charger.
FusionTech uses a proprietary 130 watt charger with this computer. It will not run at full power with just a USB-C charger and dock. The connector on the charger is very small, and does not fit very snug in the computer. I've never had it fall out or break, but I have been EXTREMELY careful not to put any pressure on the tiny, fragile plug. I usually only have it plugged in on my desk.

The web-cam placement
I never thought this would be an issue, then 2020 rolled around and virtual meetings became the new norm. FusionTech has fixed this with the newer models, but I'm not buying another $2000 computer for different webcam placement. The webcam is located at the bottom of the screen on the 9570, giving your Zoom conference call a nice view of your knuckles while typing and a quality shot of any nose hairs you might have missed while trimming. I've included a picture of how the angle looks.

Over all, I have enjoyed this computer, and would consider buying another ABC, depending on FusionTech addressing the issues above. The i7 and i9 MacBook Pros have similar thermal issues, with less I/O

I'm almost wholly a Mac girl these days. But every so often I need a Windows computer, usually because a work assignment requires it. I'm not trying to do video processing or play computer games on a Windows laptop. That means I need a "regular" PC, though my needs rarely are demanding. Overall, I find this a perfectly adequate Windows system. I could spout off all the technical specifications -- Intel Core i7, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050Ti -- but I was never expecting to stress its system performance. Mostly, I (accurately, as turns out) expected to be irritated by figuring out Windows 10; as with most versions of Windows, my first guess at how to do something new-to-me usually is inaccurate and I do a lot of cussing. (I switched to Macs long ago because they did not violate the principle of least astonishment.) But that's certainly not the fault of the FusionTech hardware; it's purely a wetware problem.

Mostly, I looked for hardware usability. I'm not planning to take the computer anywhere; if I were, I'd point out that 6.25 pounds weighs a lot more in a backpack than you think it does. I like using its fingerprint scanner instead of typing in a password. There are enough built-in ports that I do not feel an immediate need to buy any additional hardware.

All of the product specs are up to date. That is, this isn't the most advanced computer one could buy; nor is it a laggard. I expect I can use this system for several years... and that's what I was hoping for.

After having this laptop for 6 months now.... here is what to expect:
* at first, laptop needs breaking in, update all bios and drivers before installing your programs.
* get an ipearl cover, helps elevate the laptop in addition to protecting it. Which will helps in cooling it.

I recommend to apply this solution (at your own risk!) in addition to the suggested ones on the internet
* Random BSODs caused by (iaStorAVC.sys) is actually an Intel issue, Raid drivers (that are not needed in the larger battery model since there is no Raid) are not very friendly. Just uninstall Intel raid and the issue will go forever.
* FusionTech has sadly limited the GPU performance in the latest Bios updates to solve overheating issues... I think all it needs is a spring screw to put enough pressure on the cooling blocks.

title_x: it's a great machine. The 8th gen i7 gives it twice ...
text:
Blazing fast laptop with room to upgrade. As is, it's a great machine. The 8th gen i7 gives it twice the cores as before (except for the battery-draining HQ version). The HDD that comes included is only a 5400rpm but has a small hybrid SSD integrated which allows for it to optimize and speed up over time with use (it puts only the most frequently accessed files on the very limited SSD space). The hybrid drive isn't as fast as an SSD but it's much faster than a standard HDD (well, once the drive learns what it need to cache). And, if you decide later on that you need to get one of those fancy SSDs, you can use the empty m.2 slot for an affordable drive for the OS and keep the 1tb HDD for everything else.

The discrete graphics card also allows for a huge speed bump on graphics-intensive programs. The nvidia management app allows you to select which programs you want to use the 940MX for and which ones to use the Intel integrated graphics. Honestly, the vast majority of my programs are run with the integrated graphics chip but it's great to know that I can unleash the nvidia down the line when I need it.

The 8gb of RAM that this comes equipped with is very adequate for most purposes. This, however, is one of the ever-fewer laptops that allows for substantial expansion if needed. There are 2 slots which can accommodate up to 16gb each which is hard to beat in this price range.

The display looks great although it doesn't have quite the brightness range of other models. It absolutely doesn't max out as bright as it could but I tend to live at the other end of the brightness slider and haven't had any complaints in my usage. I have had intermittent problems with the touchscreen (once per week or two it stops accepting touch input) but it's always come back to life after a quick restart.

Only this is better than that PowerBook because it has no proprietary connectors or ports, and offers things like the multi-format card slot, and the ability to easily upgrade the RAM or add an M2 SSD. It's slim, light (for the size), and that 180-degree hinge is awesome for when you're chilling on the couch and want to interact with the laptop using a stylus on the screen instead of messing around with the touchpad (which is, by the way, very well made and sensitive, with both a right and left button).

The graphics power is acceptable. I got Skyrim running, but it ran pretty slow (looked beautiful, though!) and I suspect if I turned down the graphic to the lowest setting it would have been playable (but since I have it on another device, I don't really need it on my laptop). I tried other, less graphically intensive games like Fire Pro Wrestling World, Plague Inc Evolved, and Shadowrun Returns, and all ran very nicely. I wouldn't call this a gaming PC, but it does an okay job with older or more simple games. That GeForce 940MX comes in most handy when doing things with multimedia, especially video. It handles encoding, editing, and converting video pretty well-- Certainly better than the Intel graphics on most laptops, anyway. Having a recent i7 helps a lot, too, no doubt.

The USB 3.0 ports, USB C port, and HDMI port (yes, a full-size HDMI port! None of that HDMI-mini stuff here!) are all spaced apart enough to fit in even the thickest of cables and dongles without intruding on the neighboring ports. That's good design, and I appreciate little touches like that.

The speakers are surprisingly decent, though they could be a touch louder.

The i7570 doesn't get hot in your lap unless you're really doing something CPU-intensive. Otherwise, it's quiet and cool.

The bottom line: This is a laptop for someone who wants to do some work that requires a bit of a graphics and CPU boost over the standard laptops out there, but it's not quite a gaming laptop. You'll be satisfied with some basic or older games, but don't expect to load the latest (or even last-gen) AAA games and expect 60fps. You might be able to do last-gen AAA titles at 30fps on low or medium settings, though. As a general-use PC for multimedia viewing/listening, web surfing, video editing/creation, music editing/creation, general artwork, writing, and some light gaming, it's aces in my book. It does the job and then some, and it does it in sleek, slim, beautiful package.

I'll give this one five stars as a general use and multimedia PC. However, I'd say if you're looking for a gaming laptop, you can consider it three stars ("It's Okay"), but I'd lean you toward something with a beefier GPU than the 940MX for gaming. Just be aware that more graphics power means, more than likely, less battery life and a thicker build. The Worktop i7570 is what I'd call a great compromise between gaming and multimedia in a laptop. I like it a lot.

title_x: Solidly built gaming laptop for the price point
text:
Pros:
* Good thermals. Gets too hot to play on your lap, but not so hot it will burn a hole in your desk.
* Solid build. No part of this laptop seems flimsy or poorly built.
* Great graphics for a laptop. The RTX 3060 isn't pushing boundaries, but it's good enough to play new games at high to ultra settings at 1080p.
* Decent battery life. You're not going to game for 12 hours straight on this thing without plugging it in, but it will last at least 4-5 hours under heavy load on a single charge, more if you use power saver settings.

Cons:
* Very heavy. Like you could break into a car with this laptop, heavy.
* Very loud under heavy loads. The fans do a great job a dissipating heat. The downside of this is that they sound like a hurricane. It's definitely a laptop you need headphones to play on.
* Mediocre display. The display isn't bad, but it isn't great either. The colors don't really "pop" like modern gaming monitors and Apple displays and the contrast is mediocre.

title_x: A fast and capable Windows 10 desktop replacement laptop
text:
#### Appearance, materials, etc.

This is a standard laptop with a touchscreen. Unlike some Windows 10 laptops, it does not have a 180º hinge that flips the screen back to “presentation mode” or make it turn into a tablet.

In terms of overall construction, it is a black plastic laptop encased in silver anodized aluminum. It is slightly wedge shaped, and strives to look thinner than it actually is.

#### Portability

I put this laptop in the “desktop replacement” class. Despite the extra small bezels around its screen, it appears to have been optimized for performance rather than for size and weight. The FusionTech’s length and width exactly match those of my 2013 15” MacBook Pro. Its height (on the hinge end), when closed, is almost a quarter inch more than the old MacBook Pro, too. It is much heavier than the MacBook Pro, as well. I am pretty sensitive to size and weight when putting laptops in my bag, but the way I use this laptop—around the house—they do not matter that much.

#### Keyboard and track pad

The parts of the laptop that you will touch all the time feel very good.

The keyboard and trackpad feel good to the touch and work with great accuracy on Windows 10. Trackpads on Windows PCs traditionally lagged behind Apple MacBook trackpads in terms of quality, but I think the FusionTech’s trackpad is great. It is not oversized, like the newer Apple laptops, or crowded with hardware buttons, like on Lenovo Yoga laptops, or weirdly textured, like on the HP Satellite.

The keyboard is really good. It has good travel, properly sized keys, a sensible layout, And a T-shaped arrow cluster. There is far greater travel than the current generation of MacBook Pros, and about the same as the Lenova Yoga I use for work every day. I think I type more accurately on the Yoga, but I think I just need more time to get used to the key feel and key travel on the FusionTech. One minor nit about the keyboard: the bumps or ridges on the bottom of the F and K keys are very hard to feel, which makes it harder than I would like to get my fingers into typing position without looking at the keyboard.

The area around the keyboard is black, soft-touch plastic. It feels nice, and never felt cold (like aluminum cases do) or hot (when the fans blow). Its edges are rolled off, ever so slightly, so typing is always a comfortable experience. I absolutely hated the Intel sticker that was on it, but, to my surprise, it peeled off easily and left no residue behind.

The track pad reminds me of MacBook Pro trackpads from about 5-6 years ago, before they got comically large. It is a normal-sized, clicky trackpad with no physical buttons and a pleasantly smooth surface. It worked perfectly for accurate pointing and multi-finger gestures. It is the best trackpad of all my Windows laptops.

The power button, which sits to the right of the keyboard, contains a fingerprint sensor, which works very much like Touch ID does on an (older) iPhone or iPad. In my experience, setting up and using the sensor was quick and easy. Windows 10 allows you to log in with a fingerprint, which is fast and worked flawlessly.

#### The screen

The 4K, 15.6” LCD touch-enabled display is gorgeous. Everything about it is good. Colors pop on the default Windows wallpaper, but look accurate to me on my photos. The 4K resolution works very well at this screen size: text is very sharp. Screen brightness is fantastic, too. Many Windows laptops I have used have rather dim screens, which make Them almost impossible to use outside (even in shade) or near sunny windows (at the local coffeeshop, say). The FusionTech’s screen can get very, very bright, which provides far greater flexibility and visibility than I expected. The screen has an integrated touch panel, which I don't use all the time, but I absolutely love, because it makes Windows 10 a little easier to use.

#### Ports

There is a mishmash of ports on each side, which make it versatile for all kinds of uses. On the left, you have a power port, USB 3 Type A, HDMI, USB C, and a headphone/microphone jack. On the right you have another USB 3 Type A port and an SD card reader. While I welcome these various ports (especially the SD card reader), if you are all-in on USB-C, you may be disappointed. The single USB-C port is the best option for a monitor cable (at least for my monitor, which does not support 4K/60 over HDMI, but does over DisplayPort or USB-C). The USB Type A ports are perfect for plugging in a mouse and keyboard, without requiring a hub or an adapter.

#### Charging

The included power adapter is not USB-C. It is a huge brick with a long, light-up cable that has a circular plug. I did some online research which led me to believe that the USB-C port cannot be used for charging unless your charger pushes at least 60 watts. That means that you can’t trickle-charge your laptop with something smaller, like a tablet or smartphone charger. My ChromeBook came with a 45-watt charger, which I thought was standard for modern laptops, so a 60-watt charger seems pretty powerful to me. You absolutely do not need to use USB-C charging to use this laptop, but it is good to know what you can and cannot do.

#### Performance

Overall, this computer is fast. It is easily the fastest Windows laptop I have ever used, though my nearest point of comparison is a 2-year-old Lenovo Yoga Core i5 system, which is not a fair comparison point. I use it mainly for programming: Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, SQL Server Express, etc. Those heavyweight applications launch pretty fast. Compile times are snappy, and the computer (with 16 GB or RAM) does not get bogged down or resource starved throughout the day.

I have not stressed it too much with my normal computing activities. The fan does come on sometimes, and the fan exhaust goes straight down through rather large vents on the bottom of the case. This is only a problem if you are litterally using this computer on your lap. If it is on a table top, little feet on the bottom of the case prop it up so that the exhaust has somewhere to go. If you use a machine on your bed, or over a blanket that would plug up the exhaust holes, you might want to reconsider that before buying this machine, or look to a different laptop that vents out the back.

I have seem YouTube videos that claim that this laptop’s Core i9 variant runs hot and throttles, which would make the Core i7 model the sweet spot for price-to-performance ratio.

#### Problems

The only problems I have with this machine are Windows 10-related, rather than hardware-related.

My first day with it was, in a large part, wasted on software updates from Microsoft, FusionTech, and other third parties who have software pre-installed. Also, after running through a couple update-and-reboot cycles, Windows 10 told me that it was not activated. I had to click the “Troubleshoot” button in Windows activation settings to fix it. It is the sort of thing that should not happen, but fortunately it did not cause me much downtime.

Waking the computer up is also problematic. Most of the time, it takes a few presses of the power button to wake up Windows. Once Windows wakes, everything is fine.

#### Overall impressions

Overall, this is a very capable machine for software development. I particularly like the bright, sharp screen and the zippy Core i7 processor. Due to its overall size and weight, I consider it a desktop replacement, rather than an ultraportable, laptop.

title_x: Move over desktop. You’re being replaced.
text:
The specs on this new FusionTech ABC 15 7590 model laptop definitely got my attention: 4K UHD touch screen display, 9th gen Intel i7 processor, 16 GB of RAM, 1 TB SSD, 4 GB dedicated graphics memory and the fastest Wi-Fi available plus a few extras including a back-light keyboard, fingerprint reader, SD card reader and Thunderbolt capability.
Over the last week I’ve been giving this system a tryout and here’s what I’ve discovered.
The screen is glossy and beautiful offering an almost invisible bezel. Photos have true blacks and colors are vibrant. Play a 4K video and you will be drawn right in. Out of the box, the display was too bright and had to be adjusted. I also had to adjust the zoom from 250% to 300% as some program’s commands were just too small and I was experiencing eyestrain after a very short time.
Bootups are lightning fast with the SSD. Transferring large files or a lot of files is a breeze. Opening a folder containing hundreds of photos for the first time, thumbnails rendered almost instantly and they maximized to full size with no waiting even with bigger files. It was torture going back to my older laptop after using this one. Torture! Everything is so quick.
Windows 10 wasn’t activated. I discovered this when I tried to personalize the desktop. I used the Windows activation troubleshooter which fixed it. But why wasn’t Windows activated in the first place? I’ve never had this happen before on a new computer.
Battery life is very good. As an example, at 98%, it offered over two hours of battery left when several applications were running along with Windows updates downloading in the background and over eight hours when the system was idle. Watching videos did not deplete it as readily as other laptops I’ve had. And this is with the gauge leaning more toward performance than battery life. If I wanted to extend the battery, there’s a myriad of settings I can change, but I prefer better performance.
The keyboard could be bigger with larger keys. They had the room. The track pad works flawlessly. Very responsive with built in left/right mouse buttons. I have a laptop with a track pad without those and I was lost when it came to opening right click menus or dragging files. I always have to use a mouse with it. I don’t use the touch screen much; however it also performed flawlessly when I chose to.
The sound is more than acceptable. The speakers don’t have deep bass, but then again laptops rarely do. Throw on some over the ear Bluetooth headphones and the quality is full and rich. There are all kinds of enhancements available with this audio adapter if you have time to play with the settings.
Something I noticed is the fan on this FusionTech is very quiet. In fact, you rarely hear it. Just a puff of air for a few seconds and that’s it unless the system is really being throttled and even then it only runs for a couple minutes.
Wi-fi is just as fast as promised. I’m getting hard wired speeds on this system using my 5 GHz network and this morning, actually exceeded my wired speed by a click or two.
The only real drawback I can find with this machine (besides the price tag) is the weight. This isn’t a laptop I would want to carry around every day since it is on the heavy side. I view it more as a workhorse that would stay at the house or office offering mobility within that environment, but that’s my personal opinion.
Before receiving this, I had yet to find a laptop that could take the place of my desktop. That would offer the same power, speed, reliability and upgrade-ability. I just may have found it.

title_x: FusionTech fan, but unsure about this model.
text:
I am unsure whether this should be a 3 or a 4 stars rating. When I compare this to my prior model, the ABC 15 9530 which I am replacing, this one does feel like an upgrade. But not by a lot. Yes, the processor is faster and seems to speed up almost all responses. But there are a number of issues that raise doubts.

The keyboard heats up more than the older model which makes it uncomfortable to type. While there is less noise, the fan starts abruptly and can be loud. The speakers are terrible and it is inconceivable they switched the beautiful sound of the 9530 for these stinkers. Though the word stingers may be more appropriate as the 7590 speakers sting your ears when high volume is used.

I had high hopes with the 4k screen and I am sad to report that the display of the 9530 was just as good if not better. I really cannot explain why Bloomberg TV live does not look as crisp as it looked in the older model. I was able to overcome the color over saturation other users have complained about by using FusionTechPremier and the Intel application, both of which allow for some tweaking. But then, you would expect super sharp images when watching Netflix movies or similar. But it is not happening.

Finally, changes to the keyboard (narrower), the keys (tapping depth) and the sizing of the computer are not that welcome. In fact, tapping keys felt much better in the older model which also felt a lot bigger (screen) in spite of FusionTech claiming the screen has remained the same size and only the bezels have been made smaller.

I wish they had kept most of the old 9530 and only upgraded the core hardware. The 9530 was just fine and with a faster chip and a few tweaks it would have been superb.

I will not be returning this computer after weeks of customizing it and transferring work, files and personal data. Too much of a hassle. But I somewhat regret having purchased it.

text:
When I first took my ABC15 out of the box I was quite impressed. I was a PC user but got a 2008 Macbook 13" and am now moving back to PC (for my laptop anyways). This thing looked great. I loved the silicone surface around the keyboard and the metal case. After extensive use it stayed cool and quite. On my girlfriends 2012 13" Macbook you can hear the fan whirring all the time. I can even hear it when I Skype with her. This thing came with a lot of features that other laptops offer as upgrades that would push the price well over that of the ABC15 (1080 screen, blu-ray drive, NVIDIA GeForce GT 640M, etc). All of this would make it a great laptop but....

THE WIFI DOESNT WORK!!! As stated in another review, moving more then 10 feet away from a wifi signal will diminish your network connection. I have a brand new dual band N router and this thing has such a hard time connecting to it. My 2008 Macbook can connect to the router better from the opposite end of the house then this thing can right next to it! Even with my network connection is shown to be "good" at 100mbps+ nothing happens, pages don't load, no ping response, I can't even go to my router configuration page. Drivers, replacement wifi cards, DIFFERENT wifi cards won't fix this problem. The only solution seems to be to get an external USB wifi adapter. So really, with computers today, I don't care if this laptop had a 56-core processor at 999 tera hertz and 89273423 terabyte cache and the battery lasted 5 years on one charge. If the wifi doesn't work it's useless.

Another pet peeve I have with this thing is the touchpad. When typing, the SLIGHTEST graze on the touchpad will move the courser while I'm typing and sometimes highlight a whole selection that will get replaced while I'm typing. There is preinstalled FusionTech touchpad software with settings to eliminate accidental touchpad contact while typing but it doesn't seem to work at all. I have to very consciously lift my wrists up while typing to avoid touching the touchpad. I like that the touchpad is very large but there is a huge downside to it. There is also something about it that makes an annoying clicking sound when you press on it. It's like an old ball (non-optical) mouse with buttons that click very loudly when you press on it. The ENTIRE touchpad is like an old mouse button.

Great looks, nicely lit keyboard, good price. HUGE downfalls. If you NEED a laptop right now but don't depend on wifi then this is a great computer and maybe someday in the future FusionTech will fix the wifi issue (I'm pretty sure it will require a new screen which is where the antenna is located) and improve the software for the touchpad. If you want something that works likes its supposed to now, well, there are better, cheaper options out there.

text:
I bought this Advance R2 because of the features and price. I have spent months looking for a Quad resolution touch screen laptop with SSD drive, good battery life and an I7 processor with lots of RAM. I had hoped to pay less than $1K for it. At first I saw deals on the R1 series that were close to my price point, but I would have had to go through an upgrade from Windows 8 to 10. Normally, that wouldn't have bothered me, but I had gone through a similar upgrade on my FusionTech desktop and experienced problems with both sound and video drivers. I decided to pay a little more and get the R2 which comes with Windows 10 already loaded. Unfortunately, it is Windows 10 Home, and upgrading to Pro costs about another $99. I haven't done that yet.

When I unboxed this laptop I was immediately smitten. It is really sharp, the display is small (13"), but that translates into lighter weight and longer battery life. It can clearly display really small fonts (you need good eyesight), but, I left the fonts at the default of 250%, which is easier on my eyes. Some applications don't recognize the "larger font" settings though. So, I get inconsistent results at times with older applications.

The touch screen and case do show fingerprints. It would have been nice if it had an oleinophobic coating like the iPhone. I haven't figured out how to safely clean the screen yet.

The Intel Video driver has crashed and restarted a couple of times since I got this. Not sure what's going on with that. The sound seems to work great. When I plug in my Sony headphones it correctly recognizes the microphone button.

I know that the Advance name and themes are purely marketing, but I have to say that this machine performs impressively at a reasonable price compared to a MS surface product with similar features.

Oh, and by the way, another reviewer clued me in that ordering a single SSD is probably a better idea than the SSD+1TB HDD. Apparently the SSD and HHD come raided together making reconfiguration and OS upgrades difficult.

text:
Update: 14 Nov 2016

Sometimes dreams DON'T come true... This is one of them.

Since the laptop arrived I have had chronic problems, most related to kernel errors and updates from the manufacturer (FusionTech) that break things. As I write this, my laptop is completely dead. This past weekend I tried restoring the system to its original factory settings, wiping out gigabytes of software in the process, as a final attempt to set things right. It worked for a while. Then I tried applying updates from FusionTech.

The laptop is now unable to even boot. Not in safe mode. Not via command prompt. Nothing.

I hereby acknowledge defeat. I'm sending it back.

:'(

-----
For years I have drooled over Advance computers, dreaming of having a system that blew through applications like they were nothing, of having a system where games would be responsive and have incredible graphics... sigh.

FWIW I do like this system. The issues I have with it probably have more to do with getting used to Windows 10 than anything else, although the intensely high-res screen poses issues I never would have expected.

Good points:
* The system IS wicked fast! I have never had a computer that booted and shut down so quickly.
* The graphics ARE amazing! One of my recent acquisitions is the game Obduction, the latest creation from the guys who made Myst and Riven. So beautiful! Yum!
* Game play has been great for every game I've played. The response time is wonderful. Although I did have to change my virus-protection software. (I never realized Zone Alarm was such a system resource hog until I had a system with resources TO hog!)
* Playing with the Advance customizable color schemes was unexpected, but very cool!
* When running on battery, the flashing power button is a welcome warning before the system shuts down!

Not so good points:
* Windows 10 sux! I've been using Windows for more years than I like to admit to, and Microsoft has outdone themselves when it comes to hiding settings and features.
* I want to kill Cortana. Seriously! The wench needs to leave me the heck alone!
* The native screen resolution is 3000x1800, which is great, but makes reading text a bit of a challenge for those of us with "tired" eyes.
* Trying to figure out what settings to fiddle with to compensate for the extreme high-res screen has given me several dozen additional grey hairs. And even when I did finally figure it out, the fix is not universal. The overlay within Steam is still really, really tiny.
* Some things render VERY crisply - I mean sharp. Other things, like web browsers, render fuzzily. I can web surf and use non-gaming applications, but half of the apps and icons look blurry, like a Hollywood glamour shot. Very annoying.
* The surface of the laptop around the keyboard looks and feels kind of like rubber, and it picks up the oils from your hands like crazy!
* And did I mention that Windows 10 sux?
* And don't get me started on Apple! Could they POSSIBLY make it MORE difficult to transfer the sync settings for my iDevices to a new system??? Arrrrggghhhh!!!

So, the upshot to this fairly jumbled mess is that I do like the system. If all you plan to do with it is play games, it's great. I feel like I have only scratched the surface and I'm looking forward to getting into more digital trouble. If, on the other hand, you are looking for a system with a little more versatility, I don't know that this is the best way to go. I'll let you know after I start loading Adobe software onto it.

The laptop comes in great, super cushioned Advance packaging. The screen is a nice size, very viewable and a good size for gaming once I tried it out (had my doubts before I got the laptop that 13" was big enough for gaming...). When I started using the laptop, I was pleased with it almost immediately - nobody has ever mentioned that the keyboard font style is different...it's cool looking, and seem to read a bit larger than normal. Very, very handy when using in the dark. Another cool aspect is the led lighting...you can use any color for the keyboard and highlight spots (back of monitor, alien head...etc). The laptop is quiet and doesn't get super hot...a welcomed feature as you could fry an egg on my OLD laptop! The speakers sound OK, got a bit crackly when raised to high, this is best used with external speakers to really take advantage of the SoundBlaster sound system. title_x: Powerful little laptop....has worked perfectly for me.
text:
I was a little worried about the performance of this laptop after reading some of the other reviews. Fortunately, my experience has been nothing but positive.

I have owned an Advance 13-inch laptop before....purchased it about six years ago, so I am familiar with the brand. The specifications on this new one (as you would expect) blow the old one out of the water. The accelerated graphics and the amount of RAM make it a stellar performer. We (I say "we" because my 13-year-old is on it more than I am) have run several games on it and they have loaded and played flawlessly. Due to it having an SSD as opposed to a HDD, it fires up in seconds. For some reason re-starting it takes a little longer, but the initial start-up is always very fast.

Two things I did after first turning it on: 1) I allowed all the Windows updates to take place. This took quite a while, and at one time I even thought it had locked up. But, be patient and let the updates run their course.....and 2) I got rid of the trial versions of Norton and MS Office (loaded Maleware Bytes and MS Home Office). The regular security protection reverted to Windows Defender.

What I don't like? Um, very little.... the only thing that I am not too crazy about Windows 10. I am a Windows 7 guy and find 10 to be cumbersome and difficult....it is frustrating to use it when I am so used to knowing my way around Windows 7. However, I accept that times and technology change and over time I am sure I will get used to it.

The quality of the screen image is amazing....really amazing. I thought the 13-inch size would be hard to get used to again, but it hasn't been. For a small laptop, it is not what you would call thin and light as compared to some other laptops out there, but the power it has is apparent when you use it. It is, however, thinner and lighter to the one I had six years ago.

In summary, my experience with this machine has been excellent and I highly recommend it. If things change as we continue to use it I will update the review. I hope it helped, if you have any questions I will do my best to answer them....thanks for reading!

text:
So far so good.

With the number of less than stellar reviews on the product here, I was concerned about making an order, but I did, and it so far seems well worth it. I have an Advance 17, and this Advance 13 lives up to the gorgeous design and impressive build quality that is standard across Advance products. One reviewer here mentioned trackpad issues, at first I noticed some trackpad trouble as well - but quickly realized the problem wasn't the laptop, it was Windows 10. There are some settings you will want to change if you find the trackpad getting stuck or not responding.

The laptop is totally quiet, it doesn't make any sound whatsoever under normal use. When playing a game, for instance CS:GO, it does make a faint (and I mean very faint) buzzing sound which I suppose are the fans running - but that's about it. I would *not* use this laptop for any seriously hardcore gaming. I got the QHD+ Touchscreen monitor, it's very glossy and reflective, not very good for gaming compared to my Advance 17's matte and much brighter monitor. It also feels generally less suited to gaming, the Core i7 is mostly an i7 in name only, and the graphics card isn't terribly impressive.

The speakers do not compare whatsoever to those on the Advance 17. Whereas the latter has some that will make a song sound like a live concert, the 13's are awful when the volume is maxed out - but the plus side is they can get very loud, so you wouldn't be setting the volume at 100 anyway. Around 75% volume and lower, they're decent.

I have no trouble connecting extra monitors with HDMI either. I plugged my TV to it and it was recognized immediately and started broadcasting the display instantly without me having to change any settings.

All things considered, there is no better laptop in this price range and size that can do as much as this one can.

Update: I've been using it for over a month now, playing all sorts of games, using Photoshop, on power and battery, no problems at all. This has been a pleasant experience. The laptop is very lovely to use when resting in bed and doing some casual work.
-----------

I've been using this for months now in very tough conditions, 80°F+ closet with laptop on for 12+ hours at a time playing games, videos, internet, all sorts of stuff, and it holds up without a single issue. Sometimes, I even leave it in sleep mode for around two weeks and come back to it, and it goes right back to the action instantly no problem.

I'm pretty confident if you get a good unit, and know how to handle Windows 10, you will have no problem.

title_x: Great Computer, Bad Support, Technical Issues
text:
I love every aspect of this Laptop with the exception of a few major details.

The HD display is totally awesome.

The fast SSD drive makes this thing a bigger speed daemon than it already is.

Some points to consider when trying to make a purchasing decision:

FusionTech says the HDMI is 2.0, but I've read reviews saying it is 1.4. If this is important to you, be sure to look into this. If it is 2.0, make sure your monitor supports HDMI 2.0 or you will only be able to get 30 FPS on a 4K HD monitor.

The USB ports are only USB 3.1, Gen 1 (USB 3.0). That means 5 Gpps, not 10 Gpps. You would think that a computer with Thunderbolt 3 would at least utilize USB 3.1 Gen 2 on the USB ports (you can get this from the Thunderbolt port by using a USB cable where one end of the cable is a USB-C connector). But, if you are using your Thunderbolt port to hook up a DisplayPort Monitor, then you won't be able to use it for high speed USB.

All in all, it is a great computer. But, alas, I had to return mine.

The Thunderbolt port is basically a USB-C port for use with USB-C devices (USB 3.1 Gen 2, and DisplayPort.). I purchased the FusionTech TB15 Thunderbolt 3 dock and the AKiTiO Thunder3 Duo Pro RAID enclosure. This computer does not work with either of these devices. Or, at least, the computer I received does not. Neither of these devices would connect.

I called FusionTech and after 2 hours of talking and holding, I was ultimately told that the TB15 dock is not compatible with the Advance. But, that doesn't explain why the AKiTiO RAID enclosure doesn't work either. I asked if I could send the computer in to have them check the Thunderbolt port and the Tech refused and wouldn't let me do it. I asked him if he is telling me that this computer is not compatible with any Thunderbolt 3 devices and he basically said "Yes".

So back it goes because my main reason for purchasing was the Thunderbolt 3 port and the assortment of Thunderbolt 3 devices that are coming onto the market now. I still believe the Port is defective but they won't look at it.

Now, here is the big kicker.

1. FusionTech considers your purchase date to be the date they sold the computer to Amazon (or the Amazon reseller). They start your warranty from this date.

2. FusionTech told me that I'm not entitled to service because I'm not the original owner. The Tech told me I would have to initiate a transfer from Amazon (or the reseller) to me and that would take awhile.

So, basically, Amazon is the owner of this computer and not you. Not sure how legal this is.

Just some thoughts for those of you comparing this to other computers in order to make a purchasing decision.

Of course, Amazon backs what it sells and if a product is defective, they take it back. This is the reason I purchased from Amazon. Their customer service cannot be beat.

Kenny

text: If you're considering purchasing this laptop, the first thing you should do is heed the warnings of other reviewers.  I wish I had.  I purchased this laptop in spite of my doubts and concerns about FusionTech products, thinking that if it were as bad as everyone was saying, how could Advance sell as many as they apparently do?  Answer:  I don't know.  I don't know how any company can get-away-with selling a product that is basically defective as soon as you take it out of the box and plug it in.  To be fair, it seemed that most of this laptop's issues were related to Windows 10 but, the massive amount of FusionTech driver updates it immediately needed (BIOS, Video, Touchpad, Wifi) was appalling.  I literally spent two hours on the phone with Fernando from Advance support last night (who was great, BTW) attempting to update and repair all the issues and another three hours doing Windows updates.  I finally gave up when the laptop continued to automatically restart applications as soon as I closed them, the touchpad freezing until I pressed the F12 key (WTH?) and Windows informing me that I had entered the 'Incorrect Password' on every re-start before I even had the opportunity to enter my Windows password.  These products are seriously flawed and should be avoided by anyone seeking a replacement for an older gaming laptop.  By comparison, my ASUS ROG G750JX hasn't given me a minute's worth of problems since I purchased it new in 2013.  I guess I will be keeping it for awhile longer!
