title_x: Excellent general purpose laptop with a great screen (Worktop 15 5501)
text:
This is a review of the FusionTech Worktop 15 5501 15.6 inch FHD Laptop (Silver) Intel Core i7-1065G7 10th Gen, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, Nvidia Geforce MX330 2GB GDDR5, Windows 10 Home (i7501-7623SLV-PUS).

Let's start with the basics:

If you look at the picture with the System Info, you will see that I was delivered a laptop with an Intel i7-1065G7 CPU. The sales page states that this model should be equipped with an Intel 10750H, a new chip with different characteristics. The bottom line is that the old chip does use less power due to it's using 4 Cores, 8 Threads @1.30 GHz, at 15 W. The newer chip uses more power and thus drains the battery more quickly, but it is much faster using 6 Cores, 12 Threads @2.60 GHz, at 45 W.

Notice also on the picture that shows the Display Info for this machine, this unit came equipped with an NVIDIA GeForce MX330, while the sales page says Nvidia Geforce GTX 1650 4GB GDDR6. In this case, the MX330 is a newer, better chip than the GTX so, I was downgraded on the CPU and upgraded on the GPU (Graphics chip)

I think it evens out in that the faster display and more display memory probably offsets some of the lower computing power. I don't know for sure, I just know it's a different setup than I thought I was getting.

I posted the results of the third-party testing that I did in the photos. As you can see the CPU (remember, this is not what was advertised, it is a slower version) came with an average rating of 55th percentile, nothing to write home about but then again, good for general use with no issues whatever. Notice that the GPU rates in the 90th percentile. This is the chip that was newer and better than advertised. Overall, compared to a "budget laptop" this 3rd party test showed this running about 143% better than a typical budget computer. Specifically, the CPU was 133% higher and the GPU was 247% higher. Again, this correlates to the slower CPU installed and the faster Graphics chip installed. Now, I wouldn't call this a "budget" computer and maybe the comparison was unfair. The other option for comparison was "gaming computer" and that would have made this look bad but would have been a very poor comparison. In general, I would expect that with this configuration, the computing speed and abilities of this unit is very much on par with others in its price range. After all, while this is not necessarily a "budget" computer, it's not a gaming computer or a $2500 laptop either.

So, with the changes in power consumption how is the battery life of this laptop? I ran several tests, mostly just streaming video to see how long the battery would last. In each case, the battery was fully charged for several hours, left for at least 30 minutes to cool down, and then I would stream a few movies or live TV. On several tests, the battery lasted almost exactly 5 hours. In a few tests, the battery lasted six by using the battery saver function. I will say that I did not notice any difference in the quality of the video stream when I went to power-saving mode. With that in mind, I suggest that you stream using the saver mode, you'll get an extra hour and not feel the change.

The battery took 2.5 hours to recharge from fully empty to 100%; this time was pretty consistent from charge to charge. In 1 hour it would charge to 50%.

When using this in normal "office mode", i.e., opening and closing spreadsheets and documents, the occasional trip to the internet to look at cat photos, and letting it go idle as I ate my lunch, chit-chatted with fellow employees or rummaged through the supply closet, I got a full days' work in with some battery to spare.

The screen is great; bright and sharp and is a pleasure to look at. The streaming videos looked as good as one could expect on a laptop and I enjoyed the viewing experience. With its almost edge to edge design, it is large enough to view movies and not feel as if you're losing out on a big screen. It is also light enough and slim enough to keep on your lap and view without it feeling clunky or weighing down on you. I'll also add that it did not run hot, a problem I've had with other laptops when placed on my lap. It runs quietly, you can watch videos without annoying fan noises.

So far, mostly all good. What do I hate about this laptop? It's probably me but I find the distance from the laptops leading (front) edge to the keyboard just a bit too much of a stretch for me. If you will notice in the picture attached, I need to take my watch off of my left hand when I type; as you can see it is constantly getting caught on the edge of the laptop. Further, I just found the keyboard uncomfortable. Perhaps it's just different from my last keyboard but I find myself hitting the backslash key instead of the enter key and I can't seem to get comfortable with it. I switch keyboards often with no problem but perhaps this being so far back from the edge is throwing me off quite a bit.

Overall, I like the form factor, except for the keyboard placement. The battery life is not great, but it's acceptable especially since when using it for work I will usually have it plugged in. Seeing as I don't often watch videos for more than 6 hours at a time the battery life is not an issue on that end either and actually, that long will get me cross country (on a plane of course) with no issues.

Overall, this is just fine. More stars for its looks than its power, some points deducted for average battery life, and some deducted because FusionTech didn't have the decency to request my hand size or to ask me which wrist I wear my watch on before they finalized the design of the machine. Add some points back for a great display.

text:
Just to be clear, as they have merged the reviews of several FusionTech laptop models; I am reviewing a FusionTech Worktop 15 7501 laptop which was first released in July 2020. It does not have an optical drive and is extremely light and thin for a laptop of this size.

I decided to review this from the standpoint of someone getting their first computer. I am somewhat suited for such a task, having not owned a PC since Windows 98. That said I was shocked by what a miserable experience it was trying to activate and operate this FusionTech Worktop 15 out of the box. Part of this is simply what happens when a Mac user encounters a PC. And part is more directed at Windows 10 than against the features of this specific PC model.

Judging from this, over the past 20+ years there has been little that I would regard as improvements made to entry level FusionTech laptops, while complexity has increased geometrically it seems to have been almost entirely in the service of showcasing silly gimmicks. It is certainly a more powerful machine than my 1998 PC, so the internet connection permits streaming and gaming applications; and apparently it can handle ZOOM but I have had it for over six weeks and am still getting nowhere trying to utilize this feature.

My 1998 PC out of the box had an optical drive and the installed software to run Excel and Word. And with a simple driver could link to and operate a printer and a scanner. Navigation could be figured out in a couple of hours.

But out of the box with this 2020 version I have been limited to accessing the internet and to sending and receiving email. That has been the sum total of its functionality. Although based on Amazon's product detail page there are all sorts of bells and whistles designed into this machine. To be fair, with my basic computer needs I suspect that even if I could figure out how to activate them they would be of little value. I really wish the designers of these basic machines would spend less time trying to dazzle buyers with things that complicate their lives and come out with something that could simply be plugged and immediately applied to a useful purpose.

Within hours of opening the box I was wishing that I had not attempted to use it as there were so many invasive questions asked during the registration and set-up that I expect to be plagued with thousands of spam emails over the next decade. I think that I switched off most of the “receive offers” options and hopefully avoided disclosing my telephone number but I regret ever opening up this can of worms. I had my first unwanted email within minutes of disclosing my address.

What you get in the box is the laptop itself and a power cord (no mouse although that is a quick enough fix). There are also two small brochures with microscopic print regarding warranty information and several tiny diagrams with minimal explanation. When you turn it on they begin extracting personal information and internet connection details. The operation of the laptop and the operating system are not intuitive so if you are not an experienced PC user make sure you have someone handy who can help you navigate the operation of this device. The screen is pretty much blank and there are few hints about where to find files or downloads. Portable hard drives and optical drives are only acknowledged, reading them requires outside apps or guidance.

It took me 40 minutes just to figure out how to use their menu to enter my date of birth, it would not allow me to just type it in the field. It took about the same amount of time for Cortina (the chatty set-up assistant) and I to give up on activating the fingerprint reader; she simply stopped prompting me and I thought it was finally activated - but the next time I tried to log-on it did not work. I was able to access the internet and I eventually I stumbled across the Microsoft Office software. But the software requires yet another registration and is only good for seven days before you have to purchase a subscription; seriously can't FusionTech just provide generic pre-installed software for something this basic?

To be fair there are online courses and books that will allow you to track up the learning curve and there is always on-line tech support if you want to devote even more hours to the task.

First impression is that this is a flimsy feeling laptop, with moderate effort you could fold the screen in half. Overall a huge disappointment for me but a seasoned Windows 10 user will not experience the same setup irritations.

text:
My old FusionTech 8600 was on it's way out so I was looking for the next machine to replace it. I keep my computer for a long time, so I wanted to get the best I could get. I also didn't plan on carrying it around, so I wanted a large screen size. This machine looked like it fit the bill. First, the machine started out really well. It is fast. The hi res panel is pretty nice. The video card is pretty good too. My initial impressions were all good.

Once I started using it I noticed a major problem with the touch pad. The touch pad placement is wrong. The touch pad is offset about a half inch to the right. that means that your right palm will hit the touch pad when you type. That will cause the cursor to jump around. It is very frustrating and one has to wonder who the genius was who though that was a good idea. The touch pad should be centered on the letter B not the letter N.

That was the first negative. Unfortunately it was not the last. This is a high end machine and I had high expectations. After 13 months the battery died. My prior FusionTech's battery lasted much longer time. It lasted more than 3 years before I had to replace it. The other annoying problem is that right around the same time the battery died, the power plug no longer would stay connected to the back of the computer. So besides the battery dieing now it is difficult to charge the battery.

Overall this is a powerful computer that let me down because of the poor design of the touchpad and the power system. They cut corners on the battery and the power plug system. When you consider the cost, that is inexcusable. In the past I would only buy FusionTech computers. Now I am rethinking that. My next computer will probably be a different brand. I've heard good things about Sony's.

6/2013 Update***

I just dropped the rating from 3 stars to 1 star. Why the change? Because I have had two more issues with the computer. Both are due to poor design. The first new issue has to do with the power supply. For some stupid reason FusionTech thought it would be a good idea to not charge the battery if the computer does not recognize the power supply that is plugged in. You can still use the computer, but the battery will not be charged. The was it identifies the powersupply is by the tiny wire that sticks out of the middle of the power supply plug. If that gets broken off or if the internal wire connection goes bad, you get no charging. Google FusionTech power supply problem and you can read all about this STUPID design. Luckily the fix is pretty easy, just get a new power supply. I found a used one on ebay at a reasonable cost. So I can once again charge my battery.

The next problem is the headphone jack went bad. You would think, hey this machine has two jacks so I can just use the second. Unfortunately this very common failure mode is not that the jack stops working when you plug in a headphone. Instead the failure is that the computer thinks you always have headphones plugged in and the built in speakers no longer produce sound. Again, this is a common failure due to bad design. This is really inexcusable for a high end machine. I'm done with buying FusionTech computers.

text:
Tengo pocos días de estar usando esta laptop para trabajo, estudios y juegos. i7 11800H, RTX 3060, 16GB RAM dual channel, 512GB almacenamiento. La recibí sellada de fabrica.
Para trabajo y estudio es mas que excelente y sobrado, si te importa el peso, esta no es para ti, yo con todo gusto cargo esta laptop valorando sus capacidades. Si quieres una laptop que te dure la batería todo el día, búscate una laptop no gamer.
Para juegos es una maquina que no esperaba que fuera tan potente, y no esperaba que viniera con una RTX 3060 de 130w, ... feliz! La calidad de pantalla y el brillo es excelente aunque sea de 250 nits, son suficientes para que te duelan los ojos de la intensidad del brillo. Uso el brillo en 50% y es mas intenso que una laptop de bajo precio con brillo al maximo.
Es el equipo mas económico con Hybrid/Optimus (switch MUX), y es una gran ventaja para sacar todo el potencial de la RTX 3060 (15-20 fps adicionales con Optimus en Off), esta característica era importante para mi porque puedo tener toda la potencia de la gpu en la pantalla del mismo equipo y no depender de una pantalla externa para saber su verdadera capacidad.
La batería en optimus para ofimática y vídeos dura aproximadamente 3 horas y 45 minutos.
La refrigeración me parece muy funcional y muy silenciosa, con 4 salidas (2 laterales y 2 traseras) y 2 entradas amplias (por la parte de abajo y la parte superior, entre el teclado y la pantalla), recomiendo utilizar una muy buena base de refrigeración adicional para darle vida en el tiempo y cuidar tu inversión.
La tecla G activa la máxima velocidad de los ventiladores (para nada molestos) así como el brillo pero aun no he verificado si las frecuencias de la cpu o gpu suben, pero sin activar la tecla G es lo suficientemente potente para correr tus juegos en máxima calidad sin contratiempos.
Sobre el acabado, es de plástico, pero en mi opinión personal es plástico de muy buena calidad, excelente ensamble, muy solida por todos lados, fuerte, resistente y muy buen acabado. No es una laptop con diseño excesivo gamer, pero es diferente a una laptop común, discreta pero con un toque especial, sobrio y elegante.
Viene con Windows 11 para inicializar, que me parece mucho mejor que con windows 10 actualizable y tener problemas de drivers luego.

En resumen, encontré todas las características que buscaba por el dinero que pensaba invertir, hasta el momento cero fallas, gran potencia para juegos actuales. Si falla, actualizare este comentario.

La refrigeración me parece muy funcional y muy silenciosa, con 4 salidas (2 laterales y 2 traseras) y 2 entradas amplias (por la parte de abajo y la parte superior, entre el teclado y la pantalla), recomiendo utilizar una muy buena base de refrigeración adicional para darle vida en el tiempo y cuidar tu inversión.
La tecla G activa la máxima velocidad de los ventiladores (para nada molestos) así como el brillo pero aun no he verificado si las frecuencias de la cpu o gpu suben, pero sin activar la tecla G es lo suficientemente potente para correr tus juegos en máxima calidad sin contratiempos.
Sobre el acabado, es de plástico, pero en mi opinión personal es plástico de muy buena calidad, excelente ensamble, muy solida por todos lados, fuerte, resistente y muy buen acabado. No es una laptop con diseño excesivo gamer, pero es diferente a una laptop común, discreta pero con un toque especial, sobrio y elegante.
Viene con Windows 11 para inicializar, que me parece mucho mejor que con windows 10 actualizable y tener problemas de drivers luego.

En resumen, encontré todas las características que buscaba por el dinero que pensaba invertir, hasta el momento cero fallas, gran potencia para juegos actuales. Si falla, actualizare este comentario.

title_x: For the price it's a good deal, but you could do much better...
text:
An RTX 3060 laptop for under $1400 (with $140 discount at the time of purchase) seemed like a good deal but to get to that price point a lot was sacrificed it seems.

Pros:
- Price was affordable
- Build quality is very sturdy. Very little flex in the chassis or screen.
- In-stock. Nearly everything else I wanted was out of stock or price gouged by scalpers
- No dead pixels as far as I can tell.
- Nice speakers but fans can still be heard over them.

Cons:
- TDP of 3060 is only 90 watts. Confirmed with GPU-Z.
- Gets VERY Hot. GPU easily hit 90 degrees Celsius then crashed while gaming from overheating.
- Keyboard is not great. Missed key presses constantly and using red letters on black keys is a terrible idea.
- Mux switch is in the BIOS and can not be changed in Windows
- Bloatware. 512gb SSD but only 407gb free.
- Some backlight bleed. Very noticeable on dark scenes.
- Ships with dead battery. I thought I had a DOA unit cause it would not boot up.
- Color is not black. It's a very dark dirty grey unlike the pictures.

Overall its a nice laptop but I was mislead by reviews online and and the Q&A section that this was the high wattage 3060. Due to the thermal issue I'm guessing that's why they opted for the lower watt version. The cooling could be better IMHO as evidenced by the crashes I experience from overheating. If you can get it on a sale and not MSRP its a better deal than most 3050 ti laptops. It's good enough for basic gaming but don't expect to run modern games on it at high framerates/quality. Despite having a Core i7 CPU I'm constantly experiencing system stuttering which could be a windows issue or caused by all the bloatware. FusionTech did not include any backup disks or a restore option so I can not uninstall anything without losing it forever. I will update my review after the return period is over to see if it holds up.

text: I am not a professional gamer but I needed a laptop for work since I travel and wanted to have the ability to still play some games here and there. So far it has done everything I need it to. Windows 11 installed with no issues either and I am planning on upgrading the ram and adding more storage in the future. Like any new electronic just plug it into its charger and let the battery charge for a good 30 min before starting to get into the updating! Another note to consider is this laptop automatically turns on when you open the lid from a full shut down. Not a let down but it may be for others.

title_x: Incredibly awesome audio, but suffers from Nvidia issues yet again.
text:
My specs: FusionTech ABC l502x (Purchased May 2011)
Processor: i5 2410M
RAM: 6GB
HDD: 640 gb 7200 hard drive
Resolution: 1366 x 768
Video card: GeForce 540M 2GB

First off: the audio on this model is truly incredible for the price range. The JBL speakers with subwoofer make it unnecessary to have to plug your laptop in to external speakers for almost any situation (except of course... parties and what have you). In fact, you'd truly be hard pressed to find better audio quality in a laptop even now. The new Lenovo y410 and y510 models do come with JBL speakers, however they are not of the same quality.

The keyboard is comfortable for my usage, since I have fairly large hands. I have heard that some people complain about the spacing between keys, but honestly... unless you have tiny fingers I don't really understand how it's an issue.

The screen quality is pretty good for the price and resolution.

Now for the bad.. well, horrible.

The battery quality is horribly sub par; the 9cell battery I purchased with the unit barely kept about one hour charge after a year and at current lasts about 35-40 minutes with wireless enabled. Considering that the laptop is plugged in almost 85% of the time, this is fairly terrible.

And most importantly (or annoyingly), the video card. The Nvidia GeForce 540M comes with either 1GB or 2GB of dedicated video memory. I opted for the 2GB over the 1GB merely because it was only about a $20 upgrade at the time of purchase. The card has pretty solid reviews on notebookcheck in terms of performance and can play modern games at decent quality. However (and this is a HUGE however), the thing crashes. It crashes a whole ton. Like a ridiculously ludicrous amount. And by crash, I do mean that the entire computer freezes along with a looping stuttering audio sound (which is incredibly loud and annoying) and must be powered down via the button.

There are several theories as to why the video card crashes (be it overheating, which obviously can occur in laptops, or more commonly, with this video card, that there is an issue with the clock speed). While it is possible to lower the amount of crashes by a great deal by switching to the integrated graphics card, I eventually found that this card would freeze during certain games, such as Starcraft 2. You can also go the "underclock the core speed of your 540M main card" which will also lower the frequency of crashes, but they still do inevitably occur under medium to heavy load. This could be an issue with the motherboard, 540M speed, etc. and that would be fine if FusionTech acknowledged the issue and voluntarily replaced or provided solutions to fix the crashing errors. But they haven't. In fact, they have gone a highly petty route by forcing users to extend warranties and continually replace the motherboard and video card. Oh, I said petty because on their forums, they also mute people and delete comments on their forums who even whisper anything overly negative about the computer or FusionTech's possible knowledge that they shipped out faulty components with the laptops and did not voluntarily pull the laptops back to replace said faulty components (if you read FusionTech community forum posts in regards to how frequently and readily FusionTech replaced motherboards for this laptop, it becomes fairly obvious they know of the issue).

Yes, it would cost them money to replace everyone's faulty components. But this is a premium laptop and by my standards, shipping out a laptop with faulty components is essentially shipping out an incomplete product, which FusionTech should be held liable for.

I am honestly stuck at a crossroads for rating this laptop. On the one hand, everything but the video card and battery runs perfectly and as it should, and the audio quality is superb. But FusionTech's horrible business practices in regards to informing their customers of faulty hardware (this also happened with the ABC M1530 line, see Nvidia 8 series class action lawsuit) leads me to have to ultimately give this laptop a 2/5.

I bought mine direct from FusionTech (preferred customer) to replace my tired
Studio 1550.
i7, 2.2ghz, 1tb drive, 8 gig ram, GT525 & intel HD graphics, JBL sound,
bluetooth etc.

1st thing I do is set it up, and then pull the HDD out, pop in a clean one,
and set it up my way, and leave the "factory" drive on the shelf with the
expiration date of the warranty. If I have a warranty claim, pop in THEIR
drive with no personal data on it and send it back.
I didn't get the back-lit keyboard.
This thing screams on photoshop, which I use daily. Keyboard is responsive,
and easier than several of my older laptops. Keys are solid, not spongy.
The dual video is nice on the battery also. I went with the bigger battery
& charger. The bigger battery has the advantage of tilting the entire laptop
up. The sound on this thing is something to make you wonder how they get that
sort of sound out of a laptop. The JBL logo on the bottom, I guess the entire
cavity of the laptop is a tuned port. When it is sitting on a table, you can
really hear the bass pumping through. The case speakers on the top side are
clear & pretty loud. 3 USB ports. One on the left, one in back, and a combo
e-sata/usb on the right. USB 3 is plenty fast for my needs. I use a BT
mouse, and it works without any issue.
Battery life for my use is excellent. I can have it charged, unplug it after
work at 5pm, put it in sleep mode, and leave it that way til the next day, and
it might use 1-3% of the battery, making startup faster.
Wireless works perfectly, no issues.

text:
The laptop worked great until I called FusionTech, they dialed in and performed a diagnostics on the system. There was a memory card error. Sent the laptop to FusionTech. Then it was a motherboard issue. Escalated and found out the errors were because the seller installed unsupported third-party components and components that were beyond the motherboard's ability to support.

The seller used third-party parts for the memory cards (16G each) and replaced the 128G SSD with a 512G SSD. FusionTech's motherboard for this laptop only supports 8G memory cards and 128G SSD. In addition, the board does not support third-party components and will generate error codes.

FusionTech explained these issues void the warranty. Contacted the seller and sent me a legal quote from Mag-Moss Warranty Act stating why FusionTech can't refuse my warranty. The issue is the seller modified the laptop beyond its supportability. FusionTech offers a laptop with this config that is supported but the seller opted to modify a lower-end laptop and sell it as a higher-end laptop.

The point is the seller is deceptive in the product presentation and the issues can cause malfunctions with the laptop that FusionTech will not cover or fix. I wouldn't have found this out if I had not happened to run a health diagnostic from FusionTech on the laptop.

title_x: Nice Laptop, but missing key features
text:
Bought this laptop directly from FusionTech. It has great specs for the price. However, after setting up the laptop, I ran into a couple key features that make this a deal-breaker and I plan to return the box. First the camera on this laptop is not compatible with the Windows 10 Hello facial recognition feature, so make sure you get the finger print reader, if you want to do use bio-metrics login features. Second, and most important, this box does not support "Wake Timers". This is an important feature if you want to be able to run scheduled tasks during the off hours while the PC is in "sleep" mode. For example, if you want to run backup jobs during the night while you are not using the PC. Any schedule task will not be able to "wake" the PC, so all of these tasks must be performed while the PC is awake. This is unbelievable for a 'business class' machine. Also, the BIOS does not support "Wake on LAN" function either, which means you can not use remote desktop to access a sleeping PC. I tested these features extensively and was not able to get them to work. I also contacted FusionTech Support and worked with their 2nd level support team to find a solution. But none was found.

I wanted to really like this machine, but these missing features have spoiled the fun.

title_x: Great laptop with a few annoyances. If you need desktop workstation power in a portable package, this is it.
text:
Not sure why this unit is getting so many negative reviews. The system isn't perfect, but there are compromises that have to be made when you have a bezel this small on a laptop display (odd webcam placement, ease of opening/one handed operation, etc). Out of the box, the first thing should be updating the BIOS to the most recent version, then downloading all of the current drivers from the FusionTech support site.

The ABC15 is plenty powerful, and doesn't throttle the CPU under moderate to heavy workloads. Yes, the fan is audible during compute intensive periods, but I'd rather have a few dB of extra fan noise than a machine that throttles performance almost to a crawl. Equipped with the 45W i7-7700HQ, 32Gbs and the 1Tb NVme disk, it handles everything I've thrown at it quickly, and effortlessly. Full disclosure, I'm not a gamer, so cannot comment on gaming performance.

It's not perfect, however. The 4K/UHD display is very glossy and reflective. While it's stunning to look at in ideal conditions, the glare from any light source makes it almost unusable in bright environments. In the dark, it acts like a mirror, so you spend most of your working time looking at yourself. The 4K resolution is, IMO, overkill for a screen this size also. While it's great for image editing to evaluate critical sharpness, many apps don't scale properly yet, and are almost unusable at 100% scaling. Colour accuracy once calibrated is quite good. The ideal display for me would be something in between the FHD matte display, and this 4K glossy touch unit. I'd love a 2560x1600 matte, non-touch panel. It would increase usability substantially, and add an extra couple of hours to the battery life. (which is just OK with the 4K screen, at about 3.5-4.5 hours, depending on usage).

I have ordered a matte/anti-glare film to apply to the display, and will update once installed and in use.

The SD card sticks out a few mm more than it needs to, and can get caught up when placing into, or removing from a laptop bag. Plenty of expansion slots though- USB-C, 2x USB3, audio out, and the SD card. The keyboard is decent, though doesn't have as much travel as the ThinkPad or HP units.

The keyboard deck/wrist rest is a fingerprint and oil magnet. The fingerprint scanner is very fast, and very accurate. A quick swipe and you're set within a couple of seconds.

All of the units reviewed by major tech publications had the Samsung NVme disks. The bulk of the units however, are shipping with slower NVme drives from Hynix and Toshiba. While it's not likely to impact the majority of users, publishing disk read rates of up to 3,200Mbps then shipping the units with read rates of approx 1,700Mbps is a bit disappointing.

Overall a very powerful unit, relatively light and compact, and with a few minor issues.

Edited to include update: I picked up an anti-glare filter to reduce the reflections on the screen, and following all the instructions, taking my time (even did it with the shower running, to reduce floating dust particles in the air), I couldn't get it applied evenly, without trapping air bubbles or dust underneath. Gave up and threw it out.

title_x: SSD 512 GB discription is not correct, OS on 2 TB slow drive, performance is not good.
text:
In product description, key features for this laptop, it is mentioned that High quality Intel PCIe Nvme 512GB SSD + 2000 GB Hard drive. But when I received this laptop, the 512GB was SATAIII SSD not PCIe Nvme SSD. So, description was not correct. Although, after I checked the BIOS Settings at boot time, it is mentioned that THERE IS a slot for PCIe MVME M.2 but it's empty meaning it's not populated with any drive. Also, for some unknown reason, Windows 10 OS was installed by FusionTech on the 2 TB very slow drive and the whole performance is really bad. I also noticed that 512 GB has an OS on it but FusionTech made 2 TB drive the primary one to boot from. Really bad choice. I would accept immediately if it had 1 TB PCIe MVME M.2 drive with more $150 instead of those both 2 poor drives since in my experience, if you want a blazing speed laptop, just order it with the fastest hard drive you can get, it doesn't matter other specs as much as drive. I would pay the difference between both, and I calculated it, it's about $100 to $150 diff. Both those poor hard drives can cost about $150, and 1TB MVME cost about $200 to $250, but the difference in performance is unmatchable. MVME Read speed can range between 1500MBytes/s to 3000 MBytes/s, while fastest SATA3 speed can get up to 540 MBytes/s and mechanical drives even much worse with up to 150 MBytes/s max, which makes the diff 6x - 9x, that's huge comparing to only $150 max diff.
Finally, the Turn On switch is at the bottom/right corner of the laptop and it's barely noticeable so it's not easy to turn it on, but I guess it'll become okay when you can adjust yourself to it.
Weight is okay regarding its screen 17.3 inches I guess. CPU fan noise is almost not noticeable and quite. No overheating issues at all. I never felt any heat at all. I tested battery for the first 30 minutes, battery lost 7% which makes it last for up to 6 hour with normal use, meaning no Youtub or videos or heavy graphics or v. games.
About 6 hours of battery for this huge laptop, that's very good job FusionTech.
======
Edit on 1/30/2019
So, after I wrote my previous review with 2 stars, I sent the seller HotDeal Express and he was amazingly responsive and positive. He immediately apologized because he was not aware with this issue and offered a free return label and replace SATA3 SSD drive with PCIe Nvme SSD and install Win 10 home x64 on the fast one with no extra charge. I would definitely buy from him again if I needed any product that he is selling. Also, now I see they changed the description to match the real drives and I think they sell it now with PCIe Nvme 512GB SSD + 2000 GB Hard drive.
Also they raised the price a little bit about $50, which I think they should do.
I'm changing my stars to 4 instead of 2 because of that.

text:
I cannot recommend this product, or FusionTech products in general.
The G7 7790 overheats terrible out of the box. updates do not fix it.
FusionTech has the CPU set to overclock by default which just causes it to shut itself off under load.
I was able to make the device usable, so if people purchased it already and need some help, here are some things you can do if you are reasonably savvy.
First, lower the voltage going to the CPU a bit. Undervolting and underclocking helped the heat issue.
Second, reapply the thermal paste for the CPU and GPU. I disassembled it and found that they used really bad thermal paste and it wasn't applied very well. So take it apart, clean it off with some alcohol wipes, and use Arctic or Cooler Master or something better.
After adjusting clocks and redoing the thermal compound, my GPU and CPU run about 70ish degrees under load. I've noticed the fans are a lot quieter and it cools down way faster after gaming.

One thing I did like about mine, is they included the ribbon cable to connect an SSD.
I purchased mine with the smaller 512gb m.2, and took it apart to upgrade it, and saw that the ribbon cable was included for a second storage device which was a nice surprise.

text:
I have now had this laptop about 2 weeks. Since I use it mostly for work, I have been on it 8-10 hours a day since I received it.

These are my impressions so far:

1) Overall, it's an excellent laptop. I bought a machine with SSD, quad core, NVIDIA and 16GB of RAM because I need a fast machine for work (it's advertised for gaming but I do no gaming at all). It's speed has not disappointed me. Slow hard disks are the pits, but this machine gets up and running within 10 seconds (with most of that time taken up with my typing credentials, etc.). Everything being on SSD is very nice and since I save all my files to the cloud, I don't need a hard disk beyond Windows, Office and a few other things.
2) I've always liked the FusionTech keyboard, and after being on a terrible ASUS keyboard for 5 years, I'm very glad to be back on a FusionTech.
3) Screen is plenty sharp and have no problems with that. I hook up the laptop to a large monitor via HDMI and have no issues.
4) General navigation is fast and, again, no issues. The only slowness comes sometimes from Office and/or Windows, but that's not an issue with the laptop per se.
5) I've used FusionTech SupportAssist a few times and found it helpful.

So far, I've only had two issues to deal with:
1) Sound quality is inconsistent. I don't need the sound system all that much in my work, so it's a minor inconvenience for me, but if you're into gaming and depend on it more, it could become a major inconvenience.
2) The mousepad (or something else) has completely frozen the machine 2-3 times so far. I'm still in the process of looking up this issue, and don't know if it's due to Windows or FusionTech. I've powered down the system and powered back up and have no problems afterward, but I'd like to try to resolve it. One recommendation from another source was to get a USB mouse, though I don't know if that will resolve it or not.

Overall, it's a good system, and if you have a heavy workload and need to be on your system hours at a time, then I would recommend it.

Basically the internal specs on this thing are really good and will defiantly meet the needs of practically anyone; gamers, digital designers, students, anybody. This laptop is also really nice in its design and does some very smart things that a lot of other laptops don't seem to offer. The chaise is almost entirely made out of aluminum and it feels pretty think; so far i haven't encountered any areas where the metal flexes or makes creaking noises. One of the biggest problems facing the functionality of laptops is the cooling system. On laptops that are not properly ventilated the processor will over heat under enough stress and the laptop will crash (this was the main problem with the dv4). I think the best example of proper laptop cooling can be found in the Asus G73 but the ABC 15 comes in pretty close. On the left hand side of the laptop there is a large heat sink and vent that does a very good job at regulating the temp. To speak to this, while playing Fallout 3 on ultra setting the air coming out of the vent is pretty warm and would feel uncomfortable keeping your hand in front of it but the palm rests and keyboard remain cool to the touch. This thing is built like a tank (personally i hate throwing down a bunch of cash for a laptop only to find its construction feels cheap, this however feels very nicely put together). The track pad is also nice and large and has a slight matte finish that helps your fingers glide across it a bit better. The other two things that really surprised me about this machine were one, the webcam which at 2.0 MP doesn't seem like a lot but actually provides a very nice image, and the speakers. Since getting this laptop i have done away with my desktop speakers because the JBL speakers and subwoffer (yeah its got a subwoffer) sound amazing. This laptop really is amazing and i think it should defiantly be considered by anyone looking to get a new computer.

p.s. I custom built mine on FusionTech's website only because i wanted to add a backlit keyboard (only $20 extra) but the rest of my components were the standard ones you get when you buy it out right.

Cons

4. Weak Wifi (Needs an update badly, I really hope it happens soon. It is pretty bad)

This is an excellent laptop but should probably be priced $100 less. I would recommend this laptop to anyone. It just feels really good and it is relatively lightweight. If offers many features and still remains much cheaper than an equivalent Macbook Pro laptop. I still think this laptop is a good buy and would give it a 90/100. It is a bit better than 4/5 but not quite 5 stars. You immediately notice the design and quality of materials is top of the line. As I stated earlier, this laptop does not have RGBLED display, nor does it have the JBL sound system. However, it is very interesting because the image quality is simply incredible when looking at photos and watching videos. Sound quality is also very very good and it is much louder than the previous FusionTech ABC 15.

For the price, they should have put a better graphics card and larger power brick to have better gaming performance. FusionTech offers better but heavier gaming laptops with their Advance laptops.
